note: Shared glossary for every part of Ovid's Metamorphoses. Entries keyed by word form as printed in Magnus (Gotha: F.A. Perthes), lowercased. Lemma — meaning (grammatical info); the lemma may carry macrons for vowel length, the text never does.

glossary.a: ā — from, by (= ab); a morte: by death
glossary.ab: ab — from, out of; by (agent, + abl.): sorbentur ab ipsa, are swallowed by the earth herself
glossary.aberant: absum — were absent, were far off (3 pl. imperf.)
glossary.abeunt: abeō — go away, turn into (3 pl. pres.; with 'in' + acc., 'change into')
glossary.abiit: abeō — went off into, passed into (3 sg. perf.; in flammas abiit, 'went up in flames')
glossary.ablato: auferō — swept away, carried off (perf. part., m. dat. sg., with 'cervo')
glossary.abscidit: abscīdō — cut off, severed (3 sg. perf.; not abscindō 'tear away')
glossary.abstrahit: abstrahō — drags off, carries away (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.absumitur: absūmō — is used up, wastes away (3 sg. pres. pass. ind.)
glossary.absumptis: absūmō — used up, spent (perf. part., f. abl. pl., abl. absolute with 'viribus')
glossary.ac: ac — and, and also (conj.; = atque, used before consonants)
glossary.accedere: accēdō — to come near, approach (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.accinctus: accingō — girded, equipped (perf. part., m. nom.); quo accinctus erat: with which he was girt
glossary.acclivi: acclīvis — sloping upward, uphill (m. abl. sg., with limite)
glossary.acervo: acervus — heap, mass (m. abl. sg., of separation with 'exemit')
glossary.acres: ācer — fierce, hot, keen (m. nom. pl., with animi 'their tempers')
glossary.acuta: acūtus — sharp, pointed (f. abl. sg., with 'cuspide')
glossary.ad: ad — to, toward; for (+ gerundive of purpose)
glossary.adde: addō — add (2 sg. pres. act. imperat.; with acc. and dat., 'add X to Y'; also 'add the fact that…', introducing quod)
glossary.addicere: addīcō — to hand over, give up, surrender (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.adductas: addūcō — led along, brought together (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., with capellas of 676)
glossary.adducto: addūcō — drawn taut, pulled back (perf. part., m. abl. sg., with 'nervo')
glossary.adeo: adeō — so much, to such a degree (adv.; not the verb adeō 'approach')
glossary.aderis: adsum — you will be present, will attend (2 sg. fut.; + dat. 'ducibus')
glossary.adesto: adsum — be present, stand by as witness (2 sg. fut. act. imperat.)
glossary.adeunt: adeō — they approach, go up to (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.adfatur: adfor — addresses, speaks to (3 sg. pres., deponent)
glossary.adfectas: adfectō (affectō) — you reach for, aim at (2 sg. pres. act. ind.; edition's conp-/adf- spelling)
glossary.adfectasse: adfectō — to have aimed at, laid claim to (syncopated perf. inf. = adfectavisse)
glossary.adfert: adferō — brings, supplies (3 sg. pres.; + dat. 'nubibus')
glossary.adfore: adsum — that there would come, be at hand (fut. inf. = adfutūrum esse, in indirect statement)
glossary.adhaesit: adhaereō — came to rest, grounded (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.adiciunt: adiciō — add, throw in (words) (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.adit: adeō — goes to, reaches (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.adiutus: adiuvō — helped, aided (perf. part., m. nom. sg.; + abl. 'pennis')
glossary.admirantibus: admīror — marvelling, wondering at (pres. part. dep., m. dat. pl., 'to those who marvel')
glossary.admisso: admittō — let loose, given full rein (perf. part., m. abl. sg., with 'passu': at full stride)
glossary.admissum: admittō — the offense committed, the crime (perf. part. as noun, n. nom. sg., in indirect question)
glossary.admoverat: admoveō — had brought near, consigned (3 sg. pluperf.; + dat. 'umbris')
glossary.admovit: admoveō — brought near (3 sg. perf.; of a traveller's torch)
glossary.adnuit: adnuō — nodded assent (3 sg. perf.; the present is spelled the same)
glossary.adolentur: adoleō — are burned up (3 pl. pres. pass.)
glossary.adopertaque: adoperiō — and having covered (perf. part., f. nom. + -que)
glossary.adorant: adōrō — they worship, pray to (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.adsensibus: adsēnsus — shouts of assent, approval (m. abl. pl.)
glossary.adsere: adserō — lay claim to (2 sg. imper.; with 'nec' = a prohibition, 'do not claim')
glossary.adsidua: adsiduus (assiduus) — unceasing, unremitting (f. abl. sg., with vertigine)
glossary.adsiduis: adsiduus — unceasing, constant (f. abl. pl., with 'nubibus')
glossary.adspergine: aspergō — by the sprinkling, spray (abl.; older spelling adsp-)
glossary.adspice: adspiciō (aspiciō) — look at, behold (2 sg. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.adspicit: adspiciō (aspiciō) — looks upon, beholds (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.adspirate: adspīrō — breathe upon, favor (2 pl. imperative; + dat. 'coeptis')
glossary.adstricta: adstringō — bound tight, frozen fast (perf. part., f. nom. sg., with 'glacies')
glossary.adunca: aduncus — curved, hooked (f. abl. sg., with 'cumba')
glossary.adversas: adversus — facing, in their path (f. acc. pl., with 'vestes')
glossary.adversi: adversus — facing, turned to meet you (m. gen. sg., with tauri)
glossary.adversum: adversus — the opposing direction (n. acc. sg. as noun: in adversum 'against the current, uphill')
glossary.aeas: Aeās — the Aeas, a river of Epirus/Thessaly and its river-god (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.aegaeona: Aegaeōn — Aegaeon (Briareus), the hundred-armed sea-giant (m. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.aemula: aemulus — rival of, emulating (f. nom. sg.; + gen. 'Phoebes')
glossary.aenea: aēneus — of bronze, bronze (f. nom. sg., with 'proles')
glossary.aeoliis: Aeolius — Aeolian, of Aeolus the wind-king (n. abl. pl., with 'antris')
glossary.aequalibus: aequālis — equal, even (n. abl. pl., with spatiis 'at equal intervals')
glossary.aequalis: aequālis — even, uniform (f. nom. sg., predicative with 'terram'); at I.750 instead the adjective used as a noun, m. nom. sg. of Phaethon — a match, an equal ('animis aequalis et annis', matched in spirit and in years)
glossary.aequi: aequum — what is right, justice (n. gen. sg., after 'amantior'; not aequus 'level')
glossary.aequo: aequus — level, equal (n. abl.); ex aequo: on equal terms
glossary.aequor: aequor — the sea, the level expanse (n. nom. sg.)
glossary.aequora: aequor — the open sea, the sea-plains (n. acc. pl., after 'in')
glossary.aequoris: aequor — of the sea (gen.); aequoris instar: like the sea
glossary.aer: āēr — air, the air (m. nom. sg., Greek noun)
glossary.aera: āēr — the air (Greek acc.); or aes — bronze, and bronze instruments, cymbals and gongs (n. nom./acc. pl. of aes, aeris)
glossary.aere: aēr — air (m. abl. sg.), as in 'aere pendere', to hang in the air; also aes — bronze (n. abl. sg.), and so 'aere cavo', in a hollow bronze pot.
glossary.aesculeae: aesculeus — of oak, oaken (f. gen. sg., with 'frondis')
glossary.aestas: aestās — Summer, here personified as one of the seasons (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.aestu: aestus — heat (m. abl. sg., of cause)
glossary.aestusque: aestus — spells of heat, summers (m. acc. pl.) + -que
glossary.aeternum: aeternus — everlasting (n. nom. sg., with 'ver'); at I.663 instead n. acc. sg. agreeing with 'aevum' in 'in aevum' — into an everlasting age
glossary.aether: aethēr — upper air, sky (m. nom. sg., Greek noun)
glossary.aethera: aethēr — upper air, sky (m. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.aethere: aethēr — upper air, sky (m. abl. sg., of source)
glossary.aetheriis: aetherius — of the upper air, of the sky (m. abl. pl., with 'solibus')
glossary.aetherioque: aetherius — heavenly, of the sky (n. abl. sg., with 'sidere'; + -que 'and')
glossary.aethiopasque: Aethiopes — the Ethiopians (m. acc. pl., Greek acc.; + -que 'and')
glossary.aevum: aevum — age, era (n. acc. sg., with 'in')
glossary.agat: agō — would drive (3 sg. pres. act. subj., potential)
glossary.agere: agō — to keep, maintain (silence) (pres. inf., in indirect statement after 'vidit')
glossary.ages: agō — will you do (2 sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.agit: agō — drives, herds (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.agitabilis: agitābilis — easily stirred, mobile (m. nom. sg., with 'aer')
glossary.agitantia: agitō — stirring up, driving (pres. act. part., n. acc. pl., with nubila)
glossary.agitasse: agitō — to have shaken, tossed (syncopated perf. inf. = agitāvisse)
glossary.agitataque: agitō — shaken, tossed about (perf. part., n. acc. pl., with 'robora'; + -que)
glossary.ait: aiō — says, said (3 sg.; defective verb)
glossary.alas: āla — wings (f. acc. pl.; a bird's wings, and Mercury's winged sandals)
glossary.aliis: alius — to the others, other things (n. dat. pl., with 'obstabat')
glossary.alipedum: ālipēs — wing-footed, swift as wings (adj., m. gen. pl., with equorum)
glossary.aliquam: aliquī — some, some sort of (f. acc. sg., with 'faciem')
glossary.aliter: aliter — otherwise; non aliter quam: just as
glossary.aliud: alius — another thing, one thing (n. nom. sg.; 'aliud … aliis' = one another)
glossary.alta: altus — deep (n. acc. pl. at 349, with 'silentia'; f. nom. sg. earlier, with 'nix'); at I.630 f. abl. sg. with 'tellure' ('sub alta tellure', beneath the deep earth); at II.1 f. nom. sg. with 'regia' in the sense high, lofty; at II.71 n. acc. pl. with 'sidera', the high stars
glossary.altae: altus — lofty, deep (f. gen. sg., with 'mentis')
glossary.altior: altus — higher (compar., f. nom. sg., with 'unda')
glossary.altissima: altus — highest (superl., f. nom. sg., with via understood: the road is highest at mid-heaven)
glossary.altissimus: altus — highest (superl., m. nom. sg., with sol)
glossary.alto: altus — high (n. abl. with 'aethere': ab alto aethere, from the high aether); also 'deep'
glossary.altoque: altus — deep, intense (m. abl. sg., with 'aestu'; + -que)
glossary.altorum: altus — tall, deep (n. gen. pl., with nemorum)
glossary.altos: altus — high, lofty (m. acc. pl., with currus)
glossary.amantes: amāns — lovers (nom./voc. pl.; also acc. pl., as object)
glossary.amantior: amāns — more loving of, fonder of (compar., m. nom. sg.; + gen. 'aequi')
glossary.amantis: amāns — a lover (pres. part. as noun, m. gen. sg., with 'nomen')
glossary.amara: amārus — bitter (f. abl. sg., with herba)
glossary.amatum: amō — beloved (perf. part., n. acc.); corpus amatum: the beloved body
glossary.ambiguo: ambiguum — doubt, uncertainty (n. abl. sg.; in ambiguo est, 'is in doubt')
glossary.ambiguum: at I.765 ambiguus — uncertain, undecided (n. nom. sg., used impersonally: '[it is] unclear whether … or'); at II.9 instead of Proteus, shifting, of changeable shape (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.ambitae: ambiō — encircled, surrounded (perf. part., f. gen. sg., with 'terrae')
glossary.amissam: āmittō — lost (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., 'as one lost')
glossary.amnes: amnis — rivers (m. acc. pl.); at I.581 instead m. nom. pl., subject of 'deducunt' ('amnes alii', the other rivers)
glossary.amnis: amnis — of the river (m. gen. sg. with magni — not the nominative; 'the inner chambers of the great river')
glossary.amor: amor — love (m. nom. sg.); at 480 and 532 Amor, the god Love (Cupid)
glossary.amore: amor — love (m. abl. sg., abl. of agent/means with victus)
glossary.amores: amor — loves, love-affairs (m. acc. pl., poetic pl.); at 461 object of 'inritare'; earlier 'her beloved'
glossary.amoris: Amor — Love, the god Cupid (m. gen. sg.; capitalised in the edition)
glossary.amphitrite: Amphitrītē — Amphitrite, sea-goddess, wife of Neptune; here the sea itself (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.amphrysos: Amphrȳsos — the Amphrysus, a Thessalian river and its river-god (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.amplexaque: amplector — and having embraced (deponent perf. part., f. nom. + -que)
glossary.an: an — whether (in indirect question, 223); at 196 introducing a direct question, 'do you really…?'; at I.586 whether ('an sit apud manes'); at I.765 the second member of a double indirect question, 'or' ('precibus … an ira', by prayers or rather by anger)
glossary.anguipedum: anguipēs — of the snake-footed ones, i.e. the Giants (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.animalia: animal — living creatures (n.; acc. pl. at 416, 425; nom. pl. at 464)
glossary.animalibus: animal — living creatures (n. abl. pl., with 'orba')
glossary.animas: anima — souls, breath of life (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.animasse: animō — to have given life to, quickened (syncopated perf. inf. = animavisse)
glossary.animi: animus — spirits, tempers (m. nom. pl.; of the horses)
glossary.animis: animus — at I.750 in spirit (m. abl. pl., abl. of respect with aequalis); at II.39 instead from our mind (m. dat. pl., dat. of separation with detrahe)
glossary.animo: animus — mind, heart (m. abl. sg., of place where)
glossary.animoque: animus — and with the mind, heart (abl. + -que)
glossary.animosos: animōsus — spirited, mettlesome (m. acc. pl., with quadrupedes)
glossary.anni: annus — year (m. gen. sg., with 'longi'; not nom. pl.)
glossary.annis: annus — at I.750 in years (m. abl. pl., abl. of respect); at II.55 instead to years (m. dat. pl., with conveniant)
glossary.annum: annus — the year (m. acc. sg., object of 'exegit')
glossary.annus: annus — the Year, here personified beside Day and Month (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.ante: ante — before, earlier (adverb, at 442 and 487); before, in front of (prep. + acc., at 563)
glossary.antiquas: antīquus — ancient, of old (f. acc. pl., with 'figuras')
glossary.antiqui: antīquus — old, former (n. gen. sg., with 'veris')
glossary.antiquo: antīquus — old, former (m. abl. sg., with 'alveo')
glossary.antra: antrum — caves (n. nom. pl., predicate of 'fuerunt')
glossary.anxia: anxius — anxious, uneasy (f. nom. sg.; + gen. furti 'about the intrigue')
glossary.aonios: Aonius — Aonian, Boeotian (m. acc. pl.; a noun like 'agros' understood)
glossary.apertis: aperiō — thrown open (perf. part., f. abl. pl., with 'valvis')
glossary.aperto: aperiō — open, plain (perf. part., n. abl. sg., with 'discrimine')
glossary.apertos: apertus — open, unobstructed (m. acc. pl., with 'campos')
glossary.apidanusque: Apidanus — the Apidanus, a Thessalian river and its river-god (m. nom. sg.; + -que 'and')
glossary.apollineas: Apollineus — Apollo's, of Apollo (f. acc. pl., with 'medullas')
glossary.apta: aptus — suited, fitted (f. nom. sg., with 'concordia'; + dat. 'fetibus')
glossary.aptamque: aptus — suited, fit (f. acc. sg., with umbram; + dat. pastoribus; + -que 'and')
glossary.aptato: aptō — fitted, set in place (perf. part., m. abl.); aptato mucrone: the point set
glossary.aptos: aptus — fit, suited (m. acc. pl.) + dat.
glossary.apud: apud — among, in the presence of (prep. + acc.)
glossary.aquae: aqua — water, waters (f.; gen. sg., also dat. sg. and nom. pl.); at 432 with 'pugnax', at odds with water (gen., or dat.); at IV.459 nom. pl., subject of 'deprenduntur' — the waters are not caught
glossary.aquarum: aqua — of the waters (f. gen. pl.)
glossary.aquilone: Aquilō — the North Wind (m. abl. sg., of means with 'remotis')
glossary.aquilonem: Aquilō — the North Wind (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.aquis: aqua — water (f. abl. pl.); here abl. of means: mollit aquis, he softens with water
glossary.arae: āra — altars (f. nom. pl.; not gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.ararat: arō — had ploughed (3 sg. pluperf., syncopated = arāverat)
glossary.arbore: arbor — tree (f. abl. sg.); at 451 with 'de', from any tree at all; earlier abl. of source, 'patula Iovis arbore'
glossary.arborei: arboreus — of the tree (m. nom. pl.); arborei fetus: the tree's fruit
glossary.arboreis: arboreus — of trees, tree- (f. abl. pl., with frondibus)
glossary.arboribus: arbor — trees (f. abl. pl., abl. of means with consita)
glossary.arbuteos: arbuteus — of the arbutus, strawberry-tree (m. acc. pl., with 'fetus')
glossary.arcadiae: Arcadia — Arcadia, the mountainous inland region of the Peloponnese (f. gen. sg.)
glossary.arcadis: Arcas — the Arcadian, i.e. Lycaon (m. gen. sg., with 'tyranni')
glossary.arcus: arcus — bow, bows (m., 4th decl.; nom. sg., and acc. pl. -ūs, as at IV.302, 'nec arcus flectere', nor to bend bows); at II.81 m. acc. pl. (4th decl. -ūs), governed by 'per' — the Haemonian bows, i.e. the Archer
glossary.ardeat: ardeō — should blaze, catch fire (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.ardent: ardeō — blaze up, catch fire (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.ardentibus: ārdeō — burning, eager (pres. part., n. abl. pl., with 'studiis')
glossary.ardentior: ārdēns — hotter, more burning (comparative, f. nom. sg., of the fifth zone)
glossary.ardesceret: ardēscō — would catch fire, blaze up (3 sg. imperf. subj., after 'ne')
glossary.arduus: arduus — steep, lofty (m. nom. sg., with 'aether')
glossary.arestoridae: Arestoridēs — son of Arestor, patronymic of Argus (m. dat. sg.)
glossary.arge: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman (m. voc. sg.)
glossary.argentea: argenteus — of silver (f. nom. sg., with 'proles')
glossary.argenteus: argenteus — of silver, silver (m. nom. sg., with ordo)
glossary.argo: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman set to guard Io (m. dat. sg. in all three lines)
glossary.argolicae: Argolicus — Argive, of Argos (f. gen. sg., with paelicis; of Io)
glossary.argum: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.argus: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.aristis: arista — ears of grain (f. abl. pl.); at 492 abl. absolute 'demptis aristis', the ears once stripped off; earlier of means
glossary.arma: arma — arms, weapons (n. acc. pl.; plural only)
glossary.armenta: armentum — herds of cattle (n. acc. pl.)
glossary.armento: armentum — herd (n. abl. sg.; quo armento 'from what herd')
glossary.arquitenens: arquitenēns — the Bow-bearer, the Archer (m. nom. sg., of Apollo; the edition's spelling for arcitenens)
glossary.arte: ars — skill, means (f. abl. sg., with 'qua')
glossary.artibus: ars — arts, crafts (f. abl. pl., with 'paternis')
glossary.artior: artus — narrower, tighter (compar. adj., m. nom. sg., with orbis)
glossary.artus: artus — limbs (m. acc. pl., object of 'mollit')
glossary.arvis: arvum — fields, ploughland (n. abl. pl., after 'ab')
glossary.aspera: asper — rough, harsh (n. nom. pl., with 'loca')
glossary.astra: astrum — stars (n.; acc. pl. at 316, object of 'petit'; nom. pl. earlier)
glossary.astraea: Astraea — Astraea, goddess of Justice, last of the gods to leave earth (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.atlantiades: Atlantiadēs — the descendant of Atlas (m. nom. sg.): Mercury, grandson of Atlas through Maia, or Mercury's son Hermaphroditus
glossary.atram: āter — black, dark (f. acc.); in atram faciem: to a dark hue
glossary.attonitum: attonō — thunderstruck, stunned (perf. part., m. acc. sg., with 'ausum')
glossary.auctaque: augeō — increased, enhanced (perf. part., f. nom. sg., with 'forma'; + -que)
glossary.auctor: auctor — originator, source; at II.88 the giver (of a gift) (m. nom. sg. in both lines)
glossary.audita: audiō — heard (perf. part., f. nom. sg., with 'bucina')
glossary.auditque: audiō — hears (3 sg. pres. act. ind.; + -que 'and')
glossary.auferat: auferō — may carry off, sweep away (3 sg. pres. act. subj., in a ne clause of fearing/purpose)
glossary.auget: augeō — increases, swells (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.auguste: Augustus — Augustus, the emperor (m. voc. sg.)
glossary.augustis: Augustus — of Augustus, the emperor's (m. abl. pl., with 'postibus'; could also be the adjective augustus 'revered', but the edition capitalises)
glossary.aura: aura — breeze (f.); nom. sg. at 529, subject of 'dabat'; abl. of comparison at 502, 'ocior aura levi', swifter than a light breeze
glossary.auratum: aurātus — golden, gilded (n. nom. sg., of the arrow)
glossary.aureus: aureus — golden, of gold (m. nom. sg.; twice in II.107, of axis and temo)
glossary.auris: aura — breezes (f. abl. pl., with 'tepentibus'); not auris 'ear'
glossary.auro: aurum — than gold (n. abl. sg., of comparison with 'deterior'); at II.2 instead a plain abl. of means with 'micante', gleaming with gold
glossary.auroram: Aurōra — Aurora, the Dawn; here the East (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.austro: Auster — the South Wind (m. abl. sg.; with 'ab', from the south, and in an ablative absolute, 'victo austro', the south wind having been beaten).
glossary.ausum: audeō — the one who had dared (perf. part. as noun, m. acc. sg.)
glossary.autumnus: autumnus — Autumn, here personified as one of the seasons (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.auxiliaribus: auxiliāris — helping, reinforcing (f. abl. pl., with 'undis')
glossary.aversata: āversor — having spurned, turned away from (perf. part. of a deponent, f. nom. sg.; active in sense, + acc. 'petentes')
glossary.aversus: āvertō — turned away (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.: 'though turned away')
glossary.avia: avius — pathless, trackless (n. acc. pl., with 'nemora'); at I.701 the adjective used as a noun, n. acc. pl. after 'per' — through trackless country
glossary.avidissima: avidus — most greedy for (superlative, f. nom. sg., + gen. 'caedis')
glossary.axe: axis — axle; by extension the chariot (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.axis: axis — the axle of the sky, the heavens (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.barba: barba — beard (f.; nom. sg. at 266, abl. sg. at 339 with 'madida')
glossary.beatum: beātus — blessed, made happy (m. acc. sg., with nescio quem)

glossary.adsumus: adsum — we are here, we are at hand (1 pl. pres. ind.)
glossary.adulter: adulter — adulterer, paramour (m. nom. sg.; also used as an adj., 'adulterous')
glossary.adunco: aduncus — hooked, curved inward (adj., m./n. abl. sg.; here with 'cornu')
glossary.advena: advena — newcomer, stranger, foreigner (1st-decl. noun of common gender, here m. nom. sg. of Bacchus; the form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.advertite: advertō — turn (something) toward! direct! (2 pl. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.aeaeae: Aeaeus — Aeaean, of Aeaea, Circe's island (adj., f. gen. sg. agreeing with 'Circes'; the form is also dat. sg./nom. pl.)

glossary.aethalion: Aethaliōn — Aethalion, one of the Tyrrhenian sailors (m. nom. sg., Greek)

glossary.aguntur: agō — are carried out, are fulfilled; are driven (3 pl. pres. pass. ind.)
glossary.albentia: albeō — whitening, growing white (pres. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here with 'tempora', temples)

glossary.alius: alius — another, any other (m. nom. sg.; irregular gen. alīus, dat. aliī)
glossary.amatos: amō — loved, longed-for (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.; here with 'thalamos')

glossary.ambrosiam: ambrosia — ambrosia, the food of the gods (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.amoribus: amor — love, passion (m. dat./abl. pl.; the pl. often means a single love-affair)
glossary.amplius: amplius — further, more, any longer (comparative adv.; the same form is the n. nom./acc. sg. of amplior 'larger')
glossary.anguigenae: anguigena — snake-born (m. voc. pl. here, addressing the Thebans sprung from the dragon's teeth; the form is also nom. pl. and gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.animorum: animus — of spirits, of courage, of tempers (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.antemnas: antemna — yard-arms, the spars crossing a mast (f. acc. pl.)

glossary.applicor: applicō — I am brought to land, put in to shore (1 sg. pres. pass. ind.)

glossary.aranea: arānea — spider; cobweb (f. nom. sg.; here nom., subject of 'pendet')
glossary.arbitrium: arbitrium — decision, discretion, control (n. nom./acc. sg.; here acc.)
glossary.arctonque: Arctos — and the Bear, the constellation Ursa; the north (Greek f. acc. sg. Arcton + -que)
glossary.argolicas: Argolicus — Argive, of Argos (adj., f. acc. pl.; here with 'portas')
glossary.ars: ars — skill, craft, trade (f. nom. sg.)

glossary.attonuit: attonō — stunned, struck senseless, thunder-struck (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.attrahite: attrahō — drag here! haul in! (2 pl. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.attulerat: afferō — had brought, had won (for someone) (3 sg. pluperf. act.)
glossary.audacissimus: audāx — boldest, most reckless (superlative, m. nom. sg.)
glossary.auguris: augur — of the seer, of the augur (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.auguror: auguror — I foretell, prophesy, forebode (1 sg. pres. ind. of the deponent; active in sense)
glossary.autonoë: Autonoē — Autonoe, daughter of Cadmus and mother of Actaeon (f. voc. sg. here; nom. is identical, Greek)
glossary.autumni: autumnus — of autumn (m. gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.avulsumque: āvellō — and torn off, wrenched away (perf. pass. part., n. acc. sg. + -que; here with 'caput')
glossary.avus: avus — grandfather (m. nom. sg.; here Cadmus, Pentheus's grandfather)

glossary.brumales: brūmālis — of midwinter, wintry (adj., f./m. nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. with 'horas')
glossary.cacumine: cacūmen — peak, summit, tip (n. abl. sg.)

glossary.calorem: calor — warmth, vital heat (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.canoro: canōrus — melodious, ringing, clear-toned (adj., m./n. abl. sg.; here with 'aere')
glossary.cantibus: cantus — songs, chants (m. dat./abl. pl., 4th decl.)

glossary.carae: cārus — dear, beloved (adj., f. gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl.; here dat. with 'natae')
glossary.carerent: careō — would lack, would be free from (3 pl. imperf. subj.; + abl.)
glossary.carinam: carīna — keel; by metonymy ship (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.carpunt: carpō — pluck, crop, graze on (3 pl. pres. act.)

glossary.cernere: cernō — to see, discern, distinguish (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.chiae: Chius — of Chios, Chian (adj., f. gen. sg. here with 'telluris'; the form is also dat. sg./nom. pl.)
glossary.chori: chorus — of a dance, of a dancing band (m. gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.cibique: cibus — and of food (m. gen. sg. + -que; here gen. with 'expers'; the form is also nom. pl.)

glossary.clamore: clāmor — shout, outcry, uproar (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.claudere: claudō — to shut, close, bar (pres. act. inf.; the form is also 2 sg. pres. pass.)

glossary.cogam: cōgō — I shall force, compel, drive together (1 sg. fut. act.; the form is also pres. subj.)
glossary.cognita: cognōscō — learned of, once known, brought to light (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. here; the form is also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.colerent: colō — would till, would farm; would tend (3 pl. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.collaque: collum — and the neck (n. acc. pl. + -que; poetic pl. for sg.)
glossary.coloris: color — of colour, of complexion (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.colunt: colō — tend, cultivate; honour, worship (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.colus: colus — distaff, the staff holding unspun wool (usually f., nom. sg.; 4th decl. with 2nd-decl. forms — not from colō 'till' or collum 'neck')
glossary.comitesque: comes — and companions, comrades (m./f. nom. or acc. pl. + -que; here acc., object of 'voco')

glossary.coronae: corōna — garlands, wreaths (f. nom. pl. here; the form is also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.corpusque: corpus — and the body (n. nom./acc. sg. + -que)
glossary.corripiunt: corripiō — seize; upbraid, rebuke sharply (3 pl. pres. act.; with 'dictis' = they scold him)
glossary.corymbis: corymbus — clusters of ivy-berries (m. dat./abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.creati: creō — born, sprung, begotten (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl. here with 'sitis'; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.cruciataque: cruciō — and tortured, tormented (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. + -que; here with 'corpora')
glossary.crudelia: crūdēlis — cruel, savage (adj., n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.crudus: crūdus — raw, unripe; (of a person) harsh, unfeeling (adj., m. nom. sg.; here of the merciless father)
glossary.cruentati: cruentō — bloodstained, smeared with blood (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
glossary.cruentis: cruentus — bloody, bloodstained (adj., dat./abl. pl.; here abl. with 'digitis')
glossary.cultum: cultus — dress, appearance, style of grooming (m. acc. sg., 4th decl.; identical in form to the perf. part. of colō 'tended, honoured')

glossary.cutis: cutis — skin, hide (f. nom. sg.; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.cythereia: Cytherēa — the Cytherean, i.e. Venus, from her island Cythera (f. nom. sg.; adjectival in origin)
glossary.damnantem: damnō — condemning, passing sentence on (pres. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.danti: dō — to one giving, as (he) gives (pres. part., m./f. dat. sg.; here dat. of reference, 'to me as I set the sails')
glossary.dature: dō — you who are destined to give (fut. act. part., m. voc. sg.)
glossary.decebat: decet — it was fitting, it was becoming (3 sg. imperf. of the impersonal decet; + acc. and inf.)
glossary.decipere: dēcipiō — to deceive, trick, catch (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.decuit: decet — it was fitting, it became (her) (3 sg. perf. of the impersonal decet)
glossary.decurrere: dēcurrō — to run down, flow down (pres. act. inf. here, with 'vidi'; the form is also 3 pl. perf. act., = dēcurrērunt)
glossary.deferre: dēferō — to carry off, convey, bring down (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.deficis: dēficiō — you fail, grow faint, are eclipsed (2 sg. pres. act.)

glossary.deiectis: dēiciō — thrown down, struck off, torn away (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. pl.; here abl. with 'membris')
glossary.delatus: dēferō — carried down, brought (to a place) (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.delum: Dēlos — Delos, the Aegean island sacred to Apollo (f. acc. sg., Greek Dēlos; the island keeps Greek f. gender)
glossary.dementer: dēmenter — madly, out of one's senses (adv.)
glossary.demittite: dēmittō — send down! cast down! (2 pl. pres. act. imperat.; not dīmittite 'dismiss, let go')
glossary.des: dō — may you give, grant (2 sg. pres. subj. act.; here in a request)
glossary.deserto: dēserō — deserted, abandoned, lonely (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.; here with 'agro')
glossary.desiluit: dēsiliō — leapt down, jumped off (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.despecta: dēspiciō — looked down on, scorned, slighted (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.dextera: dexter — on the right, to the right (adj., f. nom. sg.; the same form is the noun dextera 'right hand')
glossary.dextramque: dextra — and the right hand (f. acc. sg. + -que; from the adj. dexter used as a noun, manus understood)
glossary.diamque: Dīa — and Dia, the old name of Naxos (f. acc. sg. + -que)
glossary.dicens: dīcō — saying (pres. part., m./f. nom. sg.)
glossary.dicite: dīcō — tell! say! (2 pl. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.dictys: Dictys — Dictys, one of the Tyrrhenian sailors, the best climber aboard (m. nom. sg., Greek)
glossary.diffamatumque: diffāmō — and spread abroad, made notorious (perf. pass. part., n. acc. sg. + -que; here with 'adulterium')
glossary.digitis: digitus — fingers (m. dat./abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.dignabere: dignor — you will deign, will think worthy (2 sg. fut. of the deponent, = dignāberis; + abl. of the honour)

glossary.diligis: dīligō — you love, hold dear, single out (2 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.dimidiae: dīmidius — half, halved (adj., f. gen. sg. here with 'lunae'; the form is also dat. sg./nom. pl.)
glossary.direpta: dīripiō — torn apart, pulled to pieces (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here with 'membra')
glossary.diris: dīrus — dreadful, dire, ill-omened (adj., dat./abl. pl.; here abl. with 'tormentis'; as a f. pl. noun, Dīrae = the Furies)
glossary.diruerent: dīruō — would tear down, would demolish (3 pl. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.distinguunt: distinguō — pick out, adorn, variegate (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.diurnis: diurnus — of the day, daily (adj., dat./abl. pl.; here with 'ministeriis')
glossary.dixi: dīcō — I said, I told (1 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.dolentius: dolēns — more painful, more grievous; more grievously (comparative, n. nom./acc. sg., or comparative adv. from dolenter)
glossary.dolor: dolor — pain, grief; resentment, wounded feeling (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.dolorem: dolor — grief, pain, resentment (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.doque: dō — and I give, and I make (1 sg. pres. act. + -que; 'doque saltus' = and I make a leap)
glossary.dubito: dubitō — I am uncertain, I doubt, I hesitate (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.ducemque: dux — and the leader, guide, chief (m./f. acc. sg. + -que)
glossary.ducentem: dūcō — drawing out, spinning (thread) (pres. part., m./f. acc. sg.)

glossary.eburnas: eburnus — of ivory, ivory-inlaid (adj., f. acc. pl.; here with 'valvas')
glossary.echione: Echīōn — from Echion, one of the Sown Men of Thebes and father of Pentheus (m. abl. sg., Greek Echīōn, -onis)
glossary.echionides: Echīonidēs — son of Echion, i.e. Pentheus (m. nom. sg.; Greek patronymic in -idēs)
glossary.efficit: efficiō — makes, fashions, brings about (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.electus: ēligō — chosen, picked out, singled out (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.elimat: ēlīmō — files smooth, polishes off, finishes (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.emerguntque: ēmergō — and they come up, rise to the surface (3 pl. pres. act. + -que)
glossary.enectum: ēnecō — worn out, crushed, done to death (perf. pass. part., m./n. acc. sg.; here with 'caput')

glossary.epopeus: Epopeus — Epopeus, the rowers' timekeeper on the ship (m. nom. sg., Greek)

glossary.errat: errō — wanders, roams, strays (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.essemus: sum — we should be, we would be (1 pl. imperf. subj. of sum; not ēssēmus from edō 'eat')
glossary.este: sum — be! (2 pl. pres. imperat. of sum; not ēste 'eat!' from edō)

glossary.eurynome: Eurynomē — Eurynome, wife of Orchamus and mother of Leucothoe (f. nom. sg., Greek)
glossary.eurynomes: Eurynomē — of Eurynome (f. gen. sg., Greek Eurynomē, gen. -ēs)
glossary.evenient: ēveniō — they will come to pass, will turn out so (3 pl. fut. ind. act.)
glossary.excusare: excūsō — to excuse, plead in excuse for (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.excussum: excutiō — shaken off, flung out (perf. pass. part., m./n. acc. sg.; here m., of the god shaken from the ship)
glossary.excute: excutiō — shake off! throw off! (2 sg. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.exemplis: exemplum — examples, warnings, precedents (n. dat./abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.exigit: exigō — exacts, demands, requires (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.explet: expleō — fills out, completes, carries through (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.expresso: exprimō — pressed out, forced out, arched up (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.; here with 'curvamine')
glossary.exsangues: exsanguis — bloodless, pale, drained (adj., m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. with 'herbas')
glossary.exsilium: exsilium — exile, banishment (n. nom./acc. sg.; here acc.)
glossary.exsiluere: exsiliō — leapt up, sprang up (3 pl. perf. act., = exsiluērunt)
glossary.exsurgo: exsurgō — I rise, get up, stand up (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.fabrilis: fabrīlis — of a craftsman, a workman's (adj., f. nom. sg.; here with 'dextra')
glossary.fabula: fābula — story, tale; the talk of the town (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.facienda: faciō — to be performed, that must be done (gerundive, n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. with 'sacra')
glossary.facis: faciō — you do, you are doing (2 sg. pres. act.; not facis, gen. sg. of fax 'torch')
glossary.facitis: faciō — you (pl.) are doing, are up to (2 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.factum: factum — deed, act, thing done (n. nom./acc. sg.; identical in form to the perf. pass. part. of faciō 'done, made')
glossary.falcata: falcātus — sickle-shaped, curved like a scythe (adj., f. nom. sg.; here with 'cauda')
glossary.fallaces: fallāx — deceitful, treacherous, false-swearing (adj., m. nom. pl.)
glossary.fallitis: fallō — you (pl.) deceive, cheat, betray (2 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.famulae: famula — maidservants, handmaids (f. voc. pl. here; the form is also nom. pl. and gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.famuli: famulus — servants, attendants (m. voc. pl. here; the form is also nom. pl. and gen. sg.)
glossary.famulis: famulus — to the servants, for the attendants (m. dat./abl. pl.; here dat. with 'imperat')
glossary.famulumque: famulus — and a servant, attendant (m. acc. sg. + -que; the form can also be the gen. pl., famulum = famulōrum)
glossary.fatentem: fateor — confessing, admitting (pres. part. of the deponent, m./f. acc. sg.; active in sense)

glossary.femineae: fēmineus — of women, womanish (adj., f. nom. pl. here with 'voces'; the form is also gen./dat. sg.)

glossary.fervens: ferveō — boiling, seething, raging (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.festisque: fēstus — and festal, holiday, festive (adj., m./n. dat./abl. pl. + -que; here abl. with 'ululatibus')

glossary.flavus: flāvus — golden-yellow, blond (adj., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.flebam: fleō — I was weeping (1 sg. impf. act.)
glossary.flectebat: flectō — was bending, turning (3 sg. impf. act.)
glossary.flectere: flectō — to bend, turn, steer (pres. act. inf.; the same form is 2 sg. pres. pass. 'you are turned' and the pres. pass. imperative)
glossary.flecti: flectō — to be bent, to be curved (pres. pass. inf.)
glossary.flenti: fleō — to/for one weeping (pres. part. flēns, dat. sg. of any gender; also abl. sg.; here dat. after similis)
glossary.foedabis: foedō — you will defile, disfigure, befoul (2 sg. fut. act.)
glossary.formosissima: formōsus — most beautiful (superl. adj., f. nom. sg.; the form is also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.fortes: fortis — brave, strong (adj., m./f. acc. pl., here used as a noun 'the brave'; the form is also nom./voc. pl.)
glossary.fraudem: fraus — deceit, trickery, harm (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.fraudes: fraus — deceits, tricks (f. nom./acc. pl.; not fraudēs, 2 sg. pres. subj. of fraudō 'you would cheat')
glossary.fremit: fremō — roars, snorts, resounds (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.fremunt: fremō — they roar, resound, are loud (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.frequentant: frequentō — they throng to, crowd, celebrate in numbers (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.frequentes: frequentō — you attend, take part in, celebrate (2 sg. pres. subj., here in an indirect question; not frequentēs, nom./acc. pl. of the adj. frequēns 'crowded, thronging', which the letters equally allow)
glossary.frequento: frequentō — I attend, take part in, celebrate (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.fueris: sum — you have been / you will have been (2 sg. perf. subj. or fut. perf. ind.; with a perf. participle it forms the perf. subj. or fut. perf. of a deponent or passive)
glossary.fune: fūnis — rope, cable, ship's line (m. abl. sg.; not fūnus 'funeral, corpse', whose abl. is fūnere)
glossary.funes: fūnis — ropes, cables (m. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.; not from fūnus 'funeral')
glossary.furens: furō — raging, frenzied, out of one's mind (pres. part. furēns, nom. sg. of any gender; also n. acc. sg.)
glossary.furor: furor — madness, frenzy, raving (m. nom. sg.; not fūror 'I steal', 1 sg. of the deponent fūror)
glossary.furtique: fūrtum — and of the theft, of the stolen love-affair (n. gen. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.fuso: fūsus — spindle (m. abl. sg.; not fūsus, perf. part. of fundō 'poured out, spread', which has the identical m./n. dat./abl. sg.)
glossary.fusus: fūsus — spindle (m. nom. sg.; not fūsus 'poured out', perf. part. of fundō)
glossary.galeaque: galea — and with a helmet (f. abl. sg.; the bare form is also nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.gelidos: gelidus — icy, chill (adj., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.gelidumque: gelidus — cold, chilled (adj., m. acc. sg.; also n. nom./acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.geminae: geminus — twin, paired (adj., f. nom./voc. pl., here vocative with sorores; also f. gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.geminaque: geminus — and twofold, double, twin (adj., f. abl. sg.; also f. nom. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.gentis: gēns — of a clan, race, people (f. gen. sg.; the form also serves as the older acc. pl. gentīs 'peoples')
glossary.glaebas: glaeba — clods, lumps of soil (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.gradumque: gradus — and the step, gait, bearing (m. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.grave: gravis — heavy, grievous, serious (adj., n. nom./acc. sg.; the same neuter also serves as an adverb, 'heavily, gravely')
glossary.habeo: habeō — I have, hold, possess (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.haerent: haereō — they stick fast, cling, are held fast (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.haerentes: haereō — clinging, holding on (pres. part. haerēns, m./f. nom. or acc. pl.)
glossary.haererem: haereō — I might stick fast, might remain stuck (1 sg. impf. subj. act.)
glossary.haesisse: haereō — to have stuck fast, to have clung (perf. act. inf.)
glossary.haesissem: haereō — I had stuck fast / would have stuck fast (1 sg. pluperf. subj. act.)
glossary.hamis: hāmus — hooks, fish-hooks (m. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
glossary.hederae: hedera — ivy, ivy-tendrils (f. nom. pl.; also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.heres: hērēs — heir, inheritor (m./f. nom. sg.; also written haerēs, so easily confused with haerēs 'you cling', 2 sg. of haereō)

glossary.humili: humilis — low, lowly, humble (adj., m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.hyadasque: Hyades — and the Hyades, the rain-bringing star-cluster in Taurus (Greek f. acc. pl. Hyadas) + -que 'and'

glossary.iacebas: iaceō — you lay, you were lying (2 sg. impf. act.; from iaceō 'lie', not iaciō 'throw', whose impf. is iaciēbās)

glossary.iactavit: iactō — tossed, flung about (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.iacuere: iaceō — they lay, lay stretched out (3 pl. perf. act. = iacuērunt; from iaceō 'lie', not iaciō 'throw')
glossary.ignesque: ignis — and fires (m. nom. or acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.ignisque: ignis — and fire (m. nom. sg.; the form is also gen. sg. 'of fire') + -que 'and'
glossary.ignota: ignōtus — unknown, unfamiliar, strange (adj., n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom./abl. sg.; from in- + nōtus)
glossary.impediunt: impediō — they entangle, hamper, block (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.impellit: impellō — drives on, strikes, urges forward (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.impia: impius — impious, undutiful, wicked (adj., f. nom. sg.; also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.inbutum: imbuō — steeped, soaked, drenched (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.; inbutum is Magnus's unassimilated spelling of imbūtum)
glossary.incidis: incidō (in + cadō) — you fall into, sink into, come down upon (2 sg. pres. act.; not incīdō (in + caedō) 'you cut into', which is spelled the same and differs only in vowel length)
glossary.incipit: incipiō — begins, sets about (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.incompta: incomptus — unkempt, undressed, untrimmed (adj./perf. pass. part. of in- + cōmō, f. nom. sg.; also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.increpor: increpō — I am rebuked, am shouted at, am railed against (1 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.indicat: indicō, -āre — points out, discloses, informs on (3 sg. pres. act.; distinct from indīcō, -dīcere 'proclaim, declare', whose 3 sg. is indīcit)
glossary.indicii: indicium — of the disclosure, of the informing, of the tip-off (n. gen. sg.)
glossary.indiciumque: indicium — and evidence, disclosure, betrayal (n. nom./acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.inermi: inermis — unarmed, weaponless (adj., m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.inferre: īnferō — to bring in, carry in, bring against (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.ingens: ingēns — huge, vast, mighty (adj., nom. sg. of any gender; also n. acc. sg.)
glossary.inludens: illūdō — mocking, making sport of, playing with (pres. part., nom. sg.; inludens is the unassimilated spelling of illūdēns)
glossary.inmansuetusque: immānsuētus — and untamed, savage, unrelenting (adj., m. nom. sg.; unassimilated spelling of immānsuētus) + -que 'and'
glossary.inmittor: immittō — I am let loose, I fling myself (1 sg. pres. pass., here with middle force, 'I launch myself' onto + dat.; unassimilated spelling of immittor)
glossary.inmurmurat: immurmurō — mutters at, murmurs against (3 sg. pres. act.; unassimilated spelling of immurmurat)

glossary.inopino: inopīnus — unexpected, unlooked-for (adj., m./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.inritaturque: irrītō — and is provoked, is goaded on (3 sg. pres. pass.; unassimilated spelling of irrītātur) + -que 'and'
glossary.insania: īnsānia — madness, frenzy, derangement (f. nom. sg.; the form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.insano: īnsānus — mad, frenzied, wild (adj., m./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.; an adjective here, not a form of īnsāniō 'rave')
glossary.instrumenta: īnstrūmentum — instruments, equipment, apparatus (n. nom. or acc. pl.)
glossary.interiit: intereō — perished, died, was destroyed (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.intextum: intexō — woven in, embroidered into (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
glossary.intortos: intorqueō — twisted, plaited, wound tight (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.invidit: invideō — envied, begrudged, looked on with envy (3 sg. perf. act.; the pres. would be invidet)
glossary.invitae: invītus — unwilling, against her will (adj., f. dat. sg.; also f. gen. sg. and nom. pl.; not from invītō 'invite')
glossary.ipsoque: ipse — and by that very one, by him/it himself (intensive pron./adj., m./n. abl. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.ismenides: Ismēnis — the Ismenides, women of Thebes (f. nom. pl., Greek; named from the Theban river Ismēnus)
glossary.isque: is — and he, and that man (m. nom. sg. of the demonstrative is, ea, id) + -que 'and'
glossary.ite: eō — go! (2 pl. pres. imperative of eō, īre 'go')
glossary.iubent: iubeō — they order, bid, command (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.iunonigenaeque: Iūnōnigena — and to the son of Juno, i.e. Vulcan (m. dat. sg., used here adjectivally with marītō) + -que 'and'
glossary.iurant: iūrō — they swear, take an oath (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.iuris: iūs — of right, of authority, of legal power (n. gen. sg.; not the identical iūs, iūris 'broth, soup')
glossary.iussae: iubeō — ordered, commanded (perf. pass. part., f. gen./dat. sg. or f. nom. pl.; here gen. sg. agreeing with necis, 'of the killing that was ordered')
glossary.iussis: iussum — to/for the orders, commands (n. dat. or abl. pl.; the same form is also the perf. pass. part. of iubeō, m./n. dat./abl. pl., 'to those who were ordered')
glossary.iuvant: iuvō — they please, delight; they help (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.laborant: labōrō — they toil, strive, struggle (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.laboribus: labor — to/for or by labours, hardships, toils (m. dat. or abl. pl.; not from lābor 'slip, glide')
glossary.lacer: lacer — torn, mangled, rent to pieces (adj., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.lacerata: lacerō — torn to pieces, mangled (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.lacrimisque: lacrima — and with tears (f. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.lacuque: lacus — and for/by the pool, lake, water (m. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.laedit: laedō — hurts, wounds, injures (3 sg. pres. act.; the perf. would be laesit)
glossary.laevam: laevus — the left (adj., f. acc. sg., here used as a noun with 'partem' understood, 'the left-hand side'; not laeva 'the left hand' in the nom.)
glossary.lanigerosve: lāniger — wool-bearing, fleecy (adj., m. acc. pl.) + -ve 'or'
glossary.lapsasque: lābor — and having slipped off, having fallen away (perf. part. of the deponent lābor, f. acc. pl.; here with catēnās) + -que 'and'
glossary.laqueos: laqueus — nooses, snares, running knots (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.larum: lār — of household gods, hence of home, hearth, shelter (m. gen. pl., poetic beside larium; 'larum inpatiens' = unable to bear a roof over her)
glossary.lascivaque: lascīvus — and playful, wanton, frisking (adj., n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom./abl. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.lati: lātus (adj.) — broad, wide (m. nom. pl.; also m./n. gen. sg.; not latus, lateris n. 'side, flank', nor lātus, the perf. part. of ferō, 'carried, borne')
glossary.laticesque: latex — and waters, liquids, streams (m. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.lecto: lectus — bed, couch (m. dat./abl. sg.; not lēctus, perf. part. of legō 'gathered, chosen, read', which has the identical m./n. dat./abl. sg.)
glossary.lemnius: Lemnius — the Lemnian, i.e. Vulcan, whose cult centre was the island of Lemnos (adj. used as a name, m. nom. sg.)
glossary.leuconoe: Leuconoë — Leuconoe, one of the daughters of Minyas who tell these tales (Greek f. nom. sg.)
glossary.leucothoe: Leucothoë — Leucothoe, daughter of Orchamus, loved by the Sun (Greek f. nom. sg.; distinct from the sea-goddess Leucothea)
glossary.leucothoen: Leucothoë — Leucothoe, daughter of Orchamus (Greek f. acc. sg. in -n, the Greek accusative Latin keeps)
glossary.levia: lēvis — smooth, polished (adj., n. nom./acc. pl.; the spelling also allows levis 'light, slight, trivial' — here the threads are smooth)
glossary.libys: Libys — Libys, one of the Tyrrhenian sailors (m. nom. sg., Greek; as a common noun the word means 'a Libyan')
glossary.ligati: ligō, -āre — bound, tied up (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.; also m./n. gen. sg.; not ligō, ligōnis 'mattock')
glossary.ligatis: ligō, -āre — bound, tied (perf. pass. part., dat. or abl. pl. of any gender)

glossary.studio: studium — eagerness, zeal, keen interest (n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.stygiam: Stygius — of the Styx, Stygian, of the underworld (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.styx: Styx — the Styx, the river of the underworld (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.suas: suus — his, her, its, their own (reflexive possessive, f. acc. pl.; it points back to the subject of its clause, not to the nearest noun)
glossary.subibat: subeō — come up, draw on, steal up; undergo (3 sg. imperf.)
glossary.subiectatque: subiectō — thrust up from below, push under (3 sg. pres., frequentative of subiciō, + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.sublimemque: sublīmis — high, aloft, lifted on high (m./f. acc. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; often best rendered adverbially, 'up on high')
glossary.sublimes: sublīmis — high, lofty, exalted (m. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.sufficiunt: sufficiō — suffice, be enough; supply (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.sume: sūmō — take, take up, pick up (2 sg. imperative)
glossary.summis: summus — highest, topmost; the top or surface of (superl. of superus, f. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
glossary.sumptumque: sūmō — take, take up, put on (perf. pass. part. sūmptus, m. acc. sg.: 'taken up, that she had put on', + enclitic -que 'and'); a separate noun sūmptus, -ūs means 'expense'
glossary.surrexere: surgō — rise, stand up (3 pl. perf. = surrēxērunt)
glossary.sustinuere: sustineō — hold up, support, sustain (3 pl. perf. = sustinuērunt)
glossary.taceo: taceō — be silent; pass over in silence, say nothing of (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.tactis: tangō — touch (perf. pass. part. tāctus, f. abl. pl.: 'touched'; also dat. pl.)
glossary.tactosque: tangō — touch (perf. pass. part. tāctus, m. acc. pl.: 'touched', + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.tacuit: taceō — be silent, fall silent, stop speaking (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.taeda: taeda — pine torch; the wedding torch, hence marriage (f. abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)
glossary.taloque: tālus — ankle, heel (m. abl. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; with tenus, 'as far as the ankle')
glossary.tantale: Tantalus — Tantalus, punished in the underworld by water and fruit that flee him (voc. sg.)
glossary.tardata: tardō — slow, delay, hold back, check (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.: 'held back, checked'; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.taxo: taxus — the yew tree, a tree of death and mourning (f. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.tectas: tegō — cover, shelter, screen (perf. pass. part. tēctus, f. acc. pl.: 'sheltered, covered over')
glossary.tectoque: tēctum — roof; house, dwelling (n. abl. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; also dat. sg.); properly the perf. part. of tegō used as a noun, 'the covered thing'
glossary.tecumque: tēcum — with you (= cum tē, the preposition suffixed to the pronoun, + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.tegat: tegō — cover, encase, hide (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.telae: tēla — web, warp; the loom itself (f. gen. sg.; also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.temperie: temperiēs — mildness, moderate warmth, an agreeable temperature (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.temptatos: temptō — try, attempt; test, feel for (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.: 'attempted, tried, put to use')
glossary.tempusque: tempus — time; a season, the right moment (n. nom. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; also acc. sg.); a separate tempus, -oris means 'the temple of the head'
glossary.tenaci: tenāx — gripping, clinging, holding fast (abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.tendens: tendō — stretch out, hold out, extend (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.tendentem: tendō — stretch out, hold out, extend (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.tendite: tendō — stretch, spread, set (a net) (2 pl. imperative)
glossary.tenditur: tendō — stretch, extend (3 sg. pres. pass.: 'is stretched out'; often middle, 'stretches himself out')
glossary.tenebo: teneō — hold, hold fast; keep hold of (an audience) (1 sg. fut.)
glossary.tenero: tener — tender, soft, delicate; young (m./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.tenuantur: tenuō — make thin, taper, draw out fine (3 pl. pres. pass.: 'are drawn thin, taper away')
glossary.tenuique: tenuis — thin, fine, slender (abl. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; also dat. sg.)
glossary.tereti: teres — rounded and smooth, tapering (abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.terretur: terreō — frighten, terrify (3 sg. pres. pass.: 'is terrified')
glossary.tetenderat: tendō — stretch out, hold out (3 sg. pluperf., reduplicated: 'had stretched out')
glossary.thalamumque: thalamus — bedchamber; the marriage bed, hence marriage (m. acc. sg., + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.thaumantias: Thaumantias — daughter of Thaumas, i.e. Iris the rainbow-goddess (patronymic, f. nom. sg.)
glossary.tincto: tingō — dip, dye, stain (perf. pass. part. tīnctus, m./n. dat. sg.; also abl. sg.: 'dyed, stained')
glossary.tinnulaque: tinnulus — ringing, tinkling, shrill (n. nom./acc. pl., + enclitic -que 'and'; also f. nom. sg.)
glossary.tinxit: tingō — dip, steep, dye, taint (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.tisiphone: Tīsiphonē — Tisiphone, one of the three Furies (f. nom. sg.); the name means 'avenger of murder'
glossary.tityos: Tityos — Tityos, the giant stretched over nine acres in the underworld while his liver is torn (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.tortoque: torqueō — twist, coil, whirl (perf. pass. part. tortus, m./n. abl. sg.: 'twisted, coiled', + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.torva: torvus — grim, fierce, savage (especially of a look) (f. abl. sg.; also f. nom. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.trado: trādō — hand over, give up, surrender (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.traiectus: trāiciō — pierce through, transfix; carry across (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.: 'run through, transfixed'); a separate noun trāiectus, -ūs means 'a crossing'
glossary.translucet: trānslūceō — shine through, show through, be visible through (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.tremuisse: tremō — tremble, quiver, shake (perf. act. inf.: 'to have trembled')
glossary.trepidoque: trepidus — trembling, agitated, panic-stricken (m./n. abl. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; also dat. sg.)
glossary.tria: trēs (n. tria) — three (n. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.triplices: triplex — threefold, triple; (of a group) three (m./f. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.trita: terō — rub, grind, wear away (perf. pass. part. trītus, n. nom./acc. pl.: 'ground up, pounded'; also f. nom. sg.)
glossary.truncos: truncus — tree trunk, bole; trunk of the body (m. acc. pl.); also an adj. truncus 'maimed, lopped off'
glossary.turbamve: turba — crowd, throng, mob (f. acc. sg., + enclitic -ve 'or')
glossary.turbata: turbō (-āre) — throw into confusion, disorder, dishevel (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; here middle with acc. of respect, turbāta capillōs, 'her hair in disarray'; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.ubera: ūber — breast, teat, udder (n. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.); a separate adj. ūber means 'fertile, rich'
glossary.ululare: ululō — howl, shriek, wail (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.ulvae: ulva — sedge, marsh grass (f. nom. pl.; also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.umbraeque: umbra — shadow, shade; the shade or ghost of a dead person (f. nom. pl., + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.urbs: urbs — city, walled town (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.urges: urgeō — press, push hard, shove; press on with (2 sg. pres.)
glossary.urget: urgeō — press, push hard; press on with, drive forward (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.urit: ūrō — burn, scorch, consume with fire (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.utve: ut — as, just as; how (here + enclitic -ve 'or': utve, 'or as, or just as')
glossary.vacuis: vacuus — empty, unoccupied, deserted (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
glossary.vagos: vagus — wandering, roaming, straying (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.valeat: valeō — be strong, be able, have power (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.valuere: valeō — be strong, be able, have the strength (3 pl. perf. = valuērunt)
glossary.variari: variō — vary, mottle, fleck with different colours (pres. pass. inf.: 'to be flecked, to be mottled')
glossary.venatibus: vēnātus — hunting, the chase (m. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
glossary.verendam: vereor — fear; revere, hold in awe (gerundive verendus, f. acc. sg.: 'to be revered, awe-inspiring')
glossary.vergit: vergō — pour, tip (something) into; intrans. slope, incline (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.versata: versō — turn about, keep turning, stir (perf. pass. part. versātus, f. nom. sg. or abl. sg.: 'stirred, having stirred'; frequentative of vertō)
glossary.verso: vertō — turn, turn round (perf. pass. part. versus, m./n. abl. sg.: 'turned'; also dat. sg., and 1 sg. pres. of versō 'I keep turning')
glossary.versum: vertō — turn, change, transform (perf. pass. part. versus, m. acc. sg.: 'changed into'; also n. nom./acc. sg.); a separate versus, -ūs means 'a line of verse'
glossary.vertere: vertō — turn, change, transform; overturn (pres. act. inf.; also 3 pl. perf. vertēre = vertērunt)
glossary.vertitis: vertō — turn, change, transform (2 pl. pres.)
glossary.vespere: vesper — evening; the evening star (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.vestro: vester — your, yours (of two or more people; m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.veterem: vetus — old, former, of long standing (m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.viaeque: via — road, way, path; a journey (f. gen. sg., + enclitic -que 'and'; also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.vicimus: vincō — conquer, win, prevail (1 pl. perf.: 'we have won'; often a poetic plural for 'I have won')
glossary.victrix: victrīx — a woman victorious, conqueress; as adj., victorious (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.vindicat: vindicō — claim as one's own; avenge, punish (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.vipereis: vīpereus — of a viper, snaky, made of snakes (m./n. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
glossary.virentibus: vireō — be green, be verdant, flourish (pres. act. part., f. abl. pl.: 'green, growing green'; also dat. pl.)
glossary.virescere: virēscō — grow green, turn green, put out leaves (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.virili: virīlis — of a man, male, manly (abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.visumque: videō — see (perf. pass. part. vīsus, m. acc. sg.: 'him once seen, the one he saw', + enclitic -que 'and'); a separate noun vīsum, -ī means 'a sight, an apparition'
glossary.vitant: vītō — shun, avoid, keep clear of (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.vites: vītis — vine, grapevine (f. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.); identical in form to vītēs, 2 sg. pres. subj. of vītō 'avoid'
glossary.vitro: vitrum — glass (n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.vocatur: vocō — call, name, summon (3 sg. pres. pass.: 'is called')
glossary.volant: volō (-āre) — fly (3 pl. pres.); not volō, velle 'wish'
glossary.volentem: volō (velle) — wish, want, be willing (pres. act. part. volēns, m./f. acc. sg.: 'wanting to, willing'); not volō, -āre 'fly'
glossary.vomunt: vomō — spew out, vomit forth, belch (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.vulgatos: vulgō — spread abroad, make widely known, publish (perf. pass. part. vulgātus, m. acc. pl.: 'widely told, common knowledge'); of a story, 'well-known', not 'vulgar'
glossary.abantiades: Abantiadēs — the descendant of Abas, i.e. Perseus (m. nom. sg.; patronymic, nom. in all five places)
glossary.abarin: Abaris — Abaris, a fighter from the Caucasus (m. acc. sg., Greek form)
glossary.abas: Abās — Abas, a warrior in Phineus' band (m. nom. sg.; not Perseus' ancestor Abas here)
glossary.abdidit: abdō — he buried, sank (it) (3 sg. perf.; the sword driven into the sea-beast)
glossary.aberat: absum — was distant, was away (3 sg. impf., with 'tantum ... quantum')
glossary.ablatus: auferō — carried off, swept away, taken away (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; with 'est', Perseus was swept; also without a copula, and in 'sibi ablatus', carried away from his own self).
glossary.absit: absum — may he be far off (3 sg. pres. subj., wish/curse: let Jupiter keep his distance from you)
glossary.abstrahor: abstrahō — I am dragged in, forced to take sides (1 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.abstuleris: auferō — you carried off (2 sg. perf. subj. in an indirect question: by what arts you took the snake-haired head)
glossary.accingitur: accingō — he girds himself, arms himself (+ abl.) (3 sg. pres. pass. used reflexively, middle sense)
glossary.accipiunt: accipiō — they accept (3 pl. pres.; the parents accept the terms)
glossary.acclinavit: acclīnō — leaned (3 sg. perf.; with 'se': leaned himself against him)
glossary.acerbo: acerbus — bitter, cruel (n. abl. sg. with 'vulnere')
glossary.acervos: acervus — heaps, piles (m. acc. pl.; of the dying in 88, of incense in 131)
glossary.aconteus: Acontēus — Aconteus, a soldier on Perseus' side (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.acrisioneas: Acrīsiōnēus — of Acrisius, Acrisian (f. acc. pl. with 'arces': the citadel of Argos)
glossary.acrisioniades: Acrīsiōniadēs — the descendant of Acrisius, i.e. Perseus (m. nom. sg.; patronymic)
glossary.acrisium: Acrīsius — Acrisius, king of Argos and Perseus' grandfather (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.acrisius: Acrīsius — Acrisius, king of Argos and Perseus' grandfather (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.actoriden: Actoridēs — the son of Actor, i.e. Erytus (m. acc. sg., Greek form; patronymic)
glossary.acutis: acūtus — shrill, high-pitched (m. abl. pl. with 'tinnitibus', not with 'ensis')
glossary.adactus: adigō — driven home (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., of the weapon driven into Phorbas' throat)
glossary.adapertaque: adaperiō + -que — opened wide (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. with 'ora' + enclitic)
glossary.adgreditur: adgredior — he attacks, goes at (3 sg. pres., deponent)
glossary.adhaerent: adhaereō — they cling (3 pl. pres.; the parents cling to Andromeda's bound body)
glossary.adhibendus: adhibeō — to be put to, employed for (gerundive, m. nom. sg. agreeing with 'tu', of Lampetides)
glossary.adigitque: adigō + -que — and he drives (it) home (3 sg. pres. + enclitic)
glossary.admonitorque: admonitor + -que — prompter, reminder (+ gen.) (m. nom. sg. + enclitic; Lucifer, who calls men to their work)
glossary.adpellare: adpellō (appellō) — to address, speak to (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.adsimilare: adsimilō (assimulō) — to liken, compare (+ dat.) (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.adspergit: adspergō (aspergō) — he spatters, sprinkles (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.adspexisse: adspiciō (aspiciō) — to have looked at (perf. act. inf., in indirect statement after 'narrat')
glossary.adstantem: adstō (astō) — standing by, standing near (pres. part., m. acc. sg., of Lampetides)
glossary.adsum: adsum — I am here (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.adversaque: adversus + -que — facing, opposing (n. acc. pl. with 'agmina' + enclitic)
glossary.aegide: aegis — with the aegis, Minerva's goatskin shield (f. abl. sg., Greek noun)
glossary.aerias: āerius — of the upper air, airy (f. acc. pl. with 'auras')
glossary.aethionque: Aethīōn + -que — Aethion, a seer in Phineus' band (m. nom. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.agnoscitque: agnōscō + -que — and he recognizes (3 sg. pres. + enclitic)
glossary.agnosse: agnōscō — to have acknowledged, recognized (perf. act. inf., contracted from agnōvisse)
glossary.agyrtes: Agyrtēs — Agyrtes, notorious for killing his own father (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.albenti: albeō — white, gleaming white (pres. part., f. abl. sg. with 'vitta')
glossary.alipedi: ālipēs — to the wing-footed one, i.e. Mercury (m. dat. sg., used as a noun)
glossary.alium: alius — another man, someone else (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.altaria: altāria — altar, altar-top (n. acc. pl.; plural in form but used of one altar; after 'post' in 36, object of 'amplexo' in 103)
glossary.alternis: alternus — alternating, one after another (m. abl. pl. with 'crinibus')
glossary.alterno: alternus — by turns, alternately (n. abl. sg. used adverbially with 'spectans': looking now at one, now at the other)
glossary.ambas: ambō — both (f. acc. pl. with 'partes': it juts out on both sides)
glossary.amicus: amīcus — friend (m. nom. sg.; 'siquis amicus adest')
glossary.ammon: Ammōn — Ammon: in IV.671 and V.17 the horned Libyan oracle-god; in V.107 a boxer of that name, Broteas' twin (m. nom. sg. in all three)
glossary.amphimedon: Amphimedōn — Amphimedon, a Libyan in Phineus' band (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.amplexo: amplector — having embraced, clasping (perf. part. of the deponent, act. in sense; m. dat. sg. with 'huic')
glossary.ampycus: Ampycus — Ampycus, the priest of Ceres (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.ampyx: Ampyx — Ampyx, a fighter on Phineus' side (m. nom. sg.; a different man from Ampycus)
glossary.andromedan: Andromedē — Andromeda, daughter of Cepheus and Cassiope (f. acc. sg., Greek form)
glossary.anguiferumque: anguifer + -que — snake-bearing (n. acc. sg. with 'caput' + enclitic)
glossary.anhelis: anhēlus — panting, breathless (m. abl. pl. with 'equis', the Sun's team)
glossary.animavit: animō — brought to life, quickened (3 sg. perf.; the earth turned the drops into snakes)
glossary.animumque: animus + -que — spirit, character (m. acc. sg. + enclitic; object of 'quaerit')
glossary.applicat: applicō — he sets against, puts up against (3 sg. pres.; his shoulders to the column)
glossary.apri: aper — of a boar (m. gen. sg. with 'ferocis', in 'more ferocis apri': like a wild boar)
glossary.aquosae: aquōsus — rain-laden, watery (f. gen. sg. with 'nubis')
glossary.ara: āra — altar (f. nom. sg. in V.755 and V.37; f. abl. sg. after 'in' in V.57)
glossary.arboreae: arboreus — of the trees, tree- (f. nom. pl. with 'frondes')
glossary.arceat: arceō — to bar, keep out (3 sg. pres. subj. in a relative clause of purpose)
glossary.arcebatque: arceō + -que — and he kept out, shut off (3 sg. impf. + enclitic)
glossary.ardescit: ardēscō — blazes up, catches fire (3 sg. pres.; the crowd flames into rage)
glossary.argento: argentum — with silver (n. abl. sg., paired with 'auro')
glossary.arguis: arguō — you allege, charge (2 sg. pres.)
glossary.argumenta: argūmentum — proofs, tokens, signs (n. nom. pl., in apposition to the pipes and singing)
glossary.armataque: armō + -que — armed (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. with 'imago' + enclitic)
glossary.armentorum: armentum — of the herds, of the cattle (n. gen. pl.)
glossary.armorum: arma — of arms, of weapons (n. gen. pl.; the noun exists only in the plural)
glossary.arripit: arripiō — he snatches up (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.assyrius: Assyrius — Assyrian (m. nom. sg., of Lycabas)
glossary.astreus: Astreus — Astreus, one of those killed in the fray (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.astu: astus — by cunning, by craft (m. abl. sg., with 'sollerti')
glossary.astyages: Astyagēs — Astyages, one of Phineus' men (m. nom. sg. in both places)
glossary.athin: Athis — Athis, the young Indian (m. acc. sg., Greek form)
glossary.athis: Athis — Athis, the young Indian (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.atla: Atlās — Atlas (m. voc. sg., Greek form; Perseus addressing him)
glossary.atlante: Atlās — Atlas, here the mountain (m. abl. sg. after 'sub')
glossary.atra: āter — black, dark (f. abl. sg. with 'nocte')
glossary.auctus: augeō — enlarged, swollen (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., of Atlas grown huge)
glossary.audenti: audeō — daring, venturing (pres. part., m. dat. sg., of Phineus, who dares not look back)
glossary.auditis: audiō — heard (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl. with 'mugitibus' in an ablative absolute)
glossary.augebat: augeō — was adding to, was heightening (3 sg. impf.)
glossary.aurata: aurātus — gilded, golden (n. nom. pl. with 'monilia')
glossary.ave: avis — by a bird, i.e. a bird-omen (f. abl. sg. with 'falsa': the augur misled by a false sign)
glossary.aversa: āvertō — turned away (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. with 'est': Minerva turned her face away)
glossary.aversum: āvertō — turned away, facing the other way (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg., of the beast taken from behind)
glossary.avertite: āvertō — turn away! (2 pl. pres. imperative, with 'vultus')
glossary.avertitur: āvertō — he turns away (3 sg. pres. pass. used reflexively, middle sense)
glossary.avidi: avidus — eager (+ inf.) (m. nom. pl., of Amphimedon and his companion)
glossary.avidos: avidus — greedy, ravenous (m. acc. pl.; with 'ungues' in 717, with 'morsus' in 724)
glossary.bactrius: Bactrius — Bactrian (m. nom. sg., of Halcyoneus)
glossary.bellare: bellō — to make war, to fight (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.bellona: Bellōna — Bellona, goddess of war (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.belua: bēlua — beast, sea-monster (f. nom. sg. in all three places)
glossary.bibulaque: bibulus + -que — thirsty, sap-drinking (f. abl. sg. with 'medulla' + enclitic)
glossary.bibulis: bibulus — water-logged, soaked through (n. abl. pl. with 'talaribus')
glossary.broteasque: Brotēās + -que — Broteas, one of the twin boxer brothers (m. nom. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.cadente: cadō — falling, sinking (pres. part., m. abl. sg. with 'die' in an ablative absolute: as the day sank)
glossary.cadentum: cadō — of those falling, of the dying (pres. part. as noun, m. gen. pl. in -um for -ium)
glossary.caelaverat: caelō — had engraved, had chased (3 sg. pluperf.)
glossary.caestibus: caestus — with boxing-gloves, the cestus (m. abl. pl.)
glossary.calcitrat: calcitrō — he kicks out, thrashes his heels (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.calido: calidus — warm, still hot (n. abl. sg. with 'vulnere')
glossary.canat: canō — to sing with (3 sg. pres. subj. in a relative clause of characteristic: not a shout for singing)
glossary.cancri: Cancer — of the Crab, Cancer (m. gen. sg.; the constellation, standing for the south)
glossary.cane: canō — sing! (2 sg. pres. imperative: sing the rest to the Stygian shades)
glossary.cantus: cantus — singing, song (m. nom., 4th decl.; subject with 'tibia' of 'sonant')
glossary.capiant: capiō — should take on, receive (3 pl. pres. subj. in a result clause with 'ut')

glossary.chaonius: Chāonius — Chaonian, of Chaonia in Epirus (m. nom. sg., of Molpeus)

glossary.claninque: Clanis + -que — Clanis, a fighter (m. acc. sg., Greek form, + enclitic)
glossary.clanis: Clanis — Clanis, a fighter (m. nom. sg.)

glossary.clarissimus: clārus — brightest (superl., m. nom. sg., of Lucifer the morning star)

glossary.clytii: Clytius — of Clytius (m. gen. sg., with 'lacerto': through both of Clytius' arms)
glossary.clytiumque: Clytius + -que — Clytius, one of those killed (m. acc. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.clytumque: Clytus — Clytus, one of those cut down (m. acc. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.cogitis: cōgō — you force, you compel (2 pl. pres.)
glossary.colubrasque: colubra — snakes (f. acc. pl. + enclitic; the serpents of Medusa's hair)
glossary.colubris: colubra — with snakes (f. abl. pl., with 'infesta')
glossary.columnae: columna — of the column, of the pillar (f. gen. sg. in both places)
glossary.comaeque: coma + -que — hair, locks (f. nom. pl. + enclitic)

glossary.committere: committō — to join, to engage in (pres. act. inf., with 'pugnam')
glossary.complentur: compleō — are filled (3 pl. pres. pass.)
glossary.concede: concēdō — grant! give up! (2 sg. pres. imperative)

glossary.conclamat: conclāmō — she cries out (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.concrevit: concrēscō — hardened, stiffened, congealed (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.concurrere: concurrō — to close with, to fight hand to hand (pres. act. inf.)

glossary.confudit: cōnfundō — smashed together, crushed (3 sg. perf.; the face broken into the shattered bones)
glossary.coniugialia: coniugiālis — of marriage, wedding- (n. nom. pl. with 'festa')
glossary.coniurata: coniūrō — sworn together, banded in conspiracy (perf. part., n. nom. pl. with 'agmina')
glossary.conlapsus: conlābor (collābor) — having collapsed, sinking down (perf. part. of the deponent, act. in sense; m. nom. sg.)
glossary.conspecta: cōnspiciō — caught sight of (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg. with 'Gorgone' in an ablative absolute)
glossary.conspectior: cōnspicuus — more striking, more remarkable (compar., f. nom. sg. with 'ulla')
glossary.contentusque: contentus + -que — content, satisfied (+ abl.) (m. nom. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.contortam: contorqueō — whirled, hurled with a twist (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg. with 'hastam')
glossary.corniger: corniger — horn-bearing, horned (m. nom. sg., of Ammon)
glossary.correptus: corripiō — seized, caught up (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; Perseus seized by the sight of her)
glossary.corruit: corruō — he collapsed, fell in a heap (3 sg.; present and perfect are alike in spelling, perfect here)
glossary.corythi: Corythus — of Corythus, a Marmarid (m. gen. sg., with 'cuspide')
glossary.costis: costa — into the ribs (f. dat. pl. of the goal with 'adactus', parallel to 'iugulo'; the form is also abl.)
glossary.cratera: crātēr — mixing-bowl, wine-bowl (m. acc. sg., Greek form)
glossary.credensque: crēdō + -que — believing, trusting (pres. part., m. nom. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.cretum: crēscō — sprung from, descended (+ abl.) (perf. part., m. acc. sg. with 'Polydegmona')

glossary.cruris: crūs — of the leg (n. gen. sg. with 'traiecti'; not nom. pl.)
glossary.cultor: cultor — devotee, one who honours (+ gen.) (m. nom. sg.; 'aequi cultor': a lover of fair dealing)
glossary.cultu: cultus — in dress, in adornment (m. abl. sg., with 'divite')
glossary.cultusque: cultus + -que — ways of life, customs (m. acc. pl. + enclitic; object of 'quaerit')
glossary.cunctantem: cūnctor — lingering, hanging back (pres. part. of the deponent, m. acc. sg., of Perseus)

glossary.cupidi: cupidus — desiring, in love (m. nom. pl. with 'amantes')
glossary.curaliis: cūrālium (corālium) — for corals (n. dat. pl.; the coral keeps the same nature)
glossary.curvo: curvus — curved, hooked (m. abl. sg. with 'hamo')
glossary.cuspidis: cuspis — of the point, of the spearhead (f. gen. sg. with 'aeratae'; not nom. pl.)
glossary.cyllenide: Cyllēnis — Cyllenian, Mercury's (f. abl. sg. with 'harpe'; Mercury was born on Mt Cyllene)
glossary.dabimus: dō — we shall give (1 pl. fut.)
glossary.dabo: dō — I shall give (1 sg. fut.)
glossary.danae: Danaē — Danaë, Perseus' mother (f. nom. sg., Greek form)
glossary.danaeius: Danaēius — Danaë's, son of Danaë (m. nom. sg. with 'heros': Perseus)
glossary.debellata: dēbellō — conquered, subdued (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. with 'India')

glossary.decutit: dēcutiō — he strikes off (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.defectos: dēficiō — drained, failing (+ abl.) (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl. with 'artus')
glossary.dependent: dēpendeō — they hang down (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.deploravit: dēplōrō — wept for, bewailed (3 sg. perf.)

glossary.despectat: dēspectō — looks down on (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.detrectas: dētrectō — you disparage, you refuse to allow (2 sg. pres.)

glossary.devovet: dēvoveō — he curses, calls down curses on (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.dextroque: dexter + -que — right (m. abl. sg. with 'armo' + enclitic)
glossary.diffudere: diffundō — they unbent, relaxed (3 pl. perf. in -ēre for -ērunt; not an infinitive)
glossary.dimotis: dīmoveō — parted, thrust aside (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl. with 'undis' in an ablative absolute)
glossary.discordibus: discors — conflicting, warring (m. abl. pl. with 'ventis')
glossary.dissiluit: dissiliō — flew apart, shattered (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.dissimulator: dissimulātor — concealer, one who hides (+ gen.) (m. nom. sg.; no concealer of true love)
glossary.distantia: distō — things far off, distant targets (pres. part. as noun, n. acc. pl.)
glossary.ditissimus: dīves — richest (+ gen.) (superl., m. nom. sg.; 'ditissimus agri')
glossary.diurnos: diurnus — of the daytime, day- (m. acc. pl. with 'currus')
glossary.divite: dīves — rich, costly (m. abl. sg. with 'cultu')
glossary.doctus: doceō — taught, skilled (+ inf.) (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; 'doctus figere': skilled at hitting)
glossary.dolebis: doleō — you will grieve, you will resent it (2 sg. fut.)
glossary.dominique: dominus + -que — of its owner, of its master (m. gen. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.dorylas: Dorylās — Dorylas, a rich Nasamonian (m. nom. sg. in both places)
glossary.dotale: dōtālis — given as a dowry (n. acc. sg. with 'regnum')
glossary.dote: dōs — with this dowry, as this return (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.dotibus: dōs — with gifts, endowments (f. abl. pl.; the dowry Perseus offers for Andromeda)
glossary.draconi: dracō — to a dragon, serpent (m. dat. sg.)
glossary.draconibus: dracō — with serpents (m. abl. pl., with 'crinita')
glossary.dubitaret: dubitō — would have hesitated (3 sg. impf. subj., potential, in a rhetorical question)
glossary.dubius: dubius — uncertain, in two minds (m. nom. sg., of Perseus)
glossary.dura: dūrus — hard, rough (f. nom. sg. with 'harena', subject of 'laedat')
glossary.durus: dūrus — hard-hearted, unrelenting (m. nom. sg., of Phineus)
glossary.echemmon: Echemmōn — Echemmon, a Nabataean fighter (m. nom. sg. in both places)
glossary.edita: ēdō — brought forth, born (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., with 'est'; of a child brought into the world by whatever parent — with 'Limnaee', born of the Ganges, and 'nostro est edita partu', she was brought forth by my own labour).

glossary.egregius: ēgregius — outstanding, remarkable (+ abl. of respect) (m. nom. sg.; 'egregius forma')

glossary.equis: equus — to the horses (m. dat. pl.; the Sun's team)

glossary.eripiet: ēripiō — will snatch away, will rescue (3 sg. fut.)

glossary.eumque: is + -que — and him (m. acc. sg. + enclitic)

glossary.exasperat: exasperō — roughens, whips up (3 sg. pres.)

glossary.exemplo: exemplum — after the manner of, like (+ gen.) (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.exerces: exerceō — you keep up, you ply (2 sg. pres.; 'exerces odium')
glossary.exhalantem: exhālō — breathing out, ebbing away (pres. part., f. acc. sg. with 'vitam')
glossary.exhausto: exhauriō — than what has been used up (perf. pass. part., n. abl. sg. of comparison after 'plus')

glossary.exiguamque: exiguus + -que — scanty, brief (f. acc. sg. with 'requiem' + enclitic)
glossary.expellere: expellō — to drive out, to expel (pres. act. inf.)

glossary.fatale: fātālis — deadly, fate-bearing (n. acc. sg. with 'iaculum')

glossary.fortissime: fortis — bravest! (superlative, m. voc. sg. in the address 'o fortissime'; not the adverb 'fortissimē')
glossary.fractis: frangō — broken, shattered (perf. part., n. abl. pl. with 'ossibus')

glossary.fratrem: frāter — brother (m. acc. sg.; once of Perseus, whom his half-sister Pallas shields, once of Chrysaor, Pegasus' brother born from Medusa's blood)

glossary.frementis: fremō — roaring, snorting (pres. part., f. gen. sg. with 'ferae': in the right shoulder of the roaring beast; not acc. pl.)

glossary.freto: fretum — strait, sea (n. dat. sg. with 'adsimilare': you might liken the uproar to a sea)
glossary.fugacem: fugāx — swift-flying, fleet (m. acc. sg. with 'Pegason': swift-winged Pegasus)

glossary.fumabat: fūmō — was smoking, smouldering (3 sg. impf.; the brand set in the middle of the altar)

glossary.furentem: furō — raging, out of his mind (pres. part., m. acc. sg. with 'te': Cepheus to the raving Phineus)
glossary.gange: Gangēs — the Ganges, the great river of India (m. abl. sg. in the form 'Gange')
glossary.gaudent: gaudeō — they rejoice, they delight (to do) (3 pl. pres.; once absolutely, once governing the infinitive 'contingere')
