glossary.gener: gener — son-in-law (m. nom. sg., predicative: I should surely be preferred to all as a son-in-law)
glossary.generosi: generōsus — noble, of noble stock or vintage (m. gen. sg. with 'Bacchi': the gift of the noble wine-god)
glossary.generumque: gener + -que — and (as) son-in-law (m. acc. sg. + enclitic: they hail Perseus as their daughter's husband)
glossary.genetrice: genetrīx — mother (f. abl. sg. with 'cum': Andromeda together with her mother Cassiope)
glossary.genitore: genitor — father, begetter (m. abl. sg.; once ablative of origin, 'dubio genitore creatus', once in an abl. abs., 'caeso genitore': his father having been killed)
glossary.gentibus: gēns — nation, people (f. abl. pl. in an abl. abs. with 'relictis': countless peoples left behind below him)
glossary.genusque: genus + -que — and race, lineage; and kind, character (n. acc. sg. + enclitic; of Bacchus' descent from Jove, and of the character of the lands Perseus describes)
glossary.geras: gerō — you wear, you bear (2 sg. pres. subj. in an indirect question: why you wear these chains)
glossary.germane: germānus — brother! (m. voc. sg.; Cepheus addressing his brother Phineus)
glossary.gesserit: gerō — she wore, came to bear (3 sg. perf. subj. in an indirect question: why she alone wore snakes twined in her hair)
glossary.gladio: gladius — sword (m. abl. sg. of instrument: he aims at Lyncides' breast with the sword)
glossary.gorgone: Gorgō — the Gorgon, Medusa (f. abl. sg. in an abl. abs., 'Gorgone conspecta' / 'Gorgone visa': at the sight of the Gorgon)
glossary.gorgoneas: Gorgoneus — of the Gorgons (adj., f. acc. pl. with 'domos': the dwelling of the Gorgons)
glossary.gorgonei: Gorgoneus — of the Gorgon (adj., n. gen. sg. with 'capitis': drops from Medusa's severed head)
glossary.gorgoneis: Gorgoneus — of the Gorgon (adj., f. abl. pl. with 'viribus': you are numb by a fault of spirit, not by any Gorgon power)
glossary.gorgoneum: Gorgoneus — the Gorgon's, Medusa's (adj., m. acc. sg. with 'crinem': turned her hair into foul water-snakes)
glossary.gorgonis: Gorgō — of the Gorgon, Medusa (f. gen. sg.: conqueror of the snake-haired Gorgon; he lifted the Gorgon's face)
glossary.grandaevus: grandaevus — of great age, aged (m. nom. sg.; of the old man among the banqueters)
glossary.grandine: grandō — hail (f. abl. sg., ablative of comparison with 'plura': thicker than winter hail)
glossary.habebit: habeō — will have, will win (3 sg. fut.: a son of Jove shall carry off this prize)
glossary.habes: habeō — you have, you get (2 sg. pres., with the partitive genitives 'invidiae ... laudis': you win more envy than praise)
glossary.habeto: habeō — have it! keep it! (2 sg. future imperative: keep the plot of ground you are pressing)
glossary.habitasse: habitō — to have dwelt (perf. act. inf., syncopated for 'habitavisse', in indirect statement: that the twin sisters lived there)
glossary.haerenti: haereō — to him as he stuck fast (pres. part., m. dat. sg., dative of disadvantage: Abas gashed the side of the man held there)
glossary.halcyoneus: Halcyoneus — Halcyoneus, a Bactrian in Phineus' band (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.hamato: hāmātus — hooked, curved (m. abl. sg. with 'ense': Perseus' hooked blade, the harpe)
glossary.hamo: hāmus — hook, barb (m. abl. sg. governed by the postposed 'tenus': buried the iron up to the curved hook)
glossary.harpe: harpē — curved sword, sickle-blade (f. abl. sg.; a Greek loanword — the Cyllenian harpe of Mercury)
glossary.harpen: harpē — the curved sword, sickle-blade (f. acc. sg. in the Greek form '-ēn')
glossary.hausta: hauriō — drawn (of water) (perf. part., f. abl. sg. with 'unda': he washes his hands in water drawn up)
glossary.helicen: Helix — Helix, one of Phineus' followers (m. acc. sg. in the Greek form '-ēn')
glossary.hiberna: hībernus — wintry, of winter (f. abl. sg. with 'grandine': more numerous than winter hail; not n. pl.)
glossary.hippotades: Hippotadēs — son of Hippotes, i.e. Aeolus, keeper of the winds (m. nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
glossary.hodites: Hoditēs — Hodites, foremost of the Cephenes after the king (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.horrendae: horrendus — dreadful, to be shuddered at (gerundive used as an adjective, f. gen. sg. with 'Medusae': the shape of the horrifying Medusa)
glossary.horrentia: horreō — bristling, shaggy (pres. part., n. acc. pl. with 'saxa': crags bristling with rough woodland)
glossary.hospitiique: hospitium — of hospitality, of the guest-bond (n. gen. sg. + enclitic, with 'deos': the gods of the guest-tie)
glossary.hospitium: hospitium — hospitality, lodging (n. acc. sg., object of 'peto')
glossary.hydros: hydrus — water-snake, serpent (m. acc. pl.; a Greek loanword)
glossary.hymenaeus: Hymenaeus — Hymen, god of the wedding (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.hypsea: Hypseus — Hypseus, one of Phineus' band (m. acc. sg. in the Greek form '-ea')
glossary.hypseus: Hypseus — Hypseus, a fighter on Phineus' side (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.iactantem: iactō — tossing, flinging about (pres. part., m. acc. sg. with 'hunc': Athis tossing his admired face in his blood)
glossary.iapetionides: Iāpetīonidēs — son of Iapetus, i.e. Atlas (m. nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
glossary.idan: Idās — Idas, the bystander whom the stray spear struck (m. acc. sg. in the Greek form '-an')
glossary.imbelle: imbellis — unwarlike, peaceable (n. acc. sg. with 'plectrum': holding the unwarlike quill)
glossary.impugnante: impugnō — assailing, attacking (pres. part., f. abl. sg. with 'causa': for a cause that attacks desert and good faith)
glossary.incessit: incessō — assails, attacks (with words) (3 sg. pres. of the 3rd-conj. 'incesso', beside 'pugnat' and 'devovet'; not the perfect of 'incedo')
glossary.increpat: increpō — rebukes, chides, upbraids (3 sg. pres.; Eryx upbraiding men frozen with fear, Ceres upbraiding the lands — 'terras increpat omnes').
glossary.incurrite: incurrō — charge! rush at him! (2 pl. pres. imperative)
glossary.incursurus: incurrō — about to charge (fut. act. part., m. nom. sg. with 'erat': he was on the point of rushing in)
glossary.india: India — India, the East that Bacchus subdued (f. nom. sg., paired with 'Achaia', which honoured him with founded temples)
glossary.indignum: indignus — shameful! outrageous! (n. nom. sg. in a parenthetical exclamation: the shame of it!)
glossary.indomitas: indomitus — untamed, ungovernable (f. acc. pl. with 'iras': the mob blazes up into unbridled fury)
glossary.indotata: indōtātus — undowered, without a dowry (n. acc. pl. with 'praemia': he carries off the prize dowerless)
glossary.induruit: indūrēscō — hardened, grew stiff (3 sg. perf.; of the seaweed at Medusa's touch, and of the moisture of Phineus' eyes)
glossary.indus: Indus — Indian (m. nom. sg., adjectival with the name Athis)
glossary.indutus: induō — clothed in, wearing (perf. part., m. nom. sg. with a retained accusative 'chlamydem': dressed in a Tyrian cloak)
glossary.inermia: inermis — unarmed, defenceless (n. acc. pl. with 'bracchia' in the next line: stretching out helpless arms)
glossary.ineunt: ineō — they enter upon, sit down to (3 pl. pres.: the Cephenian nobles begin the banquet)
glossary.inexorabile: inexōrābilis — relentless, not to be moved by entreaty (n. acc. sg. with 'odium' in the next line)
glossary.inferior: īnferior — weaker, the lesser (comparative, m. nom. sg. with the abl. 'viribus': Perseus, weaker in strength)
glossary.infestaque: īnfestus — infested, beset (+ abl.) (f. nom. sg. + enclitic, with 'terra': that land is thick and dangerous with snakes)
glossary.infligitque: īnflīgō + -que — and dashes it upon, smashes it into (+ dat.) (3 sg. pres. + enclitic: he brings the bowl down on the man)
glossary.infraque: īnfrā — and below, beneath (adverb + enclitic: peoples left behind round about and below)
glossary.ingentem: ingēns — huge, massive (m. acc. sg. with 'cratera': the great mixing-bowl)
glossary.ingenti: ingēns — huge, vast (n. abl. sg. with 'corpore': surpassing all men in the hugeness of his body)
glossary.inguine: inguen — groin (n. abl. sg.: the blade stood fixed in his groin)
glossary.inimica: inimīcus — hostile, of the enemy (n. acc. pl. with 'pectora' in the next line: would have burst the enemy's breast; not f. nom. sg.)
glossary.iniqua: inīquus — unfair, immoderate (f. abl. sg. with 'ira': there is no limit to your unjust anger; not n. pl.)
glossary.iniusti: iniūstus — unjust (n. gen. sg. with 'belli', governed by impersonal 'paenitet': Phineus repents of the unjust war)
glossary.iniustus: iniūstus — unjust (m. nom. sg. with 'Ammon', predicative: Ammon had unjustly ordered the penalty)
glossary.inlisit: inlīdō (illīdō) — dashed against, drove into (+ dat.) (3 sg. perf.: drove the blade into the bones of the neck)
glossary.inmeritam: immeritus — undeserving, guiltless (f. acc. sg., of Andromeda, accusative subject of 'pendere': paying though she had done no wrong)
glossary.inmeriti: immeritus — undeserving of it, wronged (m. gen. sg. with 'parentis': avenger of the forebear who had not deserved it)
glossary.inmitem: immītis — harsh, merciless (m. acc. sg. with 'Phinea')
glossary.inmixtos: immisceō — mingled in among (+ dat.) (perf. part., m. acc. pl. with 'angues': snakes twined among her locks)
glossary.inmotusque: immōtus — motionless, unmoved (m. nom. sg. + enclitic, predicative with 'mansit': he stayed there unmoving flint)
glossary.inplevere: impleō — they filled (3 pl. perf. in '-ēre' = 'impleverunt'; not the present infinitive)
glossary.inplevit: impleō — filled (3 sg. perf.; Andromeda fills her eyes with rising tears, and Jupiter fills the shut chamber with golden rain)
glossary.inponit: impōnō — lays upon, sets down on (3 sg. pres.: he lays Medusa's head on the strewn leaves)
glossary.inpositus: impōnō — set, placed (perf. part., m. nom. sg. with 'est': one of the two has already been set in the sky)
glossary.inpulsu: impulsus — thrust, drive, impact (m. abl. sg., 4th decl.: the waves parted by the drive of its breast)
glossary.inpune: impūne — unpunished, scot-free (adverb: that this should not go unpunished)
glossary.inridens: inrīdeō (irrīdeō) — mocking, jeering (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.insonuit: īnsonō — resounded, roared (3 sg. perf.: the sea gave a roar)
glossary.instabat: īnstō — was pressing on, bearing down (3 sg. impf.: Molpeus was pressing from the left)
glossary.instantes: īnstō — those pressing on, the attackers (pres. part., m. acc. pl., object of 'sustinet')
glossary.instanti: īnstō — to one pressing her, insisting (pres. part., m. dat. sg.: to Perseus as he asked again and again)
glossary.instructa: īnstruō — furnished, fitted out (perf. part., n. nom. pl. with 'atria': the halls set out with fine array)
glossary.insuper: īnsuper — besides, on top of that (adverb)
glossary.integer: integer — untouched, in unspoilt prime (m. nom. sg., of Athis, still fresh at twice eight years)
glossary.intellege: intellegō — understand! realize! (2 sg. pres. imperative)
glossary.intonsumque: intōnsus — unshorn, long-haired (m. acc. sg. + enclitic, with the accusative of respect 'comas': Helix with uncut hair)
glossary.intorquet: intorqueō — hurls, whirls (a weapon) (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.introitu: introitus — entrance, entryway (m. abl. sg., 4th decl.)
glossary.inveni: inveniō — I found (someone) (1 sg. perf.; Perseus: I found a man who said he had seen it — not the imperative)
glossary.invicti: invictus — unconquered, never beaten (m. nom. pl., of the two boxers Broteas and Ammon)
glossary.invidiosa: invidiōsus — envied, arousing envy (f. nom. sg. with 'spes': she was the much-envied hope of many suitors)
glossary.ipsamque: ipse — and her own self (f. acc. sg. + enclitic, of the Gorgon herself as against her snakes)
glossary.isset: eō — had gone (3 sg. pluperf. subj., syncopated for 'ivisset', in the unreal condition 'nisi ... isset')
glossary.iterant: iterō — they repeat, do it again (3 pl. pres.: the sea-nymphs repeat the trick with more twigs)
glossary.iugulo: iugulum — throat, base of the neck (n. dat. sg. of the goal with 'adactus', parallel to 'costis': driven into Phorbas' throat; not the verb 'iugulō')
glossary.iunctae: iungō — joined, shared (perf. part., f. gen. sg. with 'mortis': the comfort of a death shared; not nom. pl. or dat.)
glossary.iunctissimus: iūnctus — most closely bound, dearest (superlative of the participle of 'iungo', m. nom. sg. with 'Lycabas', + dat. 'illi')
glossary.iusque: iūs — and right, law (n. acc. sg. + enclitic, object of 'testatus': calling law and faith to witness)
glossary.iussus: iubeō — bidden, ordered (perf. part., m. nom. sg., with 'eras' making the pluperf. pass.: you had been told to grace the feast with song)
glossary.iustius: iūstius — with better reason, more justly (comparative adverb of 'iuste'; 'sed iustius illa': but she with better cause)
glossary.laboris: labor — of the toil, of the ordeal (m. gen. sg.: the girl, both the prize and the cause of the labour)
glossary.lacerto: lacertus — upper arm (m. abl. sg. of means with 'librata': the heavy spear balanced by the arm)
glossary.lacrimarum: lacrima — of tears (f. gen. pl. with 'longa [tempora]': long seasons of weeping)
glossary.laedat: laedō — should hurt, bruise (3 sg. pres. subj. in a negative purpose clause: lest the hard sand injure the snaky head)
glossary.laesa: laedō — wounded, hurt (perf. part., f. nom. sg., of the sea-beast struck by a heavy blow)
glossary.laetabere: laetor — you will rejoice (in) (2 sg. fut. of the deponent, in '-re' for '-ris': you will not long enjoy the boy's death)
glossary.laeti: laetus — joyful, glad (m. gen. sg. with 'animi': tokens of a happy mood; not nom. pl.)
glossary.laeva: laeva — the left hand (f. nom. sg., 'laeva [manus]', subject of 'gerebat'; not the ablative here)
glossary.laevane: laeva + -ne — or by the left (f. abl. sg. + the interrogative enclitic '-ne', in the double question 'dextra laevane')
glossary.laevi: laevus — left (m. gen. sg. with 'postis': the timbers of the left doorpost)
glossary.laevo: laevus — left (n. abl. sg. with 'tempore' = temple of the head, not 'time': he fixed the point in the left temple)
glossary.lammina: lammina (lāmina) — blade, thin plate of metal (f. nom. sg.: the sword-blade shatters)
glossary.lampetide: Lampetidēs — Lampetides, the singer at the wedding feast (m. voc. sg. of the Greek name)
glossary.lapsi: lābor — having slipped, having fallen (perf. part. of the deponent, m. nom. pl.; not the gen. sg.)
glossary.largis: largus — abundant, lavish (m. abl. pl. with 'odoribus': the fires are glutted with rich incense)
glossary.lata: lātus — broad, wide (the adjective, f. nom. sg. with 'bipennis': whose weapon was a broad two-headed axe; not the participle of 'fero')
glossary.laterum: latus — of the flanks, sides (n. gen. pl. of 'latus, lateris', with 'costas': the ribs of its sides)
glossary.laudatos: laudō — praised, admired (perf. part., m. acc. pl. with 'vultus': the features everyone had praised)
glossary.laudem: laus — praise, glory (f. acc. sg., object of 'detrectas'; the noun, not a form of 'laudo')
glossary.laudis: laus — of praise (f. gen. sg., partitive with 'plus ... quam': more envy than praise)
glossary.lenta: lentus — pliant, springy (n. acc. pl. with 'cornua': bending the supple horns of the bow; not f. nom. sg.)
glossary.letifer: lētifer — death-bringing, deadly (m. nom. sg. with 'locus': that spot was fatal)
glossary.levabere: levō — you will be relieved, lightened (2 sg. fut. pass. in '-re' for '-ris': you will find relief in our grief)
glossary.libycas: Libycus — Libyan, African (f. acc. pl. with 'harenas': the sands of Libya)
glossary.lignoque: lignum — wood, the wooden shaft (n. abl. sg. + enclitic, with 'cohaesit': point and shaft stuck fast together)
glossary.limnaee: Limnaeē — Limnaee, nymph daughter of the Ganges and mother of Athis (f. nom. sg. of the Greek name in '-ē'; subject of 'peperisse')
glossary.liventia: līveō — livid, blue-black (pres. part., n. acc. pl. with 'terga': the serpent's bluish back)
glossary.longi: longus — long (m. gen. sg. with 'cursus': the perils of his long journey; not nom. pl.)
glossary.luctuque: lūctus — grief, mourning (m. abl. sg., 4th decl., + enclitic: relieved by our sorrow)
glossary.lycetum: Lycētus — Lycetus, son of Spercheus, one of Phineus' men (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.lyncidae: Lyncidēs — of Lyncides, the descendant of Lynceus, i.e. Perseus (m. gen. sg. of the Greek patronymic, with 'pectora')
glossary.lyncides: Lyncidēs — Lyncides, descendant of Lynceus — Ovid's name for Perseus (m. nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
glossary.lyrae: lyra — of the lyre (f. gen. sg. with 'fila': the strings of the lyre; not nom. pl. here)
glossary.lyraeque: lyra + -que — and lyres (f. nom. pl. + enclitic, subject with 'tibia' and 'cantus' of 'sonant'; nom. pl., not gen. sg.)
glossary.mactati: mactō — sacrificed, felled at the altar (perf. part., m. gen. sg. with 'iuvenci': after the manner of a slaughtered bullock; not nom. pl.)
glossary.mactatur: mactō — is sacrificed, is slaughtered (3 sg. pres. pass.: a heifer is offered to Minerva)
glossary.madefacta: madefaciō — soaked, drenched (perf. part., f. nom. sg. with 'tellus': the ground sodden with blood)
glossary.maduere: madeō — grew wet, were drenched (3 pl. perf. in '-ēre' = 'maduerunt': his wings soaked heavy with spray)
glossary.magica: magicus — magic (n. acc. pl. with 'arma': the youth who wields magic weapons)
glossary.manabant: mānō — were streaming, running (3 pl. impf.: her eyes ran with warm tears)
glossary.manere: maneō — to await, to remain in store for (pres. act. inf. with 'poterunt'; from 'maneo', not from 'mano' to flow)
glossary.mansura: maneō — destined to last, enduring (fut. act. part., n. acc. pl. with 'monimenta': memorials that will abide through the ages)
glossary.marmaridae: Marmaridēs — Marmarian, of the Marmaridae of North Africa (m. gen. sg. with 'Corythi')
glossary.marmor: marmor — marble (n. nom. sg., predicate to the plural 'corpora': the bodies were marble)
glossary.marmoreoque: marmoreus — of marble (n. abl. sg. + enclitic, with 'ore': the wondering look stays on his marble face)
glossary.marmoreum: marmoreus — of marble (n. acc. sg. with 'opus': he would have thought her a marble statue)
glossary.massae: massa — lump, mass of metal (f. gen. sg. with 'multae ... in pondere': heavy with the weight of much bronze)
glossary.maternae: māternus — of the mother, maternal (f. gen. sg.; with 'linguae' — she pays for her mother's tongue — and with 'formae' — her mother's confidence in her beauty)
glossary.mediae: medius — middle (f. gen. sg. with 'cervicis': into the bones of the middle of the neck; not nom. pl. or dat.)
glossary.medii: medius — middle (n. gen. sg. with 'caeli', partitive: as much of mid-heaven as a sling can shoot its lead across)
glossary.medulla: medulla — pith, marrow (f. abl. sg. with 'bibula ... viva': a fresh shoot still alive with thirsty pith)
glossary.medusa: Medūsa — Medusa, the Gorgon (f. abl. sg. in an abl. abs. with 'visa': turned to flint at the sight of Medusa herself; not nom.)
glossary.medusae: Medūsa — of Medusa, the Gorgon (f. gen. sg. at every occurrence — with 'ora', 'caede', 'formam', 'vultus', 'laudem'; never dat. or nom. pl.)
glossary.medusaeo: Medūsaeus — of Medusa, Medusaean (adj., abl. sg.: n. with 'ore', by Medusa's face; m. with 'fonte', the spring Medusa's winged horse struck open).
glossary.memoratis: memorō — recounted, told (perf. part., n. abl. pl. in an abl. abs. with 'omnibus': not yet everything having been told)
glossary.menaleus: Menaleus — Menaleus, a follower of Perseus' side (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.mendesius: Mendēsius — Mendesian, of Mendes in Egypt (m. nom. sg. with 'Celadon')
glossary.mensas: mēnsa — table (f. acc. pl.: he spatters the laid tables with blood)
glossary.mentiris: mentior — you lie about, you falsely claim (2 sg. pres. of the deponent: the glory you claim falsely)
glossary.meritis: meritum — service, desert, merit (n. abl. pl.; 'meritis et voce' — by deserts and by his word — and 'meritis melior' — better in point of merits)
glossary.meritisne: meritum + -ne — is this the thanks for such services? (n. dat. pl. with 'tantis' + the interrogative enclitic '-ne')
glossary.meritum: meritum — desert, service rendered (n. acc. sg.; once object of 'addere' beside the dowry, once object of 'impugnante')
glossary.metione: Metīōn — Metion, father of Phorbas (m. abl. sg. of origin with 'genitus')
glossary.metuens: metuō — fearing (pres. part., m. nom. sg. with the acc. object 'id': Atlas, in fear of this)
glossary.minis: minae — threats (f. dat. pl. of the plural-only noun, with 'addit': he adds force to threats)
glossary.mirabere: miror — you will marvel at (2 sg. fut. of the deponent, in '-re' for '-ris': you will wonder at ours)
glossary.mirantis: miror — of the man marvelling (pres. part. of the deponent, m. gen. sg.: the face of the wondering man; not acc. pl.)
glossary.mirator: mīrātor — an admirer, one who marvels at (+ gen.) (m. nom. sg. noun with 'es'; not a verb form)
glossary.miscentem: misceō — mixing, blending (pres. part., m. acc. sg. beside 'cunctantem': mingling bold words with soothing ones)
glossary.missum: mittō — thrown, hurled (perf. part., n. nom. sg. with 'ferrum': the flung blade stood fixed)
glossary.missus: mittō — launched, sent flying (perf. part., m. nom. sg., of Perseus hurled headlong through the empty air; not the 4th-decl. noun)
glossary.mittere: mittō — to hurl, to let fly (pres. act. inf., once with 'conanti', once with 'parabat': as he tried and as he made ready to throw)
glossary.mixtos: misceō — mingled (perf. part., m. acc. pl. with 'fluctus': waves mixed with red blood)
glossary.modestos: modestus — modest, shy (m. acc. pl. with 'vultus' in the next line: she would have hidden her modest face)
glossary.molis: mōlēs — mass, bulk, massive rock (f. gen. sg. with 'solidae': safe behind the shelter of a solid mass)
glossary.mollierant: molliō — had softened (3 pl. pluperf., syncopated for 'mollīverant': neither valour nor misfortunes had softened him)
glossary.molpea: Molpeus — Molpeus, a Chaonian in Phineus' band (m. acc. sg. in the Greek form '-ea')
glossary.molpeus: Molpeus — Molpeus the Chaonian (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.monilia: monīle — necklace (n. nom. pl., subject of 'ornabant': gilded necklaces adorned his neck)
glossary.monstri: mōnstrum — of the monster (n. gen. sg. at all three occurrences — the viper-haired, snake-bearing monster Medusa; not nom. pl.)
glossary.moresque: mōs — customs, ways (m. acc. pl. + enclitic: Perseus tells of the men's customs and character)
glossary.moribundo: moribundus — dying, at the point of death (m. abl. sg. with 'vertice': he beats the ground with his dying head)
glossary.morientibus: morior — dying (pres. part. of the deponent, m. abl. pl. with 'digitis': he plucks the strings again with dying fingers)

glossary.celeberrimus: celeber — most famous, most talked of (superl., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.cephisius: Cēphīsius — the son of Cephisus, i.e. Narcissus (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.cephisus: Cēphīsus — Cephisus, the Boeotian river-god, father of Narcissus (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.certet: certō — let her compete, let her contend (3 sg. pres. act. subj., jussive)
glossary.chirona: Chīrōn — Chiron, the centaur whom Saturn begot in horse form (m. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.ciconia: cicōnia — stork (f. nom. sg., in apposition to 'ipsa')
glossary.cinctaeque: cingō — girded up (perf. pass. part., f. nom. pl., of the two weavers, with 'vestes' as Greek acc. of respect: girt as to their robes; + -que)

glossary.circumlita: circumlinō — smeared round, coated (perf. pass. part., n. nom. pl., with 'sulphura'; not the f. nom. sg.)
glossary.circumstantes: circumstō — standing round, encircling (pres. act. part., f. acc. pl., with 'silvas')
glossary.clausaeque: claudō — shut in, hemmed in (perf. pass. part., f. dat. sg., of Liriope, the dative object of 'vim tulit'; + -que)
glossary.clausis: claudō — closed, barred (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl., with 'portis')

glossary.coetus: coetus — gatherings, companies (m. acc. pl., with 'viriles', object of 'luserat'; the form is also nom. sg.)
glossary.colophonius: Colophōnius — of Colophon, the Ionian city (m. nom. sg., with 'Idmon', Arachne's father)
glossary.concordes: concors — of one mind, in harmony (m. nom. pl., with 'duo')
glossary.confecta: cōnficiō — worn out, used up (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., + abl. 'senecta')

glossary.consilii: cōnsilium — of counsel, of advice (n. gen. sg., partitive with 'satis')
glossary.consilium: cōnsilium — advice, counsel (n. acc. sg., object of 'sperne')
glossary.constituunt: cōnstituō — they take up their stations, they post themselves (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.consultus: cōnsulō — consulted, asked for a ruling (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., of the seer Tiresias); the participle, not the noun/adj. cōnsultus 'an expert'
glossary.crearit: creō — begot, brought forth (3 sg. perf. act. subj., syncopated for creāverit, in an indirect question after 'ut')

glossary.crepitante: crepitō — clattering, clacking (pres. act. part., n. abl. sg., with 'rostro')
glossary.crudelius: crūdēlis — more cruelly (comparative adv., with 'amavit'); the form is also the comparative adj., n. nom./acc. sg.
glossary.cupiere: cupiō — desired, longed for (3 pl. perf. act., poetic -ēre for -ērunt)
glossary.cupio: cupiō — I desire, I long for (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.danaen: Danaē — Danae, shut in a tower, whom Jupiter reached as a shower of gold (f. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.deceperit: dēcipiō — tricked, took in (3 sg. perf. act. subj., in an indirect question after 'ut')
glossary.decipit: dēcipiō — deceives, takes in (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.decusque: decus — grace, glory, beauty (n. acc. sg., with 'oris'; + -que)
glossary.deducitur: dēdūcō — is drawn down, is spun into the web (3 sg. pres. pass.; the weaver's word)
glossary.defenditur: dēfendō — is guarded, is protected (3 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.defluxere: dēfluō — fell away, dropped off (3 pl. perf. act., poetic -ēre for -ērunt)
glossary.delphina: delphīn — dolphin (m. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.delusa: dēlūdō — tricked, made a fool of (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., with 'sum', Juno of herself)
glossary.deoida: Dēōis — the daughter of Deo (Ceres), i.e. Proserpina, whom Jupiter reached as a spotted snake (f. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.deseruere: dēserō — abandoned, left behind (3 pl. perf. act., poetic -ēre for -ērunt; repeated at 15 and 16)
glossary.designat: dēsignō — marks out, depicts (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.despectus: dēspiciō — scorned, looked down on (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., with 'aliquis'); the participle, not the noun dēspectus 'a view downwards'

glossary.diligitur: dīligō — is loved (3 sg. pres. pass.)

glossary.discedet: discēdō — will go away, will depart (3 sg. fut. act.)
glossary.discriminis: discrīmen — of difference, of distinction (n. gen. sg., with 'parvi')
glossary.distant: distō — stand apart, are far apart (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.distincta: distinguō — picked out, set off (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl., with 'certamina'; not the f. nom. sg.)
glossary.diuturnior: diūturnus — longer-lasting, longer-lived (comparative, m. nom. sg., with 'hic')
glossary.diversi: dīversus — different, of many kinds (m. nom. pl., with 'colores')
glossary.docta: doctus — skilled, trained (n. acc. pl., with 'bracchia'; not the f. nom./abl. sg.)

glossary.doluit: doleō — grieved, was stung (3 sg. perf. act., of Pallas)
glossary.domini: dominus — of their owner, of their master (m. gen. sg., with 'lumina'; not the nom. pl.)
glossary.ductum: dūcō — drawn, carried through (perf. pass. part., n. acc. sg., with 'quod' = the weft); not the noun ductus

glossary.ecquem: ecquis — anyone at all? (interrogative pron., m. acc. sg., object of 'meministis')
glossary.ecquis: ecquis — is there anyone?, anyone at all? (interrogative pron., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.egressaque: ēgredior — having come out (perf. part. of a deponent, so active in sense, f. nom. sg., + abl. 'silva'; + -que)
glossary.eheu: eheu — alas! (interjection of grief); at 495 the boy's cry, at 496 Echo giving the same word back
glossary.elusam: ēlūdō — tricked, cheated (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., with 'Europam')
glossary.emoriar: ēmorior — let me die, I would die first (1 sg. pres. subj. of a deponent, in the 'ante...quam' clause; the form is also the fut. ind.)
glossary.equo: equus — in horse form, as a horse (m. abl. sg.; not the dat. sg.)
glossary.equum: equus — a horse (m. acc. sg., predicative after 'sensit': knew him as a horse)
glossary.erigonen: Ērigonē — Erigone, daughter of Icarius, whom Bacchus deceived with a false grape (f. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.europam: Eurōpa — Europa, carried off by Jupiter in the shape of a bull (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.evanuit: ēvānēscō — faded away, vanished (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.exhibuit: exhibeō — displayed, showed forth (3 sg. perf. act.)

glossary.exiles: exīlis — thin, spindly (m. nom. pl., with 'digiti')

glossary.expediunt: expediō — work free, ply, get through (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.exsiluisse: exsiliō — to have leapt out, to have sprung forth (perf. act. inf., in indirect statement after 'facit')
glossary.exspectare: exspectō — to wait for (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.exstinguor: exstinguō — I am being put out, I am dying (1 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.extenuant: extenuō — wear thin, waste away (3 pl. pres. act., with 'curae')
glossary.extremas: extrēmus — outermost, at the very edge (f. acc. pl., with 'oras' = the borders of the web)
glossary.faces: fax — torches (f. acc. pl.; the funeral torches)
glossary.faciendae: faciō — to be worked, of the working (gerundive, f. gen. sg., with 'lanae': fame in wool-working)
glossary.fallente: fallō — beguiling, cheating (pres. act. part., n. abl. sg., with 'studio' in an abl. abs.)

glossary.fallit: fallō — deceives, tricks (3 sg. pres. act.; at both 463 and 66)

glossary.fatidicus: fātidicus — fate-speaking, prophetic (m. nom. sg., with 'vates')
glossary.favet: faveō — backs up, seconds (3 sg. pres. act., + dat. 'verbis')

glossary.festinant: festīnō — hurry, work at speed (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.fetu: fētus — offspring, brood (m. abl. sg., with 'gemino', a twin brood)

glossary.filis: fīlum — threads (n. dat./abl. pl.; the gold is worked in among the warp threads)

glossary.fugiensque: fugiō — fleeing (pres. act. part., m. nom. sg.; + -que)
glossary.fuistis: sum — you have been (perf. 2 pl.; the woods are addressed)
glossary.furialibus: furiālis — frenzied, maddened (n. abl. pl., with 'ausis', such raging daring)

glossary.furoris: furor — of madness, of frenzied passion (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.fusum: fūsus — spindle (m. acc. sg.; not fūsum, perf. part. of fundō 'pour out')

glossary.gignis: gignō — you beget (pres. 2 sg.; Neptune is addressed)
glossary.glomerabat: glomerō — was winding into a ball, was balling up (impf. 3 sg.)
glossary.gracili: gracilis — slender, fine (n. abl. sg., with 'stamine')
glossary.grandior: grandis — greater, more advanced (compar., f. nom. sg., with 'aetas': greater age, old age)
glossary.gruem: grūs — crane, the bird (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.haemum: Haemus — Haemus, the Thracian mountain (m. acc. sg.; once a mortal, turned to stone for taking a god's name)
glossary.harundo: harundō — reed; here the loom's reed that keeps the warp apart (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.hecateidos: Hecatēis — of Hecate, Hecate's (f. gen. sg., Greek ending, with 'herbae': the witch-herb of Hecate)
glossary.herbae: herba — herb, plant (f. gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.hypaepis: Hypaepa — Hypaepa, a small Lydian town, Arachne's home (n. abl. pl.)
glossary.iacens: iaceō — lying, stretched out (pres. act. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.idmon: Idmōn — Idmon, Arachne's father, a dyer of Colophon (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.idmoniae: Idmonius — Idmon's, daughter of Idmon (f. gen. sg., with 'Arachnes')
glossary.ilion: Īlion — Ilium, Troy (n. nom. sg.; Antigone's native city)
glossary.imaginis: imāgō — of the image, of the reflection (f. gen. sg.)
glossary.imbre: imber — rain, shower (m. abl. sg.; the rainbow springs from it)
glossary.implerit: impleō — filled, made pregnant (perf. subj. 3 sg., syncopated for implēverit)
glossary.implicuit: implicō — enfolded, entangled (perf. 3 sg.; Cephisus catching Liriope in his winding stream)
glossary.improba: improbus — shameless, wicked one (f. voc. sg.; Pallas addressing Arachne)
glossary.imprudens: imprūdēns — unaware, not realizing (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.impubesque: impūbēs — beardless, boyish (f. acc. pl., with 'genas'; + -que)
glossary.inceptaque: incipiō — begun, started (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl., with 'fila'; + -que)
glossary.incepto: inceptum — undertaking, what she has begun (n. abl. sg.; the noun from the part. of incipiō)
glossary.incipiat: incipiō — she should begin, speak first (pres. subj. 3 sg.; subjunctive after 'sinit' without ut)
glossary.incitat: incitō — spurs on, goads (pres. 3 sg.; subject 'error')
glossary.indicere: indīcō — to declare, proclaim (pres. act. inf.; 'bella indicere', to declare war)
glossary.inexpleto: inexplētus — unsated, never satisfied (n. abl. sg., with 'lumine': with unfilled gaze)
glossary.inferna: infernus — of the world below, infernal (f. abl. sg., with 'sede')
glossary.inficere: inficiō — to tinge, stain with colour (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.infirmos: īnfirmus — weak, feeble (m. acc. pl., with 'artus', limbs)
glossary.iniceret: iniciō — she might throw around, fling upon (impf. subj. 3 sg.; purpose clause)
glossary.inlimis: illīmis — free of mud, unclouded (m. nom. sg.; spelled 'inlimis' here)
glossary.inmotus: immōtus — unmoving, motionless (m. nom. sg.; spelled 'inmotus' here)
glossary.inopem: inops — destitute, poor (m. acc. sg., predicative: plenty has made me poor)
glossary.inreprehensa: irreprehēnsus — unfaulted, beyond reproach (n. acc. pl., with 'responsa'; spelled 'inreprehensa')
glossary.inscribit: īnscrībō — marks, labels, identifies (pres. 3 sg.; subject 'facies')
glossary.insecti: īnsecō — cut into, notched (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl., with 'dentes'; not the gen. sg. of the same form)
glossary.inseritur: īnserō — is inserted, is threaded in (pres. pass. 3 sg.; subject 'subtemen', the weft)
glossary.intabescere: intābēscō — to melt away, waste away (pres. act. inf., with 'solent')
glossary.intellegat: intellegō — she may understand, may take it in (pres. subj. 3 sg.; purpose clause)
glossary.intendit: intendō — turned, directed (perf. 3 sg.; the form is identical with the pres. 3 sg.)
glossary.intendunt: intendō — they stretch, string up (pres. 3 pl.; of setting the warp on the loom)
glossary.intertextos: intertexō — interwoven (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with 'flores')
glossary.ipsae: ipse — ourselves, we too (f. nom. pl., subject of 'laudemur')
glossary.issen: Issē — Isse, daughter of Macareus, beguiled by Apollo in shepherd's shape (f. acc. sg., Greek ending)
glossary.istas: iste — those (words) of yours (f. acc. pl., with 'voces'; iste points at the addressee's own advice)
glossary.iterabat: iterō — repeated, said over again (impf. 3 sg.)
glossary.iustamque: iūstus — just, deserved (f. acc. sg., with 'iram'; + -que)
glossary.iuvenco: iuvencus — young bull, bullock (m. abl. sg.; the shape Neptune took)
glossary.iuvenisque: iuvenis — a youth, young man (m. nom. sg. of the noun, predicate with 'videri'; + -que)
glossary.lacrimante: lacrimō — weeping (pres. act. part., abl. sg.; abl. abs. with 'me', while I wept)
glossary.lacrimare: lacrimō — to weep (pres. act. inf., with 'videtur')
glossary.lacu: lacus — pool, standing water (m. abl. sg., 4th decl.; with 'moto', the water stirred up)
glossary.lanae: lāna — wool (f. gen. sg., with the gerundive 'faciendae': for the working of wool)
glossary.lanificae: lānificus — wool-working (f. gen. sg., with 'artis': the craft of working wool)
glossary.laomedonve: Lāomedōn — Laomedon, king of Troy, Antigone's father (m. nom. sg.; + -ve, 'or')
glossary.lapsus: lābor — fallen, slipped down (perf. part. of the deponent, m. nom. sg., with 'ramus'; not lāpsus, -ūs 'a fall')
glossary.lassus: lassus — weary, worn out (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.latebra: latebra — hiding-place, covert (f. nom. sg.; predicate with 'fuistis')
glossary.latere: latus — side, flank (n. abl. sg.; not the infinitive latēre 'to lie hidden')
glossary.laudare: laudō — to praise (pres. act. inf.; subject of 'parum est')
glossary.laudemur: laudō — let us too be praised (pres. pass. subj. 1 pl.; hortatory)
glossary.laudibus: laus — in the praises, in the renown (f. abl. pl. of respect with 'cedere'; the dat. after 'cedere' is 'sibi')
glossary.ledam: Lēda — Leda, whom Jupiter came to as a swan (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.lentum: lentus — pliant, supple (n. nom. sg., with 'aurum', of the gold thread; not 'slow' here)
glossary.levatus: levō — raised up, lifting himself (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.libentius: libenter — more gladly, more willingly (compar. adv.)
glossary.liquefacta: liquefaciō — melted, made liquid, run clear again (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg., with 'unda')
glossary.liriope: Līriopē — Liriope, a water-nymph, Narcissus's mother (f. nom. sg., Greek ending)
glossary.livor: līvor — Envy, spite (m. nom. sg.; personified, and capitalized in the text)
glossary.loci: locus — of the place (m. gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.longaque: longus — long (f. abl. sg., with 'senecta': worn out by long old age; + -que)
glossary.luctante: luctor — struggling, wrestling (pres. act. part. of the deponent, f. abl. sg., with 'aquila')
glossary.luserat: lūdō — had mocked, had made sport of (pluperf. 3 sg.)
glossary.luserit: lūdō — deceived, beguiled (perf. subj. 3 sg., in the 'ut' clauses describing the weaving)
glossary.lydas: Lydus — Lydian (f. acc. pl., with 'urbes'; Lydia is Arachne's country)
glossary.macareida: Macarēis — daughter of Macareus, i.e. Isse (f. acc. sg., Greek ending)
glossary.maeoniaeque: Maeonius — Maeonian, Lydian (f. gen. sg., with 'Arachnes'; + -que)
glossary.maeonis: Maeonis — the Maeonian woman, i.e. Arachne (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.magistra: magistra — mistress, teacher (f. abl. sg. of cause with 'tanta': offended at so great a teacher; the form is also nom. sg.)
glossary.matura: mātūrus — ripe (f. nom. sg., with 'uva': the grape not yet ripe)
glossary.maturae: mātūrus — ripe, full (f. gen. sg., with 'senectae': ripe old age)
glossary.matutinaeque: mātūtīnus — of the morning, early (f. nom. pl., with 'pruinae', morning frosts; + -que)

glossary.memorque: memor — mindful, unforgetting (f. nom. sg., of Echo, who still remembers her hurt; + -que)
glossary.mendacem: mendāx — lying, deceptive (f. acc. sg., with 'formam')
glossary.minimum: minimus — smallest, a very little thing (superl. of parvus, n. nom. sg.; substantive at III.453 'it is a tiny thing that stands in the way', with 'caput' at VI.142)

glossary.mirantia: mīror — marvelling at, gazing in wonder (pres. act. part. of the deponent, n. acc. pl., with 'lumina')

glossary.misero: miser — wretched, pitiable (m. dat. sg., with 'furori')
glossary.mixto: misceō — mingled, blended (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg., with 'candore')
glossary.mixtum: misceō — mingled, blended (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg., with 'ruborem')

glossary.adiecit: adiciō, adicere, adiēcī — to add, add besides (3rd sg. perfect active indicative)
glossary.adiectura: adiciō, adicere — about to add (future active participle, fem. nom. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with erat, an active periphrastic, 'she was on the point of adding')
glossary.adlevet: adlevō (= allevō), adlevāre — to lift up, raise; to relieve, ease (3rd sg. present active subjunctive; here in a purpose clause; unassimilated adl- for all-)
glossary.admissa: admittō, admittere, admīsī, admissum — let go at full speed, given free rein (perfect passive participle; fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here neut. acc. pl. with crura, of a galloping horse)
glossary.admonita: admoneō, admonēre, admonitum — warned, put in mind (perfect passive participle; fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with est, 'she was not warned')
glossary.adusque: adūsque (= ad + usque) — all the way to, as far as (preposition + accusative; also, as here, adverbial, 'even as far as')
glossary.adverti: advertō, advertere, advertī — to turn (something) towards (1st sg. perfect active indicative, 'I have turned'; the identical form is also the present passive infinitive 'to be turned' — here active, with lumina as object)
glossary.advolat: advolō, advolāre — to fly to, come rushing up (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.aetherium: aetherius, -a, -um — of the upper air, of the sky, heavenly (masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.; here masc. acc. sg. with axem)
glossary.agrestes: agrestis, -e — of the fields, rustic; as a noun, country folk (masc./fem. nom. or acc. pl.; here nom. pl. as subject)
glossary.albet: albeō, albēre — to be white (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.aliisque: alius, alia, aliud — other, the rest (dat. or abl. pl. of any gender; here abl. pl. in the ablative absolute aliis repertis) + -que 'and'
glossary.alphenor: Alphēnōr — Alphenor, one of Niobe's seven sons (masc. nom. sg.)
glossary.amphion: Amphīōn, -onis m. — Amphion, king of Thebes, husband of Niobe, who raised the city walls by his lyre (masc. nom. sg.)
glossary.amphiona: Amphīōn, -onis m. — Amphion, Niobe's husband (masc. acc. sg., Greek accusative in -a for Latin Amphīonem)
glossary.amphione: Amphīōn, -onis m. — Amphion, Niobe's husband (masc. abl. sg.; here 'genitis Amphione', begotten by Amphion)
glossary.arceor: arceō, arcēre — to keep off, shut out, bar (1st sg. present passive indicative, 'I am barred'; here with abl. aris, 'from the altars')
glossary.arcu: arcus, -ūs m. — bow (4th decl., abl. sg.; the same form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.arent: āreō, ārēre — to be dry, be parched (3rd pl. present active indicative, 'are parched'); the same spelling is also the 3rd pl. present subjunctive of arō 'plough' — here it is āreō
glossary.aris: āra, -ae f. — altar (dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. of separation, 'from the altars')
glossary.armentaque: armentum, -ī n. — herd of cattle (neut. nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl., object of pavit) + -que 'and'
glossary.arto: artus, -a, -um — tight, close, narrow (masc./neut. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. with nexu, 'in a tight grip'); the same form is also 1st sg. present of artō 'tighten', and must not be confused with artus, -ūs m. 'limb'
glossary.asello: asellus, -ī m. — little ass, donkey (diminutive of asinus; dat. or abl. sg.; here with haeret, 'clings to his donkey')
glossary.audete: audeō, audēre (semi-deponent, perf. ausus sum) — to dare (2nd pl. present active imperative, 'go on and dare')
glossary.auditos: audiō, audīre, audītum — heard, heard of (perfect passive participle, masc. acc. pl.; here used substantivally, 'gods merely heard of', opposed to visis 'those seen')
glossary.auroque: aurum, -ī n. — gold (dat. or abl. sg.; here abl., 'heavy with gold') + -que 'and'
glossary.ausi: audeō, audēre (semi-deponent, perf. ausus sum) — having dared (perfect participle, masc. nom. pl. or masc./neut. gen. sg.; here nom. pl. with essent, 'that they had dared')
glossary.autem: autem — but, however; moreover (postpositive conjunction, never the first word of its clause)
glossary.aviti: avītus, -a, -um — of a grandfather, ancestral (masc./neut. gen. sg. or masc. nom. pl.; here gen. sg. with nominis, 'of his grandfather's name')
glossary.bacchae: Baccha, -ae f. — a Bacchante, female follower of Bacchus (gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl.; here nom. pl.)
glossary.bacchumque: Bacchus, -ī m. — Bacchus, god of wine (masc. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.biiugum: biiugus, -a, -um — yoked two abreast, drawing in a pair (masc. gen. pl., the contracted -um for -ōrum, agreeing with lyncum, 'of the paired lynxes')
glossary.bimatrem: bimāter, bimātris — having two mothers (masc. acc. sg.; a cult epithet of Bacchus, carried by Semele and then by Jupiter's thigh)
glossary.bipenniferumque: bipennifer, -fera, -ferum — axe-bearing, wielding the double axe (masc. acc. sg., here with Lycurgum) + -que 'and'
glossary.blanda: blandus, -a, -um — coaxing, winning, caressing (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here neut. nom. pl. with verba)
glossary.bona: bonus, -a, -um — good; as a neuter substantive, goods, blessings, good fortune (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here neut. nom. pl., 'my blessings')
glossary.bromiumque: Bromius, -ī m. — Bromius, 'the Roarer', a cult name of Bacchus (masc. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.bucera: būcerus (būcerās), -a, -um — ox-horned, horned like cattle (neut. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl. with armenta; a Greek-derived compound)
glossary.buxus: buxus, -ī f. — box-tree, boxwood; by metonymy a boxwood pipe or flute (nom. sg.)
glossary.caducas: cadūcus, -a, -um — falling, ready to fall; doomed (fem. acc. pl.; here of falling tears)
glossary.calmeida: Cadmēis, -idos — Cadmean, Theban, of the city Cadmus founded (fem. acc. sg., Greek accusative in -ida, agreeing with arcem, 'the Theban citadel'; the edition here prints Calmeida for Cadmēida)
glossary.cantu: cantus, -ūs m. — song, singing; a magic incantation (4th decl., abl. sg., here abl. of means, 'by her singing'; the same form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.capite: caput, capitis n. — head (abl. sg.; here with cum); identical in spelling to capite, the 2nd pl. imperative of capiō 'take'
glossary.carbasa: carbasus, -ī f. — fine linen, canvas, a sail; its plural is the heteroclite neuter carbasa, -ōrum (neut. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl., object of deducit)
glossary.caret: careō, carēre — to lack, be without, go without (+ ablative) (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.casu: cāsus, -ūs m. — a falling; chance, accident, mishap (4th decl., abl. sg.; used adverbially, 'by chance, as it happened')
glossary.censet: cēnseō, cēnsēre — to assess, reckon, judge, be of the opinion (3rd sg. present active indicative; here governing an indirect statement, 'holds that ...')
glossary.certam: certus, -a, -um — sure, certain, settled (fem. acc. sg.; here predicative with matrem, 'made the mother certain of it')
glossary.cessura: cēdō, cēdere, cessum — about to yield, one who would give way (+ dat.) (future active participle, fem. nom. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg., of Niobe)
glossary.chimaeriferae: Chimaerifer, -fera, -ferum — Chimaera-bearing, breeder of the Chimaera (fem. gen./dat. sg. or fem. nom. pl.; here gen. sg. with Lyciae)
glossary.circumtulit: circumferō, circumferre, circumtulī — to carry round, cast about (3rd sg. perfect active indicative; here 'oculos circumtulit', she swept her eyes around)
glossary.clamabat: clāmō, clāmāre — to shout, cry out (3rd sg. imperfect active indicative, 'kept crying')
glossary.clamanti: clāmō, clāmāre — shouting, crying out (present active participle, dat. sg. of any gender; here dative of the person affected, 'from him as he cried out')
glossary.coei: Coeus, -ī m. — Coeus, the Titan, father of Latona (masc. gen. sg.; 'filia Coei' is Latona)
glossary.coeo: Coeus, -ī m. — Coeus, the Titan (masc. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. of origin with satam, 'sprung from Coeus')
glossary.cogitat: cōgitō, cōgitāre — to turn over in the mind, consider, ponder (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.cognoverat: cognōscō, cognōscere, cognōvī — to come to know, get to know, learn (3rd sg. pluperfect active indicative, 'had come to know')
glossary.collabitur: collābor, collābī — to fall in a heap, collapse (deponent, 3rd sg. present indicative)
glossary.communiter: commūniter — in common, jointly, all together (adverb, from commūnis)
glossary.comparentis: compāreō, compārēre — being visible, being there to be found (present active participle, gen. sg.; here 'non comparentis', of the part that was nowhere to be found)
glossary.compressit: comprimō, comprimere, compressī — to press together, squeeze shut, close (3rd sg. perfect active indicative)
glossary.concavaque: concavus, -a, -um — hollow, hollowed out, curved (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here neut. nom. pl. with aera, 'hollow bronzes') + -que 'and'
glossary.concolor: concolor, concolōris — of the same colour, matching in colour (3rd decl. adj., nom. sg.; here with umerus)
glossary.congelat: congelō, congelāre — to freeze solid, congeal, stiffen (3rd sg. present active indicative; here intransitive)
glossary.conlegit: conligō (= colligō), conligere, conlēgī — to gather, collect, pick up (3rd sg. perfect active indicative; here 'sitim conlegit', worked up a thirst; the edition prints the unassimilated conl- for coll-)
glossary.conscendunt: cōnscendō, cōnscendere — to climb, mount (3rd pl. present active indicative; here 'conscendunt in equos', they mount their horses)
glossary.consitor: cōnsitor, cōnsitōris m. — planter, sower (masc. nom. sg.; here 'consitor uvae', the planter of the vine, i.e. Bacchus); an agent noun from cōnserō, not a passive verb form
glossary.conspiceris: cōnspiciō, cōnspicere — to catch sight of, behold (2nd sg. present passive indicative, 'you are beheld'; the future passive would be spelled cōnspiciēris)
glossary.contactu: contāctus, -ūs m. — touch, contact (4th decl., abl. sg.; here abl. of means, 'by contact with')
glossary.contento: contendō, contendere, contentum — stretched tight, drawn taut (perfect passive participle, masc./neut. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. with arcu, 'from the drawn bow'; distinct from contentus 'content', from contineō)
glossary.conterruit: conterreō, conterrēre, conterruī — to terrify utterly, panic (3rd sg. perfect active indicative)
glossary.conticuit: conticēscō, conticēscere, conticuī — to fall silent, go quiet (inceptive verb; 3rd sg. perfect active indicative)
glossary.contulerant: cōnferō, cōnferre, contulī — to bring together, bring into contact (3rd pl. pluperfect active indicative, 'they had brought together')
glossary.conviciaque: convīcium, -ī n. — abuse, taunt, jeering (neut. nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl., object of addunt) + -que 'and'
glossary.corporeusque: corporeus, -a, -um — of flesh, bodily, of natural body (masc. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.corque: cor, cordis n. — heart (neut. nom. or acc. sg.; here acc. sg., object of satia) + -que 'and'
glossary.crus: crūs, crūris n. — leg, shin, lower leg (neut. nom. or acc. sg.; here nom. sg.)
glossary.cultuque: cultus, -ūs m. — worship, reverence; cultivation; dress, grooming (4th decl., dat. or abl. sg.; here abl., of worship) + -que 'and'
glossary.cynthi: Cynthus, -ī m. — Cynthus, the mountain on Delos where Latona bore Apollo and Diana (masc. gen. sg.)
glossary.damasichthona: Damasichthōn — Damasichthon, one of Niobe's sons (masc. acc. sg., Greek accusative in -a)
glossary.dantem: dō, dare — giving (present active participle, masc./fem. acc. sg.; here 'frena dantem', him as he gave the horse its rein)
glossary.datis: dō, dare, dedī, datum — given, given over (perfect passive participle, dat. or abl. pl.; here dat. pl., 'to the six given over to death'); the same spelling is also the 2nd pl. present active indicative of dō, 'you give'
glossary.dearum: dea, -ae f. — goddess (gen. pl., 'of the goddesses'; this noun has irregular deābus in the dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.decolor: dēcolor, dēcolōris — discoloured, darkened, swarthy (3rd decl. adj., nom. sg.; here with India, of sun-darkened skin)
glossary.decoro: decōrus, -a, -um — graceful, comely, seemly (masc./neut. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. with capite); the same form is also 1st sg. present of decorō 'adorn'
glossary.dederitis: dō, dare, dedī — to give (2nd pl. future perfect active indicative, 'you will have given', or 2nd pl. perfect active subjunctive; here future perfect, 'you will have granted me life')
glossary.deducens: dēdūcō, dēdūcere — drawing down, drawing out, spinning out (present active participle, nom. sg.; here of drawing out thread with the thumb)
glossary.deducere: dēdūcō, dēdūcere — to lead down, bring away, escort, draw out (present active infinitive)
glossary.defluit: dēfluō, dēfluere — to flow down, glide down, fall away in a slope (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.delos: Dēlos, -ī f. — Delos, the once-floating island where Latona bore her twins (fem. nom. sg.; a Greek 2nd-declension noun, feminine despite its -os ending)
glossary.demi: dēmō, dēmere — to be taken away, be subtracted (present passive infinitive; here in indirect statement after Fingite, 'imagine that ... is taken away')
glossary.demisso: dēmittō, dēmittere, dēmissum — let down, loosened, hanging loose (perfect passive participle, masc./neut. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. with crine, 'with hair let down')
glossary.deponunt: dēpōnō, dēpōnere — to lay down, put aside (3rd pl. present active indicative)
glossary.derceti: Dercetis (Derketō) — Derceto, the Syrian-Babylonian goddess who took the form of a fish (vocative sg., in apposition to the addressed Babylonia)
glossary.deriguitque: dērigēscō, dērigēscere, dēriguī — to grow stiff, harden, go rigid (3rd sg. perfect active indicative) + -que 'and'
glossary.desistunt: dēsistō, dēsistere — to leave off, cease (3rd pl. present active indicative; here with a following infinitive)
glossary.detectique: dētegō, dētegere, dētēctum — uncovered, laid bare, stripped (perfect passive participle, masc. nom. pl.; here with nervi) + -que 'and'
glossary.detinet: dētineō, dētinēre — to hold back, hold fast, keep occupied (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.detis: dō, dare — to give, grant (2nd pl. present active subjunctive; here in a ut-clause after peto, 'I beg that you grant')
glossary.detrahis: dētrahō, dētrahere — to drag off, strip away, pull from (2nd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.dilatant: dīlātō, dīlātāre — to widen, spread wide, stretch out (3rd pl. present active indicative)
glossary.dispensat: dispēnsō, dispēnsāre — to distribute, deal out in portions (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.diversaque: dīversus, -a, -um — turned different ways, various, differing (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here neut. acc. pl. with vulnera) + -que 'and'
glossary.domina: domina, -ae f. — mistress, lady of the house (nom. or abl. sg.; here abl. with sub, 'under a mistress')
glossary.dominasque: domina, -ae f. — mistress, lady of the house (acc. pl.; here paired against famulas 'maidservants') + -que 'and'
glossary.dubia: dubius, -a, -um — doubtful, uncertain, wavering (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with est, 'she is undecided')
glossary.dubitet: dubitō, dubitāre — to doubt, hesitate (3rd sg. present active subjunctive; here potential, 'who would doubt it?')
glossary.dubitor: dubitō, dubitāre — to doubt, question (1st sg. present passive indicative, 'I am doubted'; here 'an dea sim dubitor', it is questioned whether I am a goddess)
glossary.ducem: dux, ducis m./f. — leader, guide (acc. sg.)
glossary.duplicataque: duplicō, duplicāre, duplicātum — doubled up, bent double (perfect passive participle; fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with est) + -que 'and'
glossary.duraque: dūrus, -a, -um — hard, tough, unyielding (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with ungula) + -que 'and'
glossary.dux: dux, ducis m./f. — leader, guide (nom. sg.)
glossary.ebiberant: ēbibō, ēbibere, ēbibī — to drink up, drain dry (3rd pl. pluperfect active indicative, 'had drained')
glossary.ebrius: ēbrius, -a, -um — drunk, intoxicated (masc. nom. sg.; here of Silenus)
glossary.eductum: ēdūcō, ēdūcere, ēductum — drawn out, pulled out (perfect passive participle, masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.; here neut. nom. sg. with est, of the shaft pulled free — note ēdūcō 'draw out' is a 3rd-conjugation verb distinct from ēducō, -āre 'bring up, rear')
glossary.efferor: efferō, efferre — to carry out (especially a corpse, for burial); to lift up, exalt (1st sg. present passive indicative, 'I am carried out / I am borne aloft')
glossary.effluat: effluō, effluere — to flow out, slip away, escape (3rd sg. present active subjunctive; here in a negative purpose clause with ne)
glossary.egerit: agō, agere, ēgī — to spend, pass, live out (time) (3rd sg. perfect active subjunctive here, in the indirect question 'ut ... egerit annos', how she passed her years; the same form is also the 3rd sg. future perfect indicative of agō, and is spelled like ēgerit from ēgerō 'carry out')
glossary.eiaculatus: ēiaculor, ēiaculārī — having shot out, having spurted forth (deponent perfect participle, masc. nom. sg., active in sense; here 'se eiaculatus', having shot itself upward)
glossary.eleleusque: Eleleus, -eī m. — Eleleus, a cult name of Bacchus, from the ritual cry eleleu (masc. nom. sg., subject of additur) + -que 'and'
glossary.emisit: ēmittō, ēmittere, ēmīsī — to send out, let go, release (3rd sg. perfect active indicative)
glossary.eripiat: ēripiō, ēripere — to snatch away, tear from (3rd sg. present active subjunctive; here in a concessive ut-clause, 'granted that she snatches much away')
glossary.erras: errō, errāre — to wander, stray, roam (2nd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.erratica: errāticus, -a, -um — wandering, roving, not fixed in place (fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with Delos, the once-floating island)
glossary.eruta: ēruō, ēruere, ērutum — torn out, dug out, rooted up (perfect passive participle; fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with pars)
glossary.essent: sum, esse — to be (3rd pl. imperfect subjunctive, 'they were, they might be'; here in a quod-clause of reported reason)
glossary.euhan: Euhan (Euan) — Euhan, a cult name of Bacchus, from the ritual cry euhoe (masc. nom. sg.)
glossary.eveniunt: ēveniō, ēvenīre — to come out, turn out, come to pass, be fulfilled (3rd pl. present active indicative)
glossary.evitabile: ēvītābilis, -e — avoidable, escapable (neut. nom./acc. sg.; here with telum, 'a shaft not to be dodged')
glossary.exanimes: exanimis, -e — lifeless, dead; breathless (masc./fem. nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl. with natos natasque)
glossary.excessere: excēdō, excēdere, excessī — to go out, go beyond, surpass (3rd pl. perfect active indicative; excessēre is the poetic alternative for excessērunt, an ending no dictionary headword shows)
glossary.exhalarunt: exhālō, exhālāre — to breathe out (3rd pl. perfect active indicative; syncopated exhālārunt for exhālāvērunt; with animam, 'they breathed their last')
glossary.exiguam: exiguus, -a, -um — small, scanty, meagre (fem. acc. sg.)
glossary.exitiabile: exitiābilis, -e — deadly, destructive, death-dealing (neut. nom./acc. sg.; here acc. with telum)
glossary.exstabat: exstō, exstāre — to stand out, project, be visible above (3rd sg. imperfect active indicative)
glossary.exsul: exsul, exsulis m./f. — an exile, banished wanderer (nom. sg.; here with a genitive, 'an exile from the world')
glossary.exsulta: exsultō, exsultāre — to leap up, exult, gloat (2nd sg. present active imperative, 'exult!')
glossary.extremos: extrēmus, -a, -um — outermost, farthest, last (superlative of exterus; masc. acc. pl.; here with annos, 'her last years')
glossary.factoque: faciō, facere, factum — made, fashioned, wrought (perfect passive participle, masc./neut. abl. sg.; here neut. abl. with illo, of the ivory piece; the same form is also the abl. sg. of the noun factum 'deed') + -que 'and'
glossary.fatebor: fateor, fatērī — to confess, acknowledge, declare openly (deponent, 1st sg. future indicative, 'I shall declare')
glossary.fatifero: fātifer, -fera, -ferum — death-bringing, fatal (masc./neut. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. with ferro, 'with deadly iron')
glossary.fauni: Faunus, -ī m. — a Faun, woodland deity (masc. gen. sg. or nom. pl.; here nom. pl., in apposition to numina)
glossary.faunine: Faunus, -ī m. — a Faun, woodland deity (masc. gen. sg., 'of a Faun') + -ne, the enclitic marking the second limb of the indirect question, 'whether ... or'
glossary.favilla: favilla, -ae f. — glowing ashes, embers (nom. or abl. sg.; here nom. sg.)
glossary.felici: fēlīx, fēlīcis — fortunate, blessed, lucky (3rd decl. adjective, dat. or abl. sg.; here dat. sg. with tibi)
glossary.felicissima: fēlīx, fēlīcis — most fortunate, happiest (superlative fēlīcissimus, -a, -um; fem. nom./abl. sg. or neut. nom./acc. pl.; here fem. nom. sg. with a partitive genitive, 'happiest of mothers')
glossary.felixque: fēlīx, fēlīcis — fortunate, blessed, lucky (3rd decl. adjective, masc./fem. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.ferula: ferula, -ae f. — giant fennel stalk, cane, staff (nom. or abl. sg.; here abl. of means, the fennel-staff Silenus props himself on)
glossary.ferum: ferus, -a, -um — wild, savage, cruel (masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.; here neut. acc. sg. with cor)
glossary.festum: fēstum, -ī n. — festival, feast day (neut. nom./acc. sg.; here acc. sg. with celebrare; the same form is also the masc. acc. / neut. of the adjective fēstus 'festive')
glossary.fibras: fibra, -ae f. — fibre, filament; in the body, tissue or entrails (acc. pl.)
glossary.fidibusque: fidēs, fidium f. pl. — lyre strings, the lyre (dat. or abl. pl.; a plural-only noun distinct from fidēs, fideī 'faith, trust') + -que 'and'
glossary.filum: fīlum, -ī n. — thread (neut. nom./acc. sg.; here acc. sg., the thread being drawn out)
glossary.fingite: fingō, fingere — to shape, mould; to imagine, suppose (2nd pl. present active imperative, 'suppose, imagine')
glossary.flectit: flectō, flectere — to bend, turn, wheel (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.flerunt: fleō, flēre, flēvī — to weep, weep for (3rd pl. perfect active indicative; syncopated flērunt for flēvērunt)
glossary.flesse: fleō, flēre, flēvī — to weep, weep for (perfect active infinitive; syncopated flēsse for flēvisse, 'to have wept'; here in indirect statement)
glossary.flet: fleō, flēre — to weep (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.foedat: foedō, foedāre — to befoul, defile, disfigure (3rd sg. present active indicative)
glossary.formosissimus: fōrmōsus, -a, -um — beautiful, shapely; superlative fōrmōsissimus, most beautiful (masc. nom. sg.)
glossary.fortiter: fortiter — bravely, strongly, firmly (adverb from fortis; here with non, 'none too steadily')
glossary.frenis: frēnum, -ī n. — bridle, reins (dat. or abl. pl.; the plural comes both as neuter frēna and as masculine frēnī; here abl. with pictis)
glossary.frondentes: frondēns, -entis (pres. part. of frondeō, be in leaf) — leafy, in leaf, green with foliage (nom. or acc. pl. m./f.; here acc. pl. m. with thyrsos)
glossary.fruticosa: fruticōsus, -a, -um — bushy, shrubby, full of shoots (nom. or abl. sg. f., or nom./acc. pl. n.; here acc. pl. n. of the shrubby withies gathered)
glossary.fugiens: fugiō, -ere, fūgī — flee, run from (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m./f./n. or acc. sg. n.; here nom. sg. f.)
glossary.gemelliparae: gemellipara, -ae f. adj. — twin-bearing, mother of twins (a coined epithet of Lātōna; gen. or dat. sg. f., or nom. pl. f.; here gen. sg. f. with dīvae)
glossary.generosque: gener, generī m. — son-in-law (acc. pl. + -que; from gener, not from generōsus 'noble')
glossary.genialis: geniālis, -e — festive, joy-bringing, belonging to the genius of a marriage (nom. sg. m./f. or gen. sg. of any gender; here nom. sg. m. with consitor)
glossary.genitis: genitus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of gignō, beget) — born, begotten; as noun, offspring (dat. or abl. pl. m./n.; here abl. pl. m. used as a noun, of sons born to someone)
glossary.gentisque: gēns, gentis f. — clan, people, nation (gen. sg. + -que; gentis is also a poetic acc. pl. for gentēs — here it is the genitive singular)
glossary.glorior: glōrior, glōriārī, glōriātus sum — boast, take pride in (1st sg. pres. indic.; deponent, so passive in form but active in sense, and it takes an ablative of what one boasts of)
glossary.graias: Graius, -a, -um — Greek, of the Greeks (acc. pl. f.)
glossary.gressus: gressus, -ūs m. — step, tread, course of walking (nom. sg. or acc. pl. of the 4th-decl. noun; identical in form to gressus, perf. part. of gradior 'having stepped' — here the noun, acc. pl.)
glossary.habeat: habeō, -ēre, habuī — have, hold; regard as (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.; here in an indirect question)
glossary.haberent: habeō, -ēre, habuī — have, hold (3rd pl. imperf. subj. act.; here in a subordinate clause inside a wish/characterizing clause)
glossary.hauriret: hauriō, -īre, hausī — draw up, drain, swallow, drink down (3rd sg. imperf. subj. act.; here in a purpose clause with ut)
glossary.iacchus: Iacchus, -ī m. — Iacchus, a cult name of Bacchus, called out in the mysteries (nom. sg.)
glossary.ignigenamque: ignigena, -ae m. — the fire-born one, a coined epithet of Bacchus (born from the lightning that killed Semele); 1st-decl. masc., acc. sg. + -que
glossary.ignobilitate: ignōbilitās, -ātis f. — obscurity, lack of renown, low birth (abl. sg.; here abl. of cause)
glossary.ilioneus: Īlioneus, -eī m. — Ilioneus, the youngest of Niobe's sons (nom. sg.)
glossary.imbris: imber, imbris m. — rain, rainstorm, shower (gen. sg.; imbris also serves as a poetic acc. pl. for imbrēs — here the genitive, dependent on an adjective of foreknowledge)
glossary.impatiensque: impatiēns, -entis — unable to bear, impatient of (+ gen.); nom. or acc. sg. m./f. + -que; here nom. sg. m. with a genitive of what is not endured
glossary.impensius: impēnsius — more lavishly, more earnestly, at greater cost (compar. adv. of impēnsē; the same form is nom./acc. sg. n. of the compar. adj. impēnsior — here adverbial)
glossary.imposito: impositus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of impōnō, place upon) — set on, laid upon (dat. or abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. sg. n., agreeing with a neuter ablative, while the person it is laid on stands in the dative)
glossary.impositum: impositus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of impōnō) — set in place, put on (nom. sg. n. or acc. sg. m./n.; here nom. sg. n. with est, forming the perf. pass. 'was set in place')
glossary.imposuere: impōnō, -ere, imposuī — place upon, set on, impose (3rd pl. perf. indic. act.; -ēre is the alternative ending for -ērunt, so imposuere = imposuērunt)
glossary.inconsumpta: incōnsūmptus, -a, -um — unconsumed, undiminished, never used up (nom. or abl. sg. f., or nom./acc. pl. n.; here nom. sg. f. as predicate with est)
glossary.incumbens: incumbō, -ere, -cubuī — lean on, rest upon, throw oneself onto (+ dat.); pres. act. part., nom. sg. m./f./n. or acc. sg. n.; here nom. sg. f.
glossary.incumbit: incumbō, -ere, -cubuī — lean on, throw oneself upon (+ dat.); 3rd sg. pres. indic. act.
glossary.incurvata: incurvō, -āre — bend, curve; perf. pass. part. incurvātus, bent, doubled over (nom. or abl. sg. f., or nom./acc. pl. n.; here with a neuter plural, of limbs bent by grief)
glossary.indetonsusque: indetōnsus, -a, -um — unshorn, with hair never cut (a rare compound, epithet of Bacchus; nom. sg. m. + -que)
glossary.indigenaeve: indigena, -ae m./f. — native, born in the land (used adjectivally; nom. pl. m. here with deī, + the enclitic -ve 'or'; gen./dat. sg. and nom. pl. share this form)
glossary.indignata: indignor, -ārī, indignātus sum — be indignant, take offence; perf. part. of a deponent, so active in sense: 'having grown indignant' (nom. sg. f. here; also abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.indignis: indignus, -a, -um — unworthy, undeserving; as noun, the unworthy (dat. or abl. pl.; here dat. pl. m. with a verb of entreating)
glossary.infecta: two lemmas collide here: īnfectus, -a, -um (in- + factus) — unfinished, undone, not carried through; and īnfectus, perf. pass. part. of īnficiō — dyed, stained. Here the first, of rites left unfinished (nom./acc. pl. n.; the form is also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.infectaque: same collision as infecta: īnfectus, -a, -um — unfinished, unworked (in- + factus); or īnfectus, perf. part. of īnficiō — dyed, stained. Here the first, of wool not yet spun (acc. pl. n. + -que)
glossary.inflataque: īnflō, -āre — blow into, puff up; perf. pass. part. īnflātus, swollen, puffed out (nom. pl. n. here with a neuter plural subject, + -que; also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.ingemuere: ingemō, -ere, ingemuī — groan, groan aloud at (3rd pl. perf. indic. act.; -ēre for -ērunt, so ingemuere = ingemuērunt)
glossary.ingrederis: ingredior, -gredī, -gressus sum — enter, step in, advance (2nd sg. pres. indic.; deponent, passive in form and active in sense — the future would be ingrediēris)
glossary.inmaduit: immadēscō, -ere, immaduī — grow wet, become soaked (3rd sg. perf. indic. act.; the edition prints inm- for imm-, the older unassimilated spelling)
glossary.inmensae: immēnsus, -a, -um — measureless, boundless, immense (gen. or dat. sg. f., or nom. pl. f.; here nom. pl. f. with a feminine plural noun; edition prints inm- for imm-)
glossary.inmoritur: immorior, -morī, -mortuus sum — die upon, die on top of (+ dat.); 3rd sg. pres. indic., deponent; edition prints inm- for imm-
glossary.inmota: immōtus, -a, -um — unmoved, motionless, fixed (nom. or abl. sg. f., or nom./acc. pl. n.; here nom. pl. n. of eyes standing fixed; edition prints inm- for imm-)
glossary.inmunesque: immūnis, -e — exempt from, free of (+ gen.); nom. or acc. pl. m./f. + -que; here acc. pl. f., of women released from their tasks; edition prints inm- for imm-
glossary.innectite: innectō, -ere, innexuī — bind on, weave around, entwine (2nd pl. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.inpietatis: impietās, -ātis f. — impiety, irreverence toward the gods (gen. sg.; edition prints inp- for imp-, the older unassimilated spelling)
glossary.inpulsaque: impellō, -ere, impulī — strike, drive against; perf. pass. part. impulsus, struck, beaten (nom. pl. n. here with a neuter plural subject, + -que; also nom. or abl. sg. f.; edition prints inp- for imp-)
glossary.instabilemque: instabilis, -e — unsteady, shifting, giving no firm footing (acc. sg. m./f. + -que; here m., of a floating place)
glossary.intempestiva: intempestīvus, -a, -um — untimely, ill-timed, out of season (nom. or abl. sg. f., or nom./acc. pl. n.; here acc. pl. n. with a neuter plural noun)
glossary.intercepta: intercipiō, -ere, -cēpī — cut off, take away in transit; perf. pass. part. interceptus, cut off, swallowed up (nom./acc. pl. n. here with a neuter plural subject; also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.interdixit: interdīcō, -ere, -dīxī — forbid, debar someone (dat.) from something (abl., in poetry also acc.); 3rd sg. perf. indic. act.
glossary.interius: interius — further inside, deeper within (adv., the compar. neut. of interior used adverbially; the same form is also nom./acc. sg. n. of the adj. interior, inner)
glossary.internodia: internōdium, -ī n. — the space between two joints, the length of limb between joints (nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl.)
glossary.intexto: intextus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of intexō, weave in) — woven in, inwrought, embroidered into (dat. or abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. sg. n.)
glossary.intonsum: intōnsus, -a, -um — unshorn, with hair uncut (nom. sg. n. or acc. sg. m./n.; here acc. sg. m., agreeing with a Greek accusative proper name)
glossary.intra: intrā — within, inside (prep. + acc.; also used as an adverb, 'inside'). Here the preposition governing an accusative
glossary.invidia: invidia, -ae f. — envy, ill-will; also the odium one incurs, being the object of hatred (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here abl. sg. in the idiom in invidiā esse, to be hated, to be the target of resentment)
glossary.ipsos: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, herself, the very, the actual thing itself (intensive pron./adj., acc. pl. m.)
glossary.irascentemque: īrāscor, īrāscī, īrātus sum — grow angry, be enraged; pres. part. of a deponent, active in sense (acc. sg. m./f. + -que; here f.)
glossary.ismenus: Ismēnus, -ī m. — Ismenus, the eldest of Niobe's sons (the name is also that of a Theban river); nom. sg.
glossary.iuguli: iugulum, -ī n. — the throat, the hollow at the base of the neck, collarbone (gen. sg. here; the byform iugulus, -ī m. would give the same shape as nom. pl.)
glossary.iuncis: iuncus, -ī m. — rush, reed (dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl. with cum)
glossary.iuncti: iungō, -ere, iūnxī — join, yoke; perf. pass. part. iūnctus, joined, locked together, interlocked (nom. pl. m. here, of a pair gripped together; also gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.iunoni: Iūnō, Iūnōnis f. — Juno, wife of Jupiter (dat. sg.)
glossary.iunxisse: iungō, -ere, iūnxī — join, fasten together (perf. act. infin.; here in indirect statement, 'that they joined')
glossary.iussaque: iussus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of iubeō) — ordered, commanded, bidden (nom./acc. pl. n. + -que; here acc. pl. n. with a neuter plural noun. The same form serves the noun iussum, -ī n. 'command', and nom./abl. sg. f. of the participle)
glossary.iuvenalia: iuvenālis, -e — youthful, of the young (nom. or acc. pl. n.; here acc. pl. n.)
glossary.iuvenalis: iuvenālis, -e — youthful, of the young (nom. sg. m./f. or gen. sg. of any gender; here nom. sg. m.)
glossary.iuventa: iuventa, -ae f. — youth, the season of youth (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here nom. sg. as subject with est)
glossary.lactantia: lactāns, -antis (pres. part. of lactō) — full of milk, milk-giving; the participle can also mean 'sucking milk', so context decides. Nom./acc. pl. n. here, of milk-filled udders
glossary.lacum: lacus, -ūs m. — lake, pool, standing water (acc. sg. of a 4th-decl. noun)
glossary.lana: lāna, -ae f. — wool (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here abl. sg., inside an ablative absolute)
glossary.laniataque: laniō, -āre — tear, mangle; perf. pass. part. laniātus, torn, lacerated (nom./acc. pl. n. + -que; here acc. pl. n. with a neuter plural noun; also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.lapsu: lāpsus, -ūs m. — a gliding, sweeping motion, fall (abl. sg. of the 4th-decl. noun; the same form is dat./abl. sg. of lāpsus, perf. part. of lābor 'having slipped' — here the noun)
glossary.lassataque: lassō, -āre — tire out; perf. pass. part. lassātus, wearied, exhausted (nom./acc. pl. n. + -que; here acc. pl. n. with a neuter plural noun; also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.lateque: lātē — widely, far and wide, over a broad space (adv. from lātus 'broad', + -que; not a case-form of the noun latus 'side')
glossary.latois: Lātōus, -a, -um — of Latona, Latona's (dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl. f. with altars sacred to her). Distinguish the related noun Lātōis, -idis f., 'daughter of Latona' (Diana)
glossary.latona: Lātōna, -ae f. — Latona (Greek Leto), mother of Apollo and Diana by Jupiter (nom. sg.; the identical form also serves the vocative, as in a direct address to her; the ablative would be Lātōnā)
glossary.latonae: Lātōna, -ae f. — Latona, mother of Apollo and Diana (gen. or dat. sg.; both occur in this work — dative with a verb of giving, genitive with a noun she governs)
glossary.latonam: Lātōna, -ae f. — Latona, mother of Apollo and Diana (acc. sg.)
glossary.latonigenisque: Lātōnigena, -ae m. — one born of Latona, i.e. Apollo or Diana (a coined 1st-decl. masc. compound; dat. or abl. pl. + -que; here dat. pl.)
glossary.latous: Lātōus, -ī m. — the son of Latona, i.e. Apollo (the adj. Lātōus, -a, -um used as a noun; nom. sg.)
glossary.lauroque: laurus, -ī (also -ūs) f. — laurel, bay-tree, bay branch (abl. sg. + -que)
glossary.laurumque: laurus, -ī (also -ūs) f. — laurel, bay branch (acc. sg. + -que)
glossary.lectos: lēctus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of legō, gather/choose) — chosen, picked out; as noun, chosen men (acc. pl. m.). The same spelling is acc. pl. of lectus, -ī m. 'bed, couch' — here the participle
glossary.lenaeo: Lēnaeus, -ī m. — Lenaeus, a cult name of Bacchus, god of the winepress (abl. sg.; also the adj. Lēnaeus, -a, -um, 'of the winepress', dat./abl. sg. m./n.)
glossary.levemus: levō, -āre — lighten, relieve, ease (1st pl. pres. subj. act., hortatory: 'let us lighten'). Distinct from lēvō, -āre 'make smooth'
glossary.limosoque: līmōsus, -a, -um — muddy, slimy, full of silt (dat. or abl. sg. m./n. + -que; here abl. sg. m.)
glossary.limum: līmus, -ī m. — mud, slime, silt (acc. sg.)
glossary.linguas: lingua, -ae f. — tongue; by extension, speech or language (acc. pl.)
glossary.liquidissimus: liquidus, -a, -um — clear, limpid, flowing pure; superl. liquidissimus, clearest (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.litibus: līs, lītis f. — quarrel, dispute, lawsuit (dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl.)
glossary.luctantia: luctor, -ārī, luctātus sum — wrestle, struggle; pres. part. of a deponent, active in sense: wrestling, straining (nom./acc. pl. n.; here acc. pl. n. with a neuter plural noun; also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.lyaeumque: Lyaeus, -ī m. — Lyaeus, 'the releaser', a cult name of Bacchus as loosener of care (acc. sg. + -que)
glossary.lycia: Lycia, -ae f. — Lycia, a region of south-western Asia Minor (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here abl. sg. with the preposition dē)
glossary.lyciae: Lycia, -ae f. — Lycia, a region of south-western Asia Minor (gen. or dat. sg.; here gen. sg. in both occurrences)
glossary.lycurgum: Lycūrgus, -ī m. — Lycurgus, the Thracian king who resisted Bacchus and was punished (acc. sg.)
glossary.lydia: Lȳdia, -ae f. — Lydia, a kingdom of western Asia Minor (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here nom. sg.)
glossary.mactas: mactō, -āre — slaughter as a sacrifice, immolate; also punish, strike down (2nd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.maeoniam: Maeonia, -ae f. — Maeonia, the older name for Lydia (acc. sg.; the adj. Maeonius, -a, -um would give the same form in acc. sg. f. — here the place-name, as object)
glossary.maestis: maestus, -a, -um — sad, sorrowful, mournful (dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl. f.)
glossary.magnique: magnus, -a, -um — great, large (gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m., + -que; here gen. sg. n. with a neuter genitive noun)
glossary.maledicere: maledīcō, -ere, -dīxī — speak ill of, revile, abuse (+ dat.); pres. act. infin. here, dependent on a verb of trying. The same form is also 2nd sg. pres. pass. indic.
glossary.maligno: malignus, -a, -um — spiteful, malicious, grudging, stinting (dat. or abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. sg. m.)
glossary.manebo: maneō, -ēre, mānsī — remain, stay, continue to be (1st sg. fut. indic. act.; here linking, with a predicate adjective)
glossary.manifestam: manifestus, -a, -um — plain, unmistakable, openly shown (acc. sg. f.)
glossary.manto: Mantō, Mantūs f. — Manto, the prophetic daughter of Tiresias (nom. sg.; a Greek name, not a form of maneō)
glossary.manuum: manus, -ūs f. — hand; also band, company (gen. pl. of the 4th decl.)
glossary.marmora: marmor, -oris n. — marble; a marble statue or surface (nom. or acc. pl.; here nom. pl. as subject)
glossary.marsya: Marsya (Marsyās), -ae m. — Marsyas, the satyr flayed by Apollo, and the Phrygian river named after him (Greek 1st-decl. masc.; nom. sg. here, of the river bearing the name)
glossary.matrum: māter, mātris f. — mother (gen. pl.; here partitive, 'of mothers')
glossary.mediam: medius, -a, -um — middle; in Latin idiom it agrees with its noun and means 'the middle of' it (acc. sg. f.; here with a preposition + accusative, 'through the middle of the city')
glossary.mediocris: mediocris, -e — middling, moderate, of no great size (gen. sg. of any gender here, with a genitive noun; the same form is also nom. sg. m./f. and a poetic acc. pl. for mediocrēs)
glossary.metuunt: metuō, -ere, metuī — fear, be afraid of (3rd pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.minasque: minae, -ārum f. pl. — threats, menaces (a plural-only noun; acc. pl. + -que)
glossary.minerva: Minerva, -ae f. — Minerva, goddess of crafts and of wool-work, and by metonymy the wool-work itself (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here abl. sg.)
glossary.minimamque: minimus, -a, -um — smallest, least, youngest (superl. of parvus; acc. sg. f. + -que)
glossary.minora: minor, minus — smaller, lesser, too small (compar. of parvus; nom. or acc. pl. n.; here acc. pl. n., with an ablative of comparison)
glossary.minoribus: minor, minus — smaller, lesser, humbler (compar. of parvus; dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl. n. governed by ūtor, which takes the ablative)
