glossary.minyeias: Mīnyēias, -adis f. — daughter of Minyas, the Minyeid (nom. sg. f., used as an epithet of one of Minyas' daughters)
glossary.minyeides: Mīnyēides, -um f. pl. — the daughters of Minyas, the Minyeids (nom. pl. of Mīnyēis; Greek declension)
glossary.miseram: miser, -era, -erum — wretched, pitiable, unhappy (acc. sg. f.)
glossary.mitisque: mītis, -e — gentle, mild, kindly disposed (nom. sg. m./f. + -que; here nom. sg. m., predicate with a verb of being present)
glossary.mittis: mittō, -ere, mīsī — send, cast, hurl (2nd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.moderantur: moderor, -ārī, moderātus sum — control, guide, hold in check (3rd pl. pres. indic.; deponent, active in sense; takes acc. or dat.)
glossary.mollem: mollis, -e — soft, yielding, pliant (acc. sg. m./f.; here m.)
glossary.mollierat: molliō, -īre, mollīvī — soften, make soft (3rd sg. pluperf. indic. act.)
glossary.montanum: montānus, -a, -um — of the mountains, mountain- (nom. sg. n. or acc. sg. m./n.; here nom. sg. n. with a neuter noun)
glossary.moribunda: moribundus, -a, -um — dying, at the point of death (nom. or abl. sg. f., or nom./acc. pl. n.; here nom. sg. f.)
glossary.moriente: morior, morī, mortuus sum — die; pres. part. moriēns, dying, failing (abl. sg. of any gender; here abl. sg. f.)
glossary.motasse: mōtō, -āre (frequentative of moveō) — keep moving, stir, agitate (syncopated perf. act. infin. = mōtāvisse; here in indirect statement after a verb of believing — the kind of contracted perfect a dictionary will not list)
glossary.movensque: moveō, -ēre, mōvī — move, stir; pres. act. part. movēns (nom. sg. m./f./n. or acc. sg. n., + -que; here nom. sg. f.)
glossary.nabat: nō, nāre, nāvī — swim, float, drift (3rd sg. imperf. indic. act.; a short 1st-conj. verb easily mistaken for a form of nāscor or nō- compounds)
glossary.narret: narrō, -āre — tell, relate, recount (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.; here in a deliberative indirect question, 'which she is to tell')
glossary.nectar: nectar, nectaris n. — nectar, the drink of the gods; anything supremely sweet (nom. or acc. sg.; here nom. sg. as predicate with erit)
glossary.negavit: negō, -āre — deny, refuse, say no (3rd sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.nervi: nervus, -ī m. — sinew, tendon; also a bowstring (nom. pl. here, as subject; the same form is gen. sg.)
glossary.nervosus: nervōsus, -a, -um — sinewy, full of tendons, muscular (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.nervus: nervus, -ī m. — bowstring; more generally sinew, cord (nom. sg.; here of the string of a bow)
glossary.nexu: nexus, -ūs m. — a binding, grip, coil, interlocking hold (abl. sg. of the 4th-decl. noun; identical to dat./abl. sg. of nexus, perf. part. of nectō — here the noun)
glossary.niobe: Niobē, -ēs f. — Niobe, daughter of Tantalus and wife of Amphion, whose boast of her children destroyed them (Greek declension; nom. sg. in each occurrence here)
glossary.nioben: Niobē, -ēs f. — Niobe (Greek acc. sg. in -ēn, the regular accusative of these Greek feminine names)
glossary.nitidae: nitidus, -a, -um — gleaming, sleek, glistening (as with oil) (gen., dat., or nom. pl. f.; here gen. sg. f.)
glossary.nocere: noceō, -ēre, nocuī — harm, injure (+ dat.); pres. act. infin.
glossary.norat: nōscō, -ere, nōvī — come to know; in the perfect system, 'know'. nōrat is the syncopated form of nōverat, 3rd sg. pluperf. indic. act., and carries simple past sense: 'she knew' (a contraction a reader will not find under nōscō in a dictionary)
glossary.novae: novus, -a, -um — new, newly made, fresh (gen., dat., or nom. pl. f.; here nom. pl. f.)
glossary.noverca: noverca, -ae f. — stepmother (nom. sg. or abl. sg.; here abl. sg., inside an ablative absolute with a participle-like adjective)
glossary.nudum: nūdus, -a, -um — bare, naked, exposed (nom. sg. n. or acc. sg. m./n.; here nom. sg. n. with a neuter subject)
glossary.numerare: numerō, -āre — count, number, reckon up (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.numerum: numerus, -ī m. — number, count, tally (acc. sg.)
glossary.nycteliusque: Nyctelius, -ī m. — Nyctelius, 'god of the night rites', a cult name of Bacchus (nom. sg. + -que)
glossary.nyseus: Nȳseus, -eī m. — Nyseus, a cult name of Bacchus from Nysa, where he was reared (nom. sg., Greek declension)
glossary.officio: officium, -ī n. — duty, obligation, an act of dutiful service (dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. sg. with a preposition)
glossary.optata: optō, -āre — wish for, pray for; perf. pass. part. optātus, wished for, prayed for, and as a noun optāta n. pl., one's prayers or wishes (nom./acc. pl. n. here, as a noun subject; also nom. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.orantem: ōrō, -āre — beg, plead, entreat; pres. act. part. ōrāns (acc. sg. m./f.; here f. in both occurrences, of a goddess pleading)
glossary.orbam: orbus, -a, -um — bereaved, deprived of children (acc. sg. f.; here predicative in an accusative-and-infinitive construction)
glossary.orgia: orgia, -ōrum n. pl. — the secret rites, the Bacchic mysteries (a plural-only noun; nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl. as object)
glossary.ornant: ōrnō, -āre — adorn, deck out, wreathe (3rd pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.ostendisse: ostendō, -ere, ostendī — show, expose, lay bare (perf. act. infin.; here in indirect statement)
glossary.palaestini: Palaestīnus, -a, -um — Palestinian, of Syria-Palestine; as a noun, the Palestinians (nom. pl. m. here as subject; the same form is gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.palaestrae: palaestra, -ae f. — the wrestling-ground, the palaestra; wrestling itself (gen., dat., or nom. pl.; here gen. sg.)
glossary.palude: palūs, palūdis f. — marsh, swamp, standing pool (abl. sg.)
glossary.pando: pandus, -a, -um — curved, bent, sway-backed (dat. or abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. sg. m.). Not to be confused with the verb pandō, -ere 'spread open', whose 1st sg. pres. is identical
glossary.parent: pāreō, -ēre, pāruī — obey, submit to (+ dat.); 3rd pl. pres. indic. act. here. The same spelling is also 3rd pl. pres. subj. of parō ('let them prepare') and of pariō ('let them bring forth') — context settles it
glossary.paretur: pāreō, -ēre, pāruī — obey; 3rd sg. pres. pass., used impersonally: 'obedience is given', 'she is obeyed'. The identical form belongs to parō ('is being prepared') and pariō, so the sense of the passage decides
glossary.pariturae: pariō, -ere, peperī — give birth, bring forth; fut. act. part. paritūrus, about to give birth (gen., dat., or nom. pl. f.; here dat. sg. f., of the one about to bear)
glossary.partis: pars, partis f. — part, portion, share (gen. sg. here; the same form is also a poetic acc. pl. for partēs, and coincides with forms of partior and partus)
glossary.pascere: pāscō, -ere, pāvī — feed, graze, feast (something) on; two parses share this form: pres. act. infin. 'to feed', and 2nd sg. pres. pass./middle imperative 'feed yourself, gorge yourself'. Here the imperative, paired with another 2nd-person imperative
glossary.patens: pateō, -ēre, patuī — lie open, stretch out; pres. act. part. patēns, open, extending (nom. sg. m./f./n. or acc. sg. n.; here nom. sg. m.)
glossary.paternam: paternus, -a, -um — a father's, paternal, inherited from the father (acc. sg. f.)
glossary.pelops: Pelops, Pelopis m. — Pelops, son of Tantalus, served to the gods and restored with an ivory shoulder (nom. sg.)
glossary.pendentiaque: pendeō, -ēre, pependī — hang, hang down; pres. act. part. pendēns (nom. or acc. pl. n. + -que; here acc. pl. n.)
glossary.pensa: pēnsum, -ī n. — the wool weighed out to a spinner, a day's allotment of spinning (nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl. as object). The same form is nom./abl. sg. f. of pēnsus, perf. part. of pendō 'weigh out'
glossary.perbibit: perbibō, -ere, perbibī — drink in, absorb thoroughly (3rd sg.; present and perfect are identical in this verb, since the perfect stem is bib- — here perfect, matching the perfect verb it is coordinated with)
glossary.perlucentes: perlūceō, -ēre — shine through, be transparent; pres. act. part. perlūcēns, translucent, showing through (nom. or acc. pl. m./f.; here acc. pl. f.)
glossary.phaedimus: Phaedimus, -ī m. — Phaedimus, one of Niobe's sons (nom. sg.)
glossary.phrygiae: two words share this form: the adj. Phrygius, -a, -um 'Phrygian' (gen./dat. sg. f. or nom. pl. f.) and the noun Phrygia, -ae f., the region of Phrygia (gen./dat. sg.). Both occur here — once nom. pl. f. of the adjective with a feminine plural noun, once gen. sg. of the country, 'of Phrygia'
glossary.phrygiaeque: Phrygia, -ae f. — Phrygia, a region of central Asia Minor (gen. sg. + -que here, 'and of Phrygia'; the form is also gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. f. of the adj. Phrygius, -a, -um)
glossary.phrygiis: Phrygius, -a, -um — Phrygian, of Phrygia (dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl. f.)
glossary.pio: pius, -a, -um — dutiful, devoted, righteous (dat./abl. sg. m./n.; in the poem abl. sg. n. with 'officio', 'in dutiful service'. Identical in spelling to piō, 1st sg. pres. of piāre 'appease')
glossary.placatus: plācātus, -a, -um (perf. pass. part. of plācō) — appeased, calmed, gracious (nom. sg. m.; used as a predicate adjective of a male addressee)
glossary.placerent: placeō, placēre — to please, be pleasing (to, + dat.) (3rd pl. imperf. subj. act.; here in a concessive 'quamvis' clause)
glossary.placuere: placeō, placēre — to please, seem good (3rd pl. perf. ind. act. = placuērunt; the poetic/alternative -ēre ending, not an infinitive)
glossary.plangens: plangō, plangere — to beat, strike (esp. the breast in mourning) (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m./f.; in the poem nom. sg. m.)
glossary.planus: plānus, -a, -um — level, flat, open (nom. sg. m.; not to be confused with the noun plānus 'vagrant, impostor')
glossary.pleiadum: Plēiades, -um (f. pl.) — the Pleiades, the seven daughters of Atlas set among the stars (gen. pl.)
glossary.ponite: pōnō, pōnere — to put, set down, lay aside (2nd pl. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.poples: poples, poplitis (m.) — the back of the knee, the knee, the ham (nom. sg., 3rd decl.)
glossary.popularis: populāris, -e — of the same people, fellow-countryman/countrywoman (3rd-decl. adj., freely used as a noun; the form is nom. or gen. sg. m./f. — in the poem gen. sg. f. in agreement with the Greek genitive 'Arachnes', 'of her townswoman Arachne'; a nom. sg. f. reading with 'poena' is also formally open)
glossary.populique: populus, -ī (m.) — a people, the populace, the crowd (+ enclitic -que 'and'; the form is gen. sg. or nom. pl. — in the poem gen. sg., 'the people's grief'. Distinguish pōpulus, -ī (f.) 'poplar tree', identical in spelling)
glossary.populum: populus, -ī (m.) — a people, the populace (acc. sg.; identical in spelling to pōpulum, acc. sg. of pōpulus (f.) 'poplar')
glossary.portasse: portō, portāre — to carry, bear (perf. act. inf., syncopated for portāvisse; here in indirect statement)
glossary.postponere: postpōnō, postpōnere — to place after, rank below (someone, + dat.) (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.potentibus: potēns, potentis — powerful, potent, effective (3rd-decl. adj., originally the pres. part. of possum; dat./abl. pl. of any gender — in the poem abl. pl. f. with 'herbis', 'with all-too-potent herbs')
glossary.potuissent: possum, posse, potuī — to be able, to have the power (3rd pl. pluperf. subj. act.; in the poem in a rhetorical question, 'whom would they not have been able to move?')
glossary.potura: pōtō, pōtāre — to drink (fut. act. part. pōtūrus, -a, -um; nom. sg. f., also possible as nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem nom. sg. f., 'meaning to drink, about to drink', expressing purpose; this participle serves as the future participle bibō lacks)
glossary.praeferre: praeferō, praeferre — to prefer, set before (someone, + dat.) (pres. act. inf.; irregular compound of ferō)
glossary.praeponere: praepōnō, praepōnere — to put before, prefer (something to something, acc. + dat.) (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.praescia: praescius, -a, -um — foreknowing, prophetic (usually + gen. of what is foreknown) (nom. sg. f.; also possible as nom./acc. pl. n. or abl. sg. f.)
glossary.praescius: praescius, -a, -um — foreknowing, having foreknowledge of (+ gen.) (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.praeterea: praetereā — besides, moreover, in addition (adverb; indeclinable)
glossary.premunt: premō, premere — to press, weigh down; of a rider, to bestride (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.primamque: prīmus, -a, -um — first, foremost, the eldest (+ enclitic -que 'and'; acc. sg. f., agreeing with the person told to speak first)
glossary.priora: prior, prius — earlier, former, previous (comparative adj., 3rd decl.; nom./acc. pl. n., commonly used as a noun 'earlier events' — in the poem acc. pl. n., object of the verb)
glossary.prodigio: prōdigium, -ī (n.) — a portent, marvel, prodigy (dat. or abl. sg. — in the poem abl., 'known for a marvel')
glossary.profectura: prōficiō, prōficere — to be of use, avail, accomplish something (fut. act. part. prōfectūrus, -a, -um; the form is nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem acc. pl. n. with 'bracchia', 'arms that were not going to avail'. Do not confuse with the part. of proficīscor 'set out')
glossary.proferre: prōferō, prōferre — to bring forth, put out, extend (pres. act. inf.; irregular compound of ferō)
glossary.progeniem: prōgeniēs, -ēī (f.) — offspring, descent, lineage (acc. sg., 5th decl.; in the poem subject accusative of an indirect statement)
glossary.prohibere: prohibeō, prohibēre — to hold back, prevent, keep off (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.prohibetis: prohibeō, prohibēre — to keep (someone) from, debar (often + abl. of the thing withheld) (2nd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.prope: prope — near, nearby (adverb); near, close to (preposition + acc.) (indeclinable; in the poem the preposition with 'moenia')
glossary.propere: properē — quickly, hastily, in haste (adverb, from properus)
glossary.proprium: proprius, -a, -um — one's own, personal, exclusive to one (the form is acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n. — in the poem acc. sg. m. with 'solem')
glossary.prosilit: prōsiliō, prōsilīre — to leap forth, spring out, spurt (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.; the perfect is prōsiluī, so this form is present, not perfect)
glossary.prospexit: prōspiciō, prōspicere — to look out at, catch sight of (3rd sg. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.puerpera: puerpera, -ae (f.) — a woman who has just given birth, a new mother (the form is nom. or abl. sg. — in the poem nom. sg., in apposition to the subject)
glossary.pulmonis: pulmō, pulmōnis (m.) — the lung (gen. sg., 3rd decl.)
glossary.pulsatus: pulsō, pulsāre — to beat, pound, strike repeatedly (perf. pass. part. pulsātus, -a, -um; nom. sg. m., 'pounded, beaten')
glossary.pulsoque: pellō, pellere, pepulī, pulsus — to drive out, banish (perf. pass. part. pulsus; + enclitic -que 'and'; dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. m. in an ablative absolute, 'shame driven off'. Identical in spelling to pulsō, 1st sg. pres. of pulsāre 'I beat')
glossary.quadrupedis: quadrupēs, quadrupedis (m./f./n.) — four-footed; as a noun, a four-footed beast, a horse (gen. sg.)
glossary.quaerite: quaerō, quaerere — to seek, ask, inquire (2nd pl. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.quamcumque: quīcumque, quaecumque, quodcumque — whoever, whatever, any... at all (acc. sg. f.; in the poem with 'partem', 'in whatever direction')
glossary.ranae: rāna, -ae (f.) — a frog (the form is gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — in the poem nom. pl.)
glossary.rauca: raucus, -a, -um — hoarse, harsh-sounding (the form is nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem nom. sg. f. with 'vox')
glossary.reccidat: recidō, recidere (re- + cadō) — to fall back, recoil (upon someone, + in + acc.) (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.; this edition prints the doubled -cc- of the compound, = recidat)
glossary.redigar: redigō, redigere — to bring back, reduce (to a number or condition) (1st sg., fut. ind. pass. or pres. subj. pass. — in the poem future, 'I shall not be reduced')
glossary.referamus: referō, referre — to bring back, report, relate (1st pl. pres. subj. act.; irregular compound of ferō; in the poem hortatory, 'let us bring back')
glossary.referat: referō, referre — to relate, recount (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.; in the poem in an indirect question, 'what she should relate')
glossary.reguntur: regō, regere — to rule, govern, direct (3rd pl. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.relanguit: relanguēscō, relanguēscere, relanguī — to grow faint, go slack, lose strength (3rd sg. perf. ind. act.; inceptive -scō verb, so the perfect means 'went limp')
glossary.relatis: referō, referre — to report, utter in reply (perf. pass. part. relātus, -a, -um; dat./abl. pl. of any gender — in the poem abl. pl. n. in an ablative absolute, 'these words having been spoken'. The perfect stem rel- is suppletive; a reader will not find 'relatis' under referō in a dictionary)
glossary.relevare: relevō, relevāre — to lighten, relieve, assuage (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.relinque: relinquō, relinquere — to leave, leave behind, spare (2nd sg. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.relinquet: relinquō, relinquere — to leave, leave behind (3rd sg. fut. ind. act.; note the -e-: the present is relinquit)
glossary.renarrant: renarrō, renarrāre — to tell over again, recount (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.repertis: reperiō, reperīre, repperī, repertus — to find, discover (perf. pass. part.; dat./abl. pl. of any gender — in the poem abl. pl. in an ablative absolute, 'others having been found')
glossary.reponunt: repōnō, repōnere — to put back, lay aside, store away (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.resedit: resīdō, resīdere, resēdī — to sit down, settle, sink down (3rd sg. perf. ind. act.; long -ē- marks the perfect, since the present is resīdit. The same form can also be perf. of resideō 'remain sitting')
glossary.revocabile: revocābilis, -e — able to be called back, recallable (nom./acc. sg. n. — in the poem nom. sg. n. with 'telum')
glossary.ripam: rīpa, -ae (f.) — the bank of a river or pool (acc. sg.)
glossary.rogabam: rogō, rogāre — to ask, inquire (1st sg. imperf. ind. act.; here governing an indirect question)
glossary.rogandos: rogō, rogāre — to ask, entreat (gerundive rogandus, -a, -um 'to be entreated, needing to be asked'; acc. pl. m., in the poem with 'esse' in indirect statement)
glossary.rubentia: rubeō, rubēre — to be red, glow red (pres. act. part. rubēns, -entis; nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem acc. pl. n. agreeing with 'terga' in the following line)
glossary.ruricolae: rūricola, -ae (m.) — a country-dweller, tiller of the fields (1st decl. but masculine; the form is gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — in the poem nom. pl.)
glossary.sacri: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, consecrated; as a noun sacrum, -ī (n.) 'a rite, sacrifice' (the form is gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m. — in the poem gen. sg. n. of the noun, partitive with 'satis', 'enough of the rite')
glossary.sacrilegos: sacrilegus, -a, -um — sacrilegious, temple-robbing; as a noun, a profaner (acc. pl. m., used substantively)
glossary.salientia: saliō, salīre — to leap, spring, throb (pres. act. part. saliēns, -entis; nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem acc. pl. n. with 'viscera', 'the throbbing innards')
glossary.saliunt: saliō, salīre — to leap, jump (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.sanctis: sānctus, -a, -um (perf. part. of sanciō, used as an adj.) — holy, hallowed, inviolable (dat./abl. pl. of any gender — in the poem dat. pl. f. with 'flammis', 'to the holy flames')
glossary.sarcina: sarcina, -ae (f.) — a bundle, pack, burden (the form is nom. or abl. sg. — in the poem nom. sg., predicate: '[who] was once a burden to his mother')
glossary.satam: serō, serere, sēvī, satus — to sow, plant, beget (perf. pass. part. satus, -a, -um 'sown, born of', regularly with abl. of the parent; acc. sg. f.)
glossary.satia: satiō, satiāre — to satisfy, glut, sate (2nd sg. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.satiaque: satiō, satiāre — to satisfy, glut, sate (2nd sg. pres. imperative act. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.satumque: serō, serere, sēvī, satus — to sow, beget (perf. pass. part. satus, -a, -um 'begotten, born'; + enclitic -que 'and'; acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n. — in the poem acc. sg. m., a cult-epithet, 'the twice-begotten one')
glossary.septima: septimus, -a, -um — seventh (ordinal numeral; the form is nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem nom. sg. f. with 'pars')
glossary.sequente: sequor, sequī (deponent) — to follow (pres. act. part. sequēns, -entis, active in sense; abl. sg. of any gender — in the poem abl. sg. f. in an ablative absolute)
glossary.sermonibus: sermō, sermōnis (m.) — talk, conversation, common report (dat./abl. pl. — in the poem abl. pl., 'fills the world with talk')
glossary.sidereo: sīdereus, -a, -um — starry, belonging to the heavenly bodies; of the sun (dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. m. with 'aestu')
glossary.simili: similis, -e — like, similar (to, + gen. or dat.) (3rd-decl. adj.; dat. or abl. sg. of any gender — in the poem abl. sg. n. with 'murmure')
glossary.sinat: sinō, sinere — to allow, permit, let (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.sinistro: sinister, sinistra, sinistrum — left, on the left side (dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. m. with 'umero', 'on the left shoulder')
glossary.sipylumque: Sipylus, -ī (m.) — Sipylus, the Lydian mountain where Niobe's family was at home (acc. sg. + enclitic -que 'and'; the same name also belongs to one of Niobe's sons)
glossary.sipylus: Sipylus, -ī (m.) — Sipylus, one of Niobe's sons (nom. sg.; the same name belongs to the Lydian mountain elsewhere in the poem)
glossary.socero: socer, socerī (m.) — father-in-law (dat./abl. sg. — in the poem abl. sg., with a verb of boasting)
glossary.sociasque: socius, -a, -um — allied, sharing, companion (acc. pl. f. + enclitic -que 'and'; identical in spelling to sociās, 2nd sg. pres. of sociāre 'to join')
glossary.solae: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only (pronominal declension: gen. sg. sōlīus, dat. sg. sōlī; the form here is gen./dat. sg. f. or nom. pl. f. — in the poem nom. pl. f.)
glossary.solari: sōlor, sōlārī (deponent) — to console, comfort, soothe (pres. inf., active in meaning despite the passive form; identical in spelling to sōlāris, -e 'of the sun', dat./abl. sg.)
glossary.soli: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only (pronominal dat. sg. sōlī of any gender, or nom. pl. m. — in the poem dat. sg. m., 'to him alone'. Identical in spelling to sōlī, dat. of sōl 'sun', and to solī from solum 'ground')
glossary.solumque: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only, sole (+ enclitic -que 'and'; acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n. — in the poem acc. sg. m. Distinguish the adverb sōlum 'only' and the noun solum, -ī (n.) 'ground, soil', identical in spelling)
glossary.solvere: solvō, solvere — to loosen, untie, let down (pres. act. inf. — in the poem an infinitive; the same spelling can also be 3rd pl. perf. ind. act. solvēre = solvērunt)
glossary.spectantur: spectō, spectāre — to look at, behold, be on view (3rd pl. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.spina: spīna, -ae (f.) — the backbone, spine; also a thorn (the form is nom. or abl. sg. — in the poem nom. sg.)
glossary.spiritus: spīritus, -ūs (m.) — breath, the breath of life (4th decl.; the form is nom. sg., gen. sg., or nom./acc. pl. — in the poem nom. sg.)
glossary.spoliata: spoliō, spoliāre — to strip, rob, despoil (perf. pass. part. spoliātus, -a, -um; nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem nom. sg. f., of the speaker)
glossary.sprevere: spernō, spernere, sprēvī — to scorn, reject, despise (3rd pl. perf. ind. act. = sprēvērunt; the alternative -ēre ending, not an infinitive)
glossary.spumantiaque: spūmō, spūmāre — to foam, froth (pres. act. part. spūmāns, -antis; + enclitic -que 'and'; nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem acc. pl. n. with 'ora')
glossary.stagno: stāgnum, -ī (n.) — a pool, standing water, still water (dat./abl. sg. — in the poem abl. sg. Identical in spelling to stāgnō, 1st sg. pres. of stāgnāre 'to form a pool')
glossary.stagnumque: stāgnum, -ī (n.) — a pool, standing water (nom./acc. sg. + enclitic -que 'and' — in the poem acc. sg.)
glossary.subiectas: subiciō, subicere, subiectus — to throw or place under (perf. pass. part.; acc. pl. f., 'lying underneath')
glossary.submergere: submergō, submergere — to plunge under, sink, submerge (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.submoverat: submoveō, submovēre — to drive off, remove, clear away (3rd sg. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.succurritis: succurrō, succurrere — to run to help, come to the aid of (+ dat.) (2nd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.sumere: sūmō, sūmere — to take up, pick up, assume (pres. act. inf.; the perfect stem is sūmps-, so this form is unambiguously the infinitive)
glossary.summique: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost, the top of (superlative of superus; + enclitic -que 'and'; gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m. — in the poem gen. sg. m. with 'lacerti', 'of the top of the arm')
glossary.summoque: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost (+ enclitic -que 'and'; dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. m. with 'in vertice', 'on the highest peak')
glossary.summos: summus, -a, -um — topmost, uppermost, the surface of (acc. pl. m.; in the poem with 'artus', i.e. the outer surface of the limbs)
glossary.superbos: superbus, -a, -um — proud, haughty, arrogant (acc. pl. m.)
glossary.supplicat: supplicō, supplicāre — to beseech, entreat, make supplication (to, + dat.) (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.suprema: suprēmus, -a, -um — last, final, highest (superlative of superus; the form is nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem acc. pl. n. both times, with 'lumina' and with 'oscula')
glossary.tacito: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, unspoken, noiseless (originally perf. part. of taceō; dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. n. with 'murmure')
glossary.tangunt: tangō, tangere — to touch, reach (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.tantalis: Tantalis, -idis (f.) — the daughter of Tantalus, i.e. Niobe (Greek patronymic, nom. sg.)
glossary.tantalus: Tantalus, -ī (m.) — Tantalus (nom. sg.); in the poem both Niobe's father, the son of Jupiter, and one of Niobe's own sons named after him
glossary.tegens: tegō, tegere — to cover, shield, screen (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m./f. — in the poem nom. sg. f.)
glossary.telasque: tēla, -ae (f.) — a web, warp, piece of weaving on the loom (acc. pl. + enclitic -que 'and'; distinct from tēlum, -ī (n.) 'weapon, missile')
glossary.tendebant: tendō, tendere — to stretch out, hold out (3rd pl. imperf. ind. act.)
glossary.tendunt: tendō, tendere — to stretch out, extend (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.tento: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentus — to stretch, draw tight (perf. pass. part. tentus, -a, -um 'taut, drawn'; dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. m. with 'nervo', 'from the taut string'. Identical in spelling to tentō, 1st sg. pres. of tentō/temptō 'I try', a genuine trap here)
glossary.terebrata: terebrō, terebrāre — to bore through, pierce (perf. pass. part. terebrātus, -a, -um; nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem nom. sg. f. with 'aura')
glossary.thebaides: Thēbāis, -idos (f.) — a Theban woman (Greek patronymic-type noun; nom. pl. Thēbāides)
glossary.thyoneus: Thyōneus, -eī (m.) — Thyoneus, a cult title of Bacchus as son of Thyone, the deified Semele (nom. sg.)
glossary.timent: timeō, timēre — to fear, be afraid (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.tingitur: tingō, tingere — to dip, wet, dye (3rd sg. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.tiresia: Tīresiās, -ae (m.) — Tiresias, the blind Theban seer (Greek 1st-decl. masculine; the form is abl. or voc. sg. — in the poem abl. sg. of origin with a participle of birth, 'born of Tiresias')
glossary.titanida: Tītānis, -idos (f.) — a Titaness, i.e. Latona, daughter of the Titan Coeus (Greek acc. sg. in -ida)
glossary.titubantes: titubō, titubāre — to stagger, totter, reel (pres. act. part. titubāns, -antis; nom./acc. pl. m./f. — in the poem acc. pl. m. with 'artus')
glossary.tollensque: tollō, tollere — to lift, raise (pres. act. part. + enclitic -que 'and'; nom. sg. m./f. — in the poem nom. sg. f.)
glossary.toros: torus, -ī (m.) — a couch, bed; a bier laid out for the dead (acc. pl.)
glossary.trahens: trahō, trahere — to drag, draw, pull out (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m./f. — in the poem nom. sg. f.)
glossary.trahere: trahō, trahere — to draw out, pull (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.transierant: trānseō, trānsīre — to cross over, pass on (to something else) (3rd pl. pluperf. ind. act.; compound of eō, perf. stem trānsi-)
glossary.tremens: tremō, tremere — to tremble, quiver, shake (pres. act. part., nom. sg. of any gender — in the poem nom. sg. f. with 'sagitta')
glossary.trepidaeque: trepidus, -a, -um — trembling, quivering, agitated (+ enclitic -que 'and'; gen./dat. sg. f. or nom. pl. f. — in the poem nom. pl. f. with 'venae')
glossary.tritoniaca: Trītōniacus, -a, -um — of Tritonia, i.e. belonging to Minerva (from her cult title Trītōnia) (nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem abl. sg. f. with 'harundine', 'with Minerva's reed-pipe')
glossary.triumpha: triumphō, triumphāre — to triumph, celebrate a triumph, exult in victory (2nd sg. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.tulerat: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātus — to bear, carry; with 'gressus', to direct one's steps (3rd sg. pluperf. ind. act.; the perfect stem tul- is suppletive and will not be found under 'tulerat' in a dictionary)
glossary.tumescunt: tumēscō, tumēscere — to begin to swell, swell up (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.; inceptive -scō verb)
glossary.turbantes: turbō, turbāre — to disturb, throw into confusion, disrupt (pres. act. part. turbāns, -antis; nom. pl. m./f. or acc. pl. m./f. — in the poem nom. pl. f., of the daughters of Minyas)
glossary.turbavere: turbō, turbāre — to stir up, muddy, agitate (3rd pl. perf. ind. act. = turbāvērunt; the alternative -ēre ending, not an infinitive)
glossary.ture: tūs, tūris (n.) — incense, frankincense (abl. sg., 3rd decl.; often spelled thūs)
glossary.tutam: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, secure, out of danger (acc. sg. f.)
glossary.tyrioque: Tyrius, -a, -um — Tyrian, of Tyre; hence purple, since Tyre made the dye (+ enclitic -que 'and'; dat./abl. sg. m./n. — in the poem abl. sg. m. with 'suco')
glossary.tyrrhenaque: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan (+ enclitic -que 'and'; nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. — in the poem acc. pl. n. with 'corpora' in the following line)
glossary.uberaque: ūber, ūberis (n.) — an udder, teat, breast (+ enclitic -que 'and'; nom./acc. pl. — in the poem acc. pl. Distinguish the adjective ūber, ūberis 'fertile, rich')
glossary.umeroque: umerus, -ī (m.) — the shoulder (+ enclitic -que 'and'; dat./abl. sg. — in the poem abl. sg.; this edition prints the unaspirated umerus, commonly spelled humerus elsewhere)
glossary.umerum: umerus, -ī (m.) — the shoulder (acc. sg.; also spelled humerus)
glossary.umerus: umerus, -ī (m.) — the shoulder (nom. sg.; also spelled humerus)
glossary.umore: ūmor, ūmōris (m.) — moisture, liquid, fluid (abl. sg.; also spelled humor. In the poem the ablative required by careō 'lack')
glossary.ureret: ūrō, ūrere — to burn, scorch, parch (3rd sg. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.urgent: urgeō, urgēre — to press, drive, urge on (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.uteri: uterus, -ī (m.) — the womb, belly (gen. sg. or nom. pl. — in the poem gen. sg., 'a part of my womb')
glossary.uvae: ūva, -ae (f.) — a grape, a cluster of grapes; the vine (gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — in the poem gen. sg., 'planter of the grape')
glossary.vacuas: vacuus, -a, -um — empty, unoccupied, free, idle (acc. pl. f. — in the poem twice, with 'aures' and with 'auras'. Identical in spelling to vacuās, 2nd sg. pres. of vacuāre 'to empty')
glossary.validi: validus, -a, -um — strong, powerful, vigorous (gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m. — in the poem gen. sg. m. with 'venti')
glossary.vaticinata: vāticinor, vāticinārī (deponent) — to prophesy, foretell (perf. part. vāticinātus, -a, -um, active in meaning: 'having prophesied' and able to take an object; nom. sg. f. — in the poem nom. sg. f.)
glossary.vaticinatus: vāticinor, vāticinārī (deponent) — to prophesy, foretell (perf. part., nom. sg. m., active in meaning; with a form of sum it makes the perfect/pluperfect, 'had prophesied')
glossary.velantibus: vēlō, vēlāre — to veil, cover, clothe (pres. act. part. vēlāns, -antis; dat./abl. pl. of any gender — in the poem abl. pl. f. with 'squamis', 'with scales covering her limbs')
glossary.venerande: veneror, venerārī (deponent) — to revere, worship (gerundive venerandus, -a, -um used as an adjective, 'to be revered, worshipful'; voc. sg. m., addressing the god)
glossary.verbisque: verbum, -ī (n.) — a word, utterance (+ enclitic -que 'and'; dat./abl. pl. — in the poem abl. pl.)
glossary.versant: versō, versāre — to turn, twist, keep turning (frequentative of vertō) (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.versarunt: versō, versāre — to turn, roll, twist (3rd pl. perf. ind. act., syncopated for versāvērunt; in the poem 'they rolled their eyes')
glossary.verterit: vertō, vertere, vertī — to turn, change, transform (something into something, in + acc.) (3rd sg., perf. subj. act. or fut. perf. ind. act. — in the poem perf. subj. in an indirect question)
glossary.vetantes: vetō, vetāre — to forbid, refuse, prohibit (pres. act. part. vetāns, -antis; nom./acc. pl. m./f. — in the poem acc. pl. m., 'those who forbade her')
glossary.victrixque: victrīx, victrīcis (f.) — a victress, a woman who conquers; as adj., victorious (+ enclitic -que 'and'; nom. sg.)
glossary.victum: vincō, vincere, vīcī, victus — to conquer, defeat, overcome (perf. pass. part. victus, -a, -um; acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n. — in the poem acc. sg. m., 'him, defeated'. Identical in spelling to victum, acc. sg. of victus, -ūs (m.) 'food, sustenance')
glossary.vimina: vīmen, vīminis (n.) — an osier, pliant twig, withe (nom./acc. pl. — in the poem acc. pl.)
glossary.vinco: vincō, vincere — to conquer, win, prevail (1st sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.viret: vireō, virēre — to be green, be verdant, flourish (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.viroque: vir, virī (m.) — a man; a husband (+ enclitic -que 'and'; dat./abl. sg. — in the poem abl. sg., 'by me and by my husband')
glossary.virque: vir, virī (m.) — a man; a husband (nom. sg. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.virumque: vir, virī (m.) — a man; a husband (+ enclitic -que 'and'; acc. sg. — in the poem acc. sg., 'her husband'. The same spelling also serves as the contracted gen. pl. virum = virōrum)
glossary.viscere: viscus, visceris (n.) — flesh, an inner organ; in the plural viscera, the vitals, entrails (abl. sg. — in the poem 'sticking in her flesh')
glossary.vivatis: vīvō, vīvere — to live, be alive (2nd pl. pres. subj. act.; in the poem jussive, 'may you live')
glossary.vulgaris: vulgāris, -e — common, ordinary, widely known (3rd-decl. adj.; nom. sg. of any gender or gen. sg. — in the poem nom. sg. f. with 'fabula'. Identical in spelling to vulgāris, 2nd sg. pres. pass. of vulgāre 'to make public')
glossary.abdit: abdō — hides, conceals, puts out of sight (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.absentes: absēns, -entis (absum) — absent, away (pres. part. of absum used as adjective/noun; the form is nom. or acc. pl. m./f. — here acc. pl., of people spoken of as away)
glossary.abstulerunt: auferō — took away, carried off, stripped away (3 pl. perf. act.)
glossary.accersite: accersō (= arcessō) — summon, fetch, send for (2 pl. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.actaea: Actaeus, -a, -um — Attic, Athenian (from Actē, the old name of Attica; f. nom. sg. here, with a f. noun; the form is also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.acto: agō — driven through, spent, completed (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.; here n. abl. in an ablative absolute of time, a year being completed)
glossary.acuti: acūtus, -a, -um — sharp; of sound, shrill, piercing (gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m.; here gen. sg. n., with 'aeris', of shrill bronze)
glossary.adduxit: addūcō — drew toward himself, pulled close (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.adflata: adflō (afflō) — breathed upon, blown upon, blasted (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., with 'est'; the form is also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.adhaeret: adhaereō — clings to, adjoins, is attached to (3 sg. pres. act.; takes the dative)
glossary.adhibet: adhibeō — brings up to, admits, invites (to a table) (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.admotumque: admoveō + -que — and (was) brought near, moved up (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg. with 'est'; the form is also m. acc. sg.)
glossary.admovet: admoveō — brings up, applies, offers (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.admovique: admoveō + -que — and I brought up, and I applied, and I offered (1 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.aenis: aēnum — bronze vessel, cauldron (n. dat./abl. pl., here abl.; a substantive of the adj. aēnus 'of bronze', whose dat./abl. pl. is spelled the same)
glossary.aerii: āerius, -a, -um — of the air, airy, high in the air (gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m.; here gen. sg. m., with 'cursus')
glossary.agendum: agō — to be done, to be dealt with, to be gone about (gerundive, n. nom. sg.; with 'est', 'this is not to be done')
glossary.agitata: agitō — driven, harried, goaded (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; the form is also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.agitati: agitō — stirred up, fanned, driven about (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.; the form is also gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.agitque: agō + -que — and renders, and drives, and does (3 sg. pres. act.; with 'grates' it is the idiom 'render thanks')
glossary.ambarum: ambō, ambae, ambō — both, the pair (f. gen. pl.)
glossary.ambos: ambō, ambae, ambō — both, the pair (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.amplectitur: amplector — embraces, throws her arms around (3 sg. pres. of a deponent; passive in form, active in meaning)
glossary.amplexumque: amplexus, -ūs + -que — and an embrace (m. acc. sg.; identical in spelling to amplexum, the perf. part. of the deponent amplector, 'having embraced' — here the noun)
glossary.animaeque: anima + -que — and of the life-breath, of the soul (f.; the form is gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — here gen. sg., partitive with 'aliquid', something of life)
glossary.animosque: animus + -que — and spirit, passion, fierce temper (m. acc. pl.; the plural often of high or violent spirits rather than 'minds')
glossary.argosque: Argos + -que — and Argos, city of the Argolid in the Peloponnese (n., Greek, indeclinable in the sg.; here nom.)
glossary.arreptamque: arripiō + -que — and (her), seized, snatched up (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.arserunt: ārdeō — blazed, burned (3 pl. perf. act.)
glossary.artificem: artifex, -ficis — craftsman; contriver, author of a deed (m./f. acc. sg.; also used adjectivally, 'artful, cunning')
glossary.ast: ast — but (conjunction; archaic and poetic form of 'at')
glossary.atras: āter, ātra, ātrum — black, dark; of mourning, funereal (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.attonitamque: attonō + -que — and (her), thunderstruck, stunned, dazed (perf. pass. part. used as adjective, f. acc. sg.)
glossary.attulit: afferō (adferō) — brought, brought to (3 sg. perf. act.; with 'salutem', brought a greeting)
glossary.audiet: audiō — will hear (3 sg. fut. act.)
glossary.ausim: audeō — I would dare (1 sg.; 'ausim' is an old aorist-optative form used as a potential subjunctive beside 'audeam')
glossary.ausit: audeō — he would dare, he might venture (3 sg.; 'ausit' is the old subjunctive form beside 'audeat')
glossary.avidosque: avidus, -a, -um + -que — and greedy, ravenous, eager (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.avito: avītus, -a, -um — of a grandfather, ancestral, inherited (dat./abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. n., with a n. noun)
glossary.barbaque: barba + -que — and the beard (f. nom. sg.; the abl. sg. barbā is spelled the same)
glossary.barbara: barbarus, -a, -um — foreign, non-Greek, barbarian (n. nom./acc. pl. here, with 'agmina'; the form is also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.barbare: barbarus — barbarian, savage (m. voc. sg. of the adjective used as a noun, in direct address; identical in spelling to the adverb barbarē, 'in foreign fashion')
glossary.barbarica: barbaricus, -a, -um — foreign, barbarian (f. nom./abl. sg. or n. nom./acc. pl.; here f. abl. sg., with 'tela', on a barbarian loom)
glossary.bello: bellum — war, warfare (n. dat./abl. sg.; here abl. of means, by war)
glossary.blanditiis: blanditia, usually pl. blanditiae — coaxing words, caresses, endearments (f. dat./abl. pl.; abl. in both places here — mingled with caresses, and achieved by coaxing)
glossary.boreae: Boreās — Boreas, the North Wind, personified as a god (m., Greek 1st decl.; the form is gen. or dat. sg. — here dat., the one being harmed)
glossary.bustum: bustum — funeral pyre, place of burning, tomb (n. nom./acc. sg.; here acc. as predicate, calling herself a tomb)
glossary.cadebant: cadō — were falling (3 pl. imperf. act.)
glossary.caecae: caecus, -a, -um — blind, unseeing; dark (f. gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl.; here gen. sg., with 'noctis', of blind night)
glossary.caesis: caedō — struck, beaten, cut (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. pl.; here abl. pl. m. in an ablative absolute, arms beaten in mourning)
glossary.calaisque: Calais + -que — and Calais, son of Boreas and Orithyia, brother of Zetes (m. nom.; Greek name)
glossary.calydon: Calydōn — Calydon, a city of Aetolia (f. nom. sg.; Greek name)
glossary.cani: cānus, -a, -um — grey, hoary, white with age (gen./dat. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m.; here gen. sg. m., with 'lupi', of a grey wolf. Identical in spelling to canī, dat. sg. of canis 'dog', and to canī, pres. pass. inf. of canō 'to be sung' — neither is the sense here)
glossary.capiunt: capiō — hold, contain, have room for (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.capto: capiō — for the one caught, for the captive (perf. pass. part. used as a noun, m. dat. sg.; the form is also abl. sg. m./n., and is spelled like captō, 1 sg. pres. of captāre 'snatch at')
glossary.carina: carīna — keel; by extension, ship (f. abl. sg. here; the nom. sg. carīna is spelled the same)
glossary.caruit: careō — lacked, was without, was deprived of (3 sg. perf. act.; takes the ablative of the thing lacked)
glossary.cecropidum: Cecropidae / Cecropis — descendants of Cecrops, first king of Athens; hence Athenians (gen. pl., in the shorter -um form; here of women, so the f. patronymic Cecropis is as likely a lemma as the m. Cecropidae)
glossary.cecropios: Cecropius, -a, -um — Cecropian, Athenian (from Cecrops, first king of Athens; m. acc. pl.)
glossary.cephalus: Cephalus — Cephalus, Athenian hero, husband of Procris (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.cernunt: cernō — see, discern, perceive (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.cervae: cerva — hind, doe (f.; the form is gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — here gen. sg., a hind's)
glossary.cervina: cervīnus, -a, -um — of a deer, deerskin (n. nom./acc. pl. here, with 'vellera'; the form is also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.cessastis: cessō — you hung back, you did nothing, you failed to act (2 pl. perf. act., syncopated for 'cessāvistis')
glossary.ciboque: cibus + -que — and food, nourishment; fuel (m. dat./abl. sg.; here abl., after 'pro')
glossary.ciconum: Cicones — the Cicones, a people of Thrace (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.ciet: cieō — summons, calls up, rouses (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.cingere: cingō — to encircle, to gird, to enclose (pres. act. inf.; the same form can be 2 sg. pres. pass., 'you are girt')
glossary.clamantem: clāmō — crying out, shouting (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.clamato: clāmō — called on, cried out to (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg., in an ablative absolute; the verb is transitive here, 'call upon by name'. The form is also the future imperative, 'shout!' — not the sense here)
glossary.clarum: clārus, -a, -um — bright; renowned, famous (m./n. acc. sg.; here n. acc., with 'nomen')
glossary.clauduntur: claudō — are shut in, are enclosed, are hemmed (3 pl. pres. pass.)
glossary.clausa: claudō — shut in, confined, penned (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; the form is also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.cleonae: Cleōnae — Cleonae, a small town of the Argolid between Corinth and Argos (f. nom. pl.; the name is plural in form)
glossary.coactis: cōgō — forced, compelled, wrung out (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. pl.; here f. abl. pl., of tears forced out)
glossary.coegit: cōgō — compelled, forced, drove (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.columba: columba — dove (f. nom. sg. here; the abl. sg. columbā is spelled the same)
glossary.comitante: comitor — accompanying, escorting (pres. part. of the deponent comitor, abl. sg.; active in meaning, in an ablative absolute)
glossary.commendat: commendō — entrusts, commits to another's care (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.committitur: committō — is begun, is entered upon; of talk, is joined (3 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.commota: commoveō — stirred up, roused, set in motion (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., with 'est' understood; the form is also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.comprensam: comprehendō — gripped, seized fast (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.; Magnus prints the syncopated 'comprensam' for 'comprehensam')
glossary.concessit: concēdō — gave way, yielded, withdrew (3 sg. perf. act.; with dat., yielded to)
glossary.concursibus: concursus, -ūs — a running together, collision, clash (m. dat./abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.concutio: concutiō — I shake violently, I convulse, I batter (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.confusura: cōnfundō — about to confound, meaning to jumble together (future active participle, f. nom. sg.; expresses intention, 'rushing off to confound')
glossary.congerit: congerō — heaps up, piles together, packs in (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.coniuncti: coniungō — joined, united; of marriage, wedded (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.; the form is also gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.constituit: cōnstituō — sets up, erects, establishes (3 sg. pres. act. here, among historic presents; the form is identical to the 3 sg. perf., 'he/she set up')
glossary.conubio: cōnūbium — marriage, wedlock (n. dat./abl. sg.; with 'iunxit' either dat., joined to marriage, or abl., joined in marriage — the case cannot be told apart here; uncertain, though the ablative of means is the commoner construction. Often scanned as three syllables, with consonantal i)
glossary.convexa: convexus, -a, -um — arched, vaulted, hollowed out (n. nom./acc. pl. here, with 'foramina'; the form is also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.corinthus: Corinthus — Corinth, the city on the Isthmus (f. nom. sg.; city names are feminine)
glossary.corripiens: corripiō — snatching up, seizing; of speech or weeping, cutting short, rebuking (pres. act. part., m./f. nom. sg.; with an object like weeping or words it carries the second sense)
glossary.corrumpere: corrumpō — to corrupt, to bribe, to buy off; to spoil (pres. act. inf.; the form is also 2 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.crearat: creō — had begotten, had fathered (3 sg. pluperf. act., syncopated for 'creāverat')
glossary.cremabo: cremō — I shall burn, I shall set ablaze (1 sg. fut. act.)
glossary.cremet: cremō — should burn, may burn (3 sg. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.cristae: crista — crest, tuft, plume (f. nom. pl. here; the form is also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.cultus: cultus, -ūs — dress, adornment, grooming, style of living (m., 4th decl.; nom. sg., gen. sg., nom. pl. and acc. pl. all share the form — here acc. pl. Identical in spelling to cultus, perf. pass. part. of colō, 'tended, cultivated')
glossary.cupidoque: cupidus, -a, -um + -que — and eager, desirous, lustful (dat./abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. n., with 'ore'. Identical in spelling to the nom. sg. of cupīdō, -inis 'desire, passion' — here the adjective)
glossary.custodia: custōdia — guard, watch, close keeping (f. nom. sg. here; the abl. sg. custōdiā is spelled the same)
glossary.dabis: dō — you will give, you will grant (2 sg. fut. act.; in the idiom 'poenas dare' it means 'you will pay the penalty', and both uses occur in these lines)
glossary.dantur: dō — are given, are given over, are surrendered (3 pl. pres. pass.)
glossary.debueram: dēbeō — I ought to have (1 sg. pluperf. act.; Latin uses the indicative where English says 'I should have')
glossary.dedecet: dēdecet — it ill becomes, it is unseemly for (impersonal, 3 sg. pres.; the person is accusative)
glossary.deduci: dēdūcō — to be drawn down, to be launched (pres. pass. inf.; of ships, hauled down from shore into the water)
glossary.defendere: dēfendō — to defend, to hold by force against attack, to keep off (pres. act. inf.; the form is also 2 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.defuerunt: dēsum — were lacking, failed, ran short (3 pl. perf. act.; with dat., failed someone)
glossary.degeneras: dēgenerō — you fall short of your birth, you degenerate, you are unworthy of your stock (2 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.deiectoque: dēiciō + -que — and cast down, lowered (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg., in an ablative absolute; the form is also n. abl. sg. and m. dat. sg.)
glossary.deique: deus + -que — and of the god (m. gen. sg. here, with a following noun; the form is also nom. pl., 'the gods')
glossary.demit: dēmō — takes off, removes, strips away (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.deripit: dēripiō — tears off, snatches down (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.detorquet: dētorqueō — turns away, twists aside (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.develat: dēvēlō — unveils, uncovers (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.dextrae: dext(e)ra — right hand (f., the adjective dextra used as a noun; the form is gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — here dat. sg., hand joined to hand)
glossary.dilaniant: dīlaniō — they tear to pieces, they rend apart (3 pl. pres. act.)
glossary.diras: dīrus, -a, -um — dreadful, accursed, ill-omened (f. acc. pl.; the same spelling as the acc. pl. of Dīrae, the Furies — here the adjective, with a f. noun)
glossary.disque: deus + -que — and to the gods (m. dat. pl.; 'dīs' is the contracted dat./abl. pl. for 'deīs' — here dat.)
glossary.dissimulare: dissimulō — to conceal, to hide one's feelings, to pretend a thing is not so (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.divis: dīvus — god, deity (m. dat./abl. pl.; here abl., picking up the run of ablative absolutes; uncertain — it can also be read as the ablative governed by 'super', 'above the great gods')
glossary.divitior: dīves — richer (comparative dīvitior, m./f. nom. sg.; with an ablative of respect, richer in something)
glossary.divum: dīvus — of the gods (m. gen. pl., the contracted form for 'dīvōrum'; identical in spelling to the acc. sg. dīvum, 'god')
glossary.domestica: domesticus, -a, -um — of the household, one's own, native to one (f. nom. sg. here, agreeing with a f. noun; the form is also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.dominae: domina — mistress, lady of the house (f.; the form is gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl. — both occurrences in these lines are singular, one genitive, 'her mistress's', and one dative, 'to her mistress')
glossary.dryadas: Dryas, -adis — Dryad, wood-nymph (f. acc. pl., with the Greek ending -as)
glossary.duarum: duo, duae, duo — of the two (f. gen. pl.)
glossary.effectum: efficiō — accomplished, completed, brought off (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg. with 'est' understood; the form is also m. acc. sg. and the supine)
glossary.effreno: effrēnus, -a, -um — unbridled, unchecked (dat./abl. sg. m./n.; here abl. m., with 'amore')
glossary.egere: agō — they rendered, they gave, they did (3 pl. perf. act. in the poetic '-ēre' for '-ērunt'; with 'grates', rendered thanks. Identical in spelling to egēre, pres. inf. of egeō 'to be in need' — not the sense here)
glossary.egerere: ēgerō — to carry out, to discharge, to disgorge (pres. act. inf.; the form is also 2 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.egressa: ēgredior — having gone out, having left (perf. part. of the deponent ēgredior, f. nom. sg.; active in meaning, and with 'est' it makes the perfect 'she went out')
glossary.elisi: ēlīdō — struck out, dashed out, forced out (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.; the form is also gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.epops: epops — hoopoe (m. nom. sg.; a Greek loan-word, the name of the crested bird)
glossary.epulae: epulae, -ārum — banquet, feast, the dishes of a meal (f. nom. pl.; the word is used in the plural)
glossary.equique: equus + -que — and the horses (m. nom. pl. here; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.erechtheus: Erechtheus — Erechtheus, king of Athens after Pandion, father of Orithyia (m. nom. sg. in both places here)
glossary.eripis: ēripiō — you snatch away, you tear out, you wrench free (2 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.euhoeque: euhoe (euoe) + -que — and 'euhoe!', the ritual cry of Bacchus's worshippers (indeclinable interjection, here the thing shouted)
glossary.eumenides: Eumenides — the Eumenides, the avenging Furies (f. nom. pl.; Greek 'the Kindly Ones', a euphemism meant to avert them)
glossary.exaestuat: exaestuō — boils up, seethes (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.excussa: excutiō — shaken out, struck loose, thrown clear (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; the form is also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.expellam: expellō — I shall drive out, I shall force out (1 sg. fut. act. here, beside other futures; the form is also 1 sg. pres. subj., 'let me drive out')
glossary.exsiliantque: exsiliō + -que — and leap out, and spring forth (3 pl. pres. subj. act.; in a result clause with 'ut')
glossary.exsistere: exsistō — to come forth, to step out, to show oneself (as something) (pres. act. inf.; with a predicate noun, to emerge as that thing)
glossary.exstimulat: exstimulō — goads on, spurs, pricks forward (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.exsultatque: exsultō — and exults, leaps up, is beside himself (3 sg. pres. act.; the verb is literally 'leap up', and of things it keeps that physical sense)
glossary.exteriusque: exterius + -que — and further out, on the outer side (comparative adverb of 'exter'; the form is also the n. nom./acc. sg. of the comparative adjective exterior)
glossary.exululatque: exululō + -que — and howls out, and shrieks aloud (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.facibusque: fax, facis + -que — and torches, firebrands (f. dat./abl. pl.; here abl., after 'pro')
glossary.faciendus: faciō — to be made (into something), having to be made so (gerundive, m. nom. sg.; with 'erat', he had to be made so)
glossary.facundum: fācundus, -a, -um — eloquent, ready of speech (m. acc. sg. here, predicate with 'faciebat', made him eloquent; the form is also n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.faenilibus: faenīle, -is — hayloft, hay-store (n. dat./abl. pl.; here abl. of place, in the haylofts)
glossary.falsisque: falsus, -a, -um + -que — and false, unreal, counterfeit (dat./abl. pl.; here dat., the recipients of an offering)
glossary.famulosque: famulus + -que — and servants, household attendants (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.fasque: fās + -que — and what is right, what heaven allows (n., indeclinable; here acc., the object of a participle; the paired '-que … -que' is 'both … and')
glossary.fassusque: fateor, fatērī, fassus — and having confessed, having avowed (perf. part. of the deponent, m. nom. sg.; active in meaning, and transitive, taking a direct object; + -que)
glossary.fausto: faustus, -a, -um — favourable, auspicious, of good omen (m./n. abl. sg.; here n. abl. sg., in an ablative of attendant circumstance, 'with a favourable omen')
glossary.fecisses: faciō, facere, fēcī, factum — you had done, you had made (2 sg. pluperf. subj. act.; after 'utinam' it is a wish for what did not happen, 'would that you had done')
glossary.feri: ferus, -a, -um — savage, brutal, wild (gen. sg. m./n., or nom. pl. m.; here gen. sg. m. with a genitive noun). Identical in spelling to ferī, gen. sg. of the noun ferus 'a wild beast', and to ferī, 2 sg. imperative of feriō 'strike!' — here the adjective
glossary.fessis: fessus, -a, -um — weary, worn out, spent (dat./abl. pl. of any gender; here abl. pl. f.)
glossary.fictos: fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum — feigned, faked, put on (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.fingit: fingō, fingere — he shapes, he invents, he pictures to himself (3 sg. pres. act.; of forming a thing in the mind as much as in the hand)
glossary.finitimi: fīnitimus, -a, -um — neighbouring, bordering, adjoining (m. nom. pl., here with a plural subject; also gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.flagrat: flagrō, flagrāre — he blazes, is on fire, burns (3 sg. pres. act.; regularly of passion, with the ablative of what he burns with)
glossary.flexis: flectō, flectere, flexī, flexum — bent, twisted back (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. pl.; here abl. pl. f. in an ablative absolute)
glossary.foramina: forāmen, -inis (n.) — openings, holes, hollow passages (n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.)
glossary.forcipe: forceps, -cipis (f.) — with tongs, with pincers (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.fortunaeque: fortūna, -ae (f.) — fortune, lot, plight (f. gen. sg. here, depending on a noun; the form is also dat. sg. and nom. pl.; + -que)
glossary.fuderat: fundō, fundere, fūdī, fūsum — had routed, had scattered, had poured out (3 sg. pluperf. act.; of putting an enemy to flight; not fundāre 'to found')
glossary.fulgentia: fulgeō, fulgēre — gleaming, flashing, glittering (pres. act. part. fulgēns, n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl. n.)
glossary.funere: fūnus, -eris (n.) — funeral, funeral rites, funeral pyre; also a death, a corpse (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.furiali: furiālis, -e — frenzied, maddened, Fury-like (dat./abl. sg. of any gender; here abl. sg. f.; formed on Furia, an avenging Fury)
glossary.furialiaque: furiālis, -e — frenzied, maddening, Fury-like (n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.; + -que)
glossary.furiisque: furia, -ae (f.) — frenzies, fits of madness (f. dat./abl. pl.; here abl. of means, 'driven by'; + -que). Capitalised, Furia is one of the avenging Furies
glossary.gangetica: Gangēticus, -a, -um — of the Ganges, Indian (f. nom. sg.; the river standing for India as a whole)
glossary.gemellos: gemellus, -a, -um — twin; as a noun, twins (m. acc. pl.; diminutive of geminus)
glossary.geminus: geminus, -a, -um — twin, double, twofold (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.germana: germāna, -ae (f.) — sister, full sister (f. nom. sg. or voc. sg. — both occur in these lines; also abl. sg.; feminine of germānus, 'of the same parents')
glossary.germanamque: germāna, -ae (f.) — sister, full sister (f. acc. sg.; + -que)
glossary.gradivo: Grādīvus — Gradivus, a cult title of Mars the war-god (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.grande: grandis, -e — great, large, mighty (n. nom./acc. sg.; here nom. sg. as predicate)
glossary.gratata: grātor, grātārī, grātātus — having offered congratulations, having rejoiced with (perf. part. of the deponent, f. nom. sg.; active in meaning, and with a form of 'esse' it makes the perfect indicative, 'congratulated'; the person congratulated stands in the dative)
glossary.habuissem: habeō, habēre — I should have had, I would have had (1 sg. pluperf. subj. act.)
glossary.haeserat: haereō, haerēre, haesī — had stuck fast, had clung (3 sg. pluperf. act.; what one sticks to stands in the dative or ablative)
glossary.hederarum: hedera, -ae (f.) — of ivy (f. gen. pl.; ivy is the plant of Bacchus)
glossary.horret: horreō, horrēre — she shudders, bristles, shrinks in dread (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.humilesque: humilis, -e — low-lying, low, lowly (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here f. nom. pl.; + -que)
glossary.iactatibus: iactātus, -ūs (m.) — by the tossing, by the flapping, by the shaking (m. dat./abl. pl.; here abl. of means; a rare fourth-declension noun from iactāre 'to toss')
glossary.ignarum: ignārus, -a, -um — unaware, not knowing, in ignorance (m. acc. sg.; also n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.illatum: īnferō, īnferre, intulī, illātum — brought upon, inflicted, visited on (perf. pass. part.; n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.; here n. acc. sg., with 'esse' understood in indirect statement)
glossary.impendere: impendō, impendere, impendī, impēnsum — to spend, to lay out, to expend (pres. act. inf.). Identical in spelling to impendēre, pres. inf. of impendeō 'to overhang, threaten' — here the former, governing an accusative object
glossary.impius: impius, -a, -um — undutiful, unholy, sinning against what is owed to kin and gods (m. nom. sg.; the negative of pius)
glossary.implebo: impleō, implēre, implēvī, implētum — I shall fill (1 sg. fut. act.)
glossary.implumes: implūmis, -e — unfledged, featherless (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here m. nom. pl.)
glossary.inclusas: inclūdō, inclūdere, inclūsī, inclūsum — shut in, confined, pent up (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.indignantem: indignor, indignārī, indignātus — indignant, protesting in outrage (pres. part. of the deponent, m./f. acc. sg.; here f. acc. sg.; active in meaning)
glossary.induiturque: induō, induere, induī, indūtum — she puts on, clothes herself in (3 sg. pres.; passive in form but used reflexively, keeping an accusative of the garment — the so-called middle voice; + -que)
glossary.induroque: indūrō, indūrāre — I harden, I freeze hard (1 sg. pres. act.; + -que)
glossary.inferiora: īnferus, -a, -um, comparative īnferior — lower, lesser, feebler (comparative, n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl. used as a noun, 'things no feebler'; the thing compared stands in the ablative)
glossary.infert: īnferō, īnferre — she brings in, offers, presents (3 sg. pres. act.; commonly of offerings brought to the dead)
glossary.infractaque: īnfringō, īnfringere, īnfrēgī, īnfrāctum — broken, weakened, checked (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. here; also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.; + -que)
glossary.ingenium: ingenium, -ī (n.) — natural talent, inventiveness, resourcefulness (n. nom./acc. sg.; here nom. sg.)
glossary.ingentibus: ingēns, -entis — huge, enormous, vast (dat./abl. pl. of any gender; here abl. pl.)
glossary.inmersaque: immergō, immergere, immersī, immersum (Magnus prints the unassimilated inmersa) — plunged in, sunk deep within, swallowed down (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl. or f. nom./abl. sg.; here n. acc. pl.; + -que)
glossary.inmitibus: immītis, -e (Magnus prints inmītis) — harsh, merciless, unrelenting (dat./abl. pl.; here abl. pl.)
glossary.inmittam: immittō, immittere (Magnus prints inmittam) — I shall fling in, hurl into, let loose upon (1 sg.; the form is future indicative or present subjunctive — here future, standing beside other futures)
glossary.inmodicum: immodicus, -a, -um (Magnus prints inmodicum) — immoderate, outsized, beyond all measure (n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.); here it may agree with a neuter nominative subject or stand as an adverbial accusative with the verb, 'juts out hugely'; uncertain — the Latin allows either and the sense is the same
glossary.innata: innāscor, innāscī, innātus — inborn, innate, native to one (perf. part. of the deponent used as an adjective, f. nom. sg.; also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.; not from innatāre 'to swim in')
glossary.insonet: īnsonō, īnsonāre — resounds, crashes, roars (3 sg. pres. subj. act., in a result clause)
glossary.instruitur: īnstruō, īnstruere — she is equipped, is fitted out, is arrayed (3 sg. pres. pass.; readily taken reflexively, 'equips herself', with the ablative of what she is equipped with)
glossary.intendens: intendō, intendere — stretching out, holding out, straining (pres. act. part., nom. sg. of any gender)
glossary.intexuit: intexō, intexere, intexuī, intextum — she wove in, worked into the weaving (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.invisa: invīsus, -a, -um — hated, hateful, loathed (f. nom. sg. here, with a dative of the person who hates; also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.). Distinguish the rarer invīsus 'unseen' (in- + vīsus) and invīsa from invīsō 'visit' — here 'hated'
glossary.invitique: invītus, -a, -um — unwilling, reluctant, against one's will (m. nom. pl.; Latin puts the adjective where English wants the adverb, 'unwillingly'; + -que)
glossary.isthmo: Isthmus — the Isthmus, the neck of land at Corinth joining the Peloponnese to mainland Greece (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.ityn: Ītys, Ītyos — Itys, the young son of Tereus and Procne (Greek acc. sg. Ityn)
glossary.ityosque: Ītys, Ītyos — of Itys, son of Tereus and Procne (Greek gen. sg. Ityos; + -que)
glossary.itys: Ītys, Ītyos — Itys, the young son of Tereus and Procne (nom. sg.)
glossary.iungitur: iungō, iungere — is joined, is clasped (3 sg. pres. pass.; what it is joined to stands in the dative)
glossary.iurare: iūrō, iūrāre — to swear, to take an oath (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.iussere: iubeō, iubēre, iussī, iussum — they ordered, they bade (3 pl. perf. act. = iussērunt, the poetic short form; not a present infinitive)
glossary.iustitia: iūstitia, -ae (f.) — justice, fair dealing (f. nom. or abl. sg.; here abl. of respect with a comparative, 'more powerful in justice')
glossary.iuventae: iuventa, -ae (f.) — youth, young manhood (f. dat. sg. here, with a verb of yielding, 'gave way to young manhood'; the form is also gen. sg. and nom. pl., and a genitive reading, 'the boyish season of youth', is defensible; uncertain — the case turns on how 'concessit' is taken)
glossary.lacerum: lacer, lacera, lacerum — mangled, mutilated, torn (n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.; here n. acc. sg. with a neuter object)
glossary.lactentem: lactēns, -entis — suckling, still at the milk (m./f. acc. sg.; here m. acc. sg.; present participle of lactēre 'to take milk')
glossary.latumque: lātus, -a, -um — broad, wide (n. nom./acc. sg.; here nom. sg. agreeing with a neuter subject; + -que). Distinguish latus, lateris (n.) 'side, flank' and lātus, perf. pass. part. of ferō 'borne' — here the adjective
glossary.laudemque: laus, laudis (f.) — praise, credit, a good name (f. acc. sg.; + -que). Identical in spelling to laudem, 1 sg. pres. subj. of laudāre 'I may praise' — here the noun
glossary.lenimen: lēnīmen, -inis (n.) — a solace, a comfort, a soothing (n. nom./acc. sg.; here acc. sg.; a rare noun built on lēnīre 'to soothe')
glossary.liberat: līberō, līberāre — he frees, releases, draws clear (3 sg. pres. act.; what a thing is freed from stands in the ablative)
glossary.libidine: libīdō, -inis (f.) — lust, sexual desire, appetite (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.libido: libīdō, -inis (f.) — lust, sexual desire, appetite (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.locutus: loquor, loquī, locūtus — having spoken, having said (perf. part. of the deponent, m. nom. sg.; active in meaning)
glossary.longaeque: longus, -a, -um — long (f. gen. sg. here, agreeing with a feminine genitive; also f. dat. sg. and nom. pl.; + -que)
glossary.loquar: loquor, loquī — I shall speak of, I shall tell (1 sg. of the deponent; the form is future indicative or present subjunctive — here future)
glossary.luctantemque: luctor, luctārī, luctātus — struggling, wrestling (pres. part. of the deponent, m./f. acc. sg.; here f. acc. sg., with a complementary infinitive, 'struggling to —'; + -que)
glossary.luctor: luctor, luctārī, luctātus — I wrestle, I struggle, I heave (1 sg. pres. of the deponent; active in meaning despite the passive ending)
glossary.lugendae: lūgeō, lūgēre, lūxī — to be mourned, deserving to be mourned (gerundive, f. gen. sg. here; also f. dat. sg. and nom. pl.; the gerundive states what ought to be done, not what is done)
glossary.lugenti: lūgeō, lūgēre — mourning, one in mourning (pres. act. part. lūgēns, dat. sg. of any gender; here dat. after an adjective that governs the dative)
glossary.lugubre: lūgubris, -e — mournful, grievous, a cause of grief (n. nom./acc. sg.; here nom. sg. as predicate, with a dative of the person it grieves)
glossary.lupi: lupus, -ī (m.) — wolf (m. gen. sg. here; also nom. pl.)
glossary.lustraverat: lūstrō, lūstrāre — had traversed, had gone the round of (3 sg. pluperf. act.; of passing over or through a whole space. The same verb also means 'to purify by lustration' and 'to survey' — here the circuit)
glossary.madefactis: madefaciō, madefacere, madefēcī, madefactum — soaked, drenched, wetted through (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. pl.; here abl. pl. f.)
glossary.malae: māla, -ae (f.) — cheeks, jaws (f. nom. pl.). Identical in spelling to malae from malus, -a, -um 'bad, evil' (f. gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl.), and to mālae from mālus 'apple tree' — here the noun 'cheeks'
glossary.maluit: mālō, mālle, māluī — she preferred, she would rather have (3 sg. perf. act.; contracted from magis + volō)
glossary.mandabat: mandō, mandāre — he was charging, was giving his instructions, was committing to another's care (3 sg. impf. act.; not mandō, mandere 'to chew')
glossary.mandasset: mandō, mandāre — he had entrusted, had commissioned (3 sg. pluperf. subj. act., syncopated for mandāvisset)
glossary.mandata: mandātum, -ī (n.) — instructions, charge, commission, the message one is sent with (n. nom. or acc. pl. — both occur in these lines; the noun is the perf. pass. part. of mandāre used substantivally, and the same form can still be a participle, 'entrusted')
glossary.mavult: mālō, mālle — he prefers, he would rather (3 sg. pres. act.; contracted from magis + vult)
glossary.memori: memor, memoris — mindful, remembering, that does not forget (dat./abl. sg. of any gender; here abl. sg. n.)
glossary.mentita: mentior, mentīrī, mentītus — having feigned, having falsely claimed, having faked (perf. part. of the deponent, f. nom. sg.; active in meaning and here transitive, taking a direct object)
glossary.messeneque: Messēnē — Messene, the chief city of Messenia in the south-west Peloponnese (f. nom. sg., Greek; + -que)
glossary.micat: micō, micāre — it quivers, twitches, darts (3 sg. pres. act.; of a quick trembling or flashing movement)
glossary.minaces: mināx, -ācis — threatening, menacing (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here acc. pl. m.)
glossary.minyis: Minyae, -ārum (m. pl.) — the Minyae, that is the Argonauts, named from the Minyan stock of Iolcus (m. dat./abl. pl.; here abl. after 'cum')
glossary.mirum: mīrus, -a, -um — wonderful, astonishing; as a neuter noun, a marvel (n. nom./acc. sg.; here nom. sg. in a parenthetical exclamation taking an infinitive, 'a marvel, that —'; also m. acc. sg.)
glossary.miserisque: miser, -era, -erum — wretched, pitiable, in distress (dat. or abl. pl. of any gender; here dat. pl.; + -que)
glossary.missae: mittō, mittere, mīsī, missum — sent, sent off (perf. pass. part., f. gen. or dat. sg., or nom. pl.; here f. gen. sg. depending on a noun, 'of her who is sent'; uncertain — a dative of advantage, 'for her who is sent', is equally construable)
glossary.mites: mītis, -e — gentle, soft, mild (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here f. nom. pl.)
glossary.mixtaque: misceō, miscēre, miscuī, mixtum — mixed, mingled (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.; what a thing is mingled with stands in the ablative or dative; + -que)
glossary.molimine: mōlīmen, -inis (n.) — effort, exertion, a massive undertaking (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.mopsopios: Mopsopius, -a, -um — Mopsopian, that is Athenian (m. acc. pl.; from Mopsopia, an old poetic name for Attica)
glossary.moris: mōs, mōris (m.) — custom, usage, ancestral practice (m. gen. sg.). Identical in spelling to mōrīs, dat./abl. pl. of mora 'delay' — here the genitive of mōs
glossary.motusque: mōtus, -ūs (m.) — movements, gestures, bearing (m. acc. pl.; + -que). Identical in spelling to mōtus, perf. pass. part. of moveō 'moved' (m. nom. sg.) — here the noun
glossary.movebo: moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — I shall move, I shall stir (1 sg. fut. act.)
glossary.mutilatae: mutilō, mutilāre — mutilated, docked, cut short (perf. pass. part., f. gen. sg. here; also f. dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.mutum: mūtus, -a, -um — mute, dumb, speechless (n. nom./acc. sg.; here nom. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
glossary.mycenae: Mȳcēnae, -ārum (f. pl.) — Mycenae, the Argive citadel of Agamemnon (f. nom. pl.; the name is plural in form though it is one city, and takes plural agreement)
glossary.naidas: Nāis, Nāidos (f.) — Naiads, water-nymphs (Greek acc. pl. Nāidas)
glossary.nefandam: nefandus, -a, -um — unspeakable, abominable, not to be uttered (f. acc. sg.; gerundive in shape, from fārī 'to speak' with the negative ne-)
glossary.nelea: Nēlēus, -a, -um — Neleian, of Neleus, king of Pylos and father of Nestor (f. nom. sg., agreeing with a Greek feminine place-name; also n. nom./acc. pl.). The same spelling can serve the Greek acc. sg. of the king's own name, Nēleus — here the adjective
glossary.nepotemque: nepōs, nepōtis (m.) — grandson; also descendant (m. acc. sg.; + -que)
glossary.nido: nīdus, -ī (m.) — nest (m. dat. or abl. sg.; here abl. with a preposition, 'in the nest')
glossary.nives: nix, nivis (f.) — snows, snowfalls (f. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.nobilis: nōbilis, -e — famous, renowned, of high birth (m./f. nom. sg.; here f. nom. sg.; also gen. sg. of any gender. What one is famous for stands in the ablative)
glossary.notas: nota, -ae (f.) — marks, signs, written characters (f. acc. pl.). Identical in spelling to nōtās from nōtus 'known' (f. acc. pl.) and to notās, 2 sg. pres. of notāre 'you mark' — here the noun
glossary.nupta: nūbō, nūbere, nūpsī, nūptum — married, wedded (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; said of the woman, and taking a dative of the man she is married to; also used as a noun, nūpta 'a bride, a wife'; the form is also f. abl. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.nutricisque: nūtrīx, -īcis (f.) — nurse, the woman who suckled and reared a child (f. gen. sg.; + -que)
glossary.obuncis: obuncus, -a, -um — hooked, crooked, curved inward (dat./abl. pl.; here abl. pl.; regularly of talons and beaks)
glossary.odrysius: Odrysius, -a, -um — Odrysian, that is Thracian (m. nom. sg.; the Odrysae were the leading people of Thrace)
glossary.omine: ōmen, -inis (n.) — omen, sign, auspice (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.opacas: opācus, -a, -um — shady, dark, overshadowed (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.orandus: ōrō, ōrāre — to be entreated, needing to be begged (gerundive, m. nom. sg.; with a form of 'esse' it states obligation, 'ought to be entreated')
glossary.oravere: ōrō, ōrāre — they begged, they entreated (3 pl. perf. act. = ōrāvērunt, the poetic short form; not a present infinitive)
glossary.orchomenosque: Orchomenos — Orchomenus, a Greek city (m. nom. sg., keeping the Greek -os ending; + -que). The name belonged both to the rich Boeotian city and to an Arcadian one; uncertain which is meant, since the surrounding catalogue is largely Peloponnesian but not only so
glossary.orithyia: Ōrīthyia — Orithyia, daughter of Erechtheus king of Athens (f. abl. sg. here, with a verb of lacking; the form is also nom. sg.)
glossary.orithyian: Ōrīthyia — Orithyia, daughter of Erechtheus king of Athens (Greek acc. sg. Orithyian)
glossary.osculaque: ōsculum, -ī (n.) — kisses (n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.; literally 'little mouth', diminutive of ōs; + -que)
glossary.pallentem: palleō, pallēre — pale, white, blanching (pres. act. part. pallēns, m./f. acc. sg.; here f. acc. sg.)
glossary.palpitat: palpitō, palpitāre — it twitches, throbs, jerks convulsively (3 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.pandion: Pandīōn, -onis — Pandion, king of Athens, father of Procne and Philomela (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.pandiona: Pandīōn, -onis — Pandion, king of Athens (Greek acc. sg. Pandīona)
glossary.pandione: Pandīōn, -onis — Pandion, king of Athens (m. abl. sg.; with a participle of birth, 'nata', 'genitas', it is the ablative of origin, 'born of Pandion')
glossary.paratus: parātus, -ūs (m.) — outfit, trappings, finery, display (m. acc. pl. of the fourth declension; also nom./gen. sg.). Identical in spelling to parātus, perf. pass. part. of parāre 'prepared, ready' (m. nom. sg.) — here the noun, acc. pl.
glossary.paravi: parō, parāre — I have made ready, I have prepared, I have set myself to (1 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.partus: partus, -ūs (m.) — offspring, young, the children brought forth; also a birth (m. acc. pl. of the fourth declension; also nom./gen. sg.). Identical in spelling to partus, perf. pass. part. of pariō 'brought forth' — here the noun, acc. pl.
glossary.passos: pandō, pandere, pandī, passum — spread out, loosened, dishevelled (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.; the regular word for unbound hair). Identical in spelling to passōs, acc. pl. m. of passus, perf. part. of the deponent patior 'having suffered' — here pandō
glossary.patraeque: Patrae, -ārum (f. pl.) — Patrae, a city on the Achaean coast of the Peloponnese (f. nom. pl.; + -que)
glossary.patrii: patrius, -a, -um — ancestral, of one's fathers, of the fatherland (m./n. gen. sg.; here gen. sg. m.; also m. nom. pl.)
glossary.pavidamque: pavidus, -a, -um — trembling, panic-stricken, terrified (f. acc. sg.; + -que)
glossary.pello: pellō, pellere, pepulī, pulsum — I drive off, I beat away, I rout (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.pelopeiadesque: Pelopēias, -adis — of Pelops, Pelopean (f. nom. pl., a Greek patronymic adjective; Pelops was the hero whose name the Peloponnese carries; + -que)
glossary.perfectaque: perficiō, perficere, perfēcī, perfectum — finished, completed, brought to an end (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl. standing as a noun, 'the finished work'; also f. nom./abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.perierunt: pereō, perīre, periī — they have perished, have been destroyed, are gone (3 pl. perf. act.)
glossary.pertulit: perferō, perferre, pertulī, perlātum — she carried through, delivered, brought all the way (3 sg. perf. act.)
glossary.petentem: petō, petere — reaching for, making for, seeking (pres. act. part. petēns, m./f. acc. sg.; here m. acc. sg.)
glossary.petiisse: petō, petere, petīvī (petiī), petītum — to have sought, to have made for (perf. act. inf., syncopated for petīvisse)
glossary.philomela: Philomēla — Philomela, daughter of Pandion of Athens and sister of Procne (f. nom. sg. and voc. sg. — both occur in these lines; the form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.piacula: piāculum, -ī (n.) — propitiatory offerings, expiatory sacrifices (n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.; from piāre 'to appease')
glossary.pietate: pietās, -ātis (f.) — dutiful devotion, the loyalty owed to kin, country and gods (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.piis: pius — dutiful, faithful, tender (of what duty owes to kin and gods) (m./f./n. dat. or abl. pl.; here f. abl. pl.)
glossary.piraeaque: Pīraeus — of the Piraeus, the port of Athens (adj., n. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.pittheia: Pitthēius — of Pittheus, king of Troezen and grandfather of Theseus (adj., f. nom. sg.)
glossary.poenaeque: poena — punishment, vengeance, the penalty exacted (f. gen. or dat. sg., also nom. pl.; in these lines gen. sg., 'of vengeance') + -que 'and'
glossary.ponitur: pōnō — is set out, is served, is placed (3 sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.poposcit: poscō — demanded, called for, asked for (3 sg. perf.; reduplicated perfect poposcī)
glossary.portasque: porta — gates, doors (f. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'; the form is also 2 sg. pres. of portō 'carry' — here the noun
glossary.positasque: pōnō — laid up, stored, put by (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.potentior: potēns — more powerful, stronger (comparative adj., m./f. nom. sg.)
glossary.praecontrectatque: praecontrectō — gropes, fondles in advance (3 sg. pres. act.; prae- 'beforehand' + contrectō 'handle, feel, fondle', used of sexual touching) + -que 'and'; the compound is rare and appears to have been coined for this passage
glossary.praedator: praedātor — plunderer, raider, bird of prey (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.procne: Procnē — Procne, daughter of Pandion, wife of Tereus and sister of Philomela (f. nom. sg., Greek 1st decl.; the abl. sg. is identical in form)
glossary.procnen: Procnē — Procne (f. acc. sg.; the Greek accusative in -n, not the Latin -am)
glossary.procnes: Procnē — of Procne (f. gen. sg.; the Greek genitive in -ēs)
glossary.procri: Procris — Procris, daughter of Erechtheus and wife of Cephalus (f. voc. sg., the Greek vocative in -i)
glossary.profanus: profānus — unhallowed, impious, ill-omened (adj., m. nom. sg.; literally 'outside the sacred precinct')
glossary.proiecto: prōiciō — thrown down, cast off, flung aside (perf. pass. part., m. or n. abl. sg., also dat.; here m. abl. sg. in an ablative absolute)
glossary.prominet: prōmineō — juts out, projects, sticks forward (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.promittes: prōmittō — you will promise, will guarantee (2 sg. fut.)
glossary.pronuba: prōnuba — the matron who attends the bride, bridal patroness (f. nom. sg.; a cult title of Juno as the goddess who presides over marriage)
