glossary.pronumque: prōnus — leaning forward; inclined, prone, disposed (toward) (n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.; here n. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.propinquae: propinquus — neighbouring, close by (f. nom. pl.; the form is also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.prosiluit: prōsiliō — leapt forward, sprang out (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.pudibunda: pudibundus — shamefaced, covered in shame (n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. acc. pl.)
glossary.puerile: puerīlis — of boyhood, boyish (n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.pulsabant: pulsō — were beating, were striking (3 pl. imperf.; frequentative of pellō)
glossary.pulso: pulsō — I beat, batter, pound (1 sg. pres. act.; the form is also m./n. dat. or abl. sg. of pulsus 'driven, struck' (part. of pellō) and of the noun pulsus 'a beating' — here the verb)
glossary.pulvereamque: pulvereus — dusty, of dust (adj., f. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.purpureasque: purpureus — purple, crimson (adj., f. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.pylos: Pylos — Pylos, Neleus' city on the west coast of the Peloponnese (f. nom. sg., Greek)
glossary.quales: quālis — such as, of the kind that (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; correlative with tālis; here acc. pl.)
glossary.quandocumque: quandōcumque — whenever; at some time or other, sooner or later (adv./conj.)
glossary.radiantia: radiō — shining, gleaming, giving off rays (pres. act. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.)
glossary.rapere: rapiō — to seize, snatch away, carry off by force, abduct (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.rapiam: rapiō — I will tear away, snatch out by force (1 sg. fut.; the form is also 1 sg. pres. subj.; future in these lines)
glossary.raptaeque: rapiō — seized, dragged off (perf. pass. part., f. dat. or gen. sg., also f. nom. pl.; here dat. sg., of the person the thing is put on) + -que 'and'
glossary.raptas: rapiō — snatched, caught up, carried off (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.recursus: recursus — a running back, return journey (m. 4th decl., acc. pl.; the form is also nom. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.redito: redeō — come back, you shall return (2 sg. future imperative in -tō, the solemn form used in requests, laws and prayers; also 3 sg. fut. imperative)
glossary.redituram: redeō — about to return, going to come back (fut. act. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.refringit: refringō — breaks open, bursts, smashes down (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.regales: rēgālis — royal, of a king (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here f. nom. pl.)
glossary.reges: rēx — kings (m. acc. pl.; the form is also nom. pl., and 2 sg. fut. of regō 'rule' — here the noun, acc. pl.)
glossary.regionibus: regiō — regions, districts, territories (f. dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.reliqui: relinquō — I left behind, I abandoned (1 sg. perf.; the form is also m./n. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl. of reliquus 'remaining, left over' — here the verb)
glossary.remige: rēmex — oarsman, rower (m. abl. sg.; often collective, 'oarage, rowing', paired with vēlum 'sail')
glossary.remittas: remittō — you should send back, may release (2 sg. pres. subj.; in a request or indirect command)
glossary.remotam: removeō — removed, set apart, out of the way, remote (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.removente: removeō — removing, driving away, keeping off (pres. act. part., m./f./n. abl. sg.)
glossary.repellit: repellō — drives back, thrusts away, overturns (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.repetisse: repetō — to have gone back to, to have attacked again (perf. act. inf., syncopated from repetīvisse/repetiisse); with a person's body as object, to assault sexually again
glossary.repetiti: repetō — sought again, come round again, recurring (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg.; the form is also m. nom. pl.)
glossary.rerumque: rēs — of things, of affairs, of the state (f. gen. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.reserato: reserō — unbarred, unlocked, opened up (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg., also dat.; here n. abl. sg. in an ablative absolute)
glossary.restet: restō — may remain, may be left over (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.retinentia: retineō — holding on to, still keeping (pres. act. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.)
glossary.reverti: revertor — to return, to go back (pres. inf.; the verb is deponent in the present system, so the -ī form is its active-meaning infinitive. The same spelling is also 1 sg. perf. act. 'I returned', since the perfect is active — here the infinitive)
glossary.revertitur: revertor — returns, comes back (3 sg. pres.; deponent in the present system, active in meaning)
glossary.rigent: rigeō — stand stiff, are rigid, stand hard and unyielding (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.ritibus: rītus — rites, ritual observances, the customary usages of a cult (m. 4th decl., dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.sacrum: sacrum — a rite, a sacred observance, a sacrifice (n. acc. sg. of the noun; the form is also m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg. of the adj. sacer 'holy, consecrated' — here the noun)
glossary.saevi: saevus — savage, cruel, brutal (m./n. gen. sg.; the form is also m. nom. pl., and the sg. imperative of saeviō 'rage' — here gen. sg.)
glossary.saevitiam: saevitia — savagery, brutality, ferocity (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.saevo: saevus — savage, fierce, cruel (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; here n. abl. sg.; the form is also 1 sg. pres. of saeviō 'I rage')
glossary.salire: saliō — to leap, jump, twitch convulsively (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.salutent: salūtō — (that they) greet, send greetings to (3 pl. pres. subj.; in an indirect command)
glossary.sceleris: scelus — of the crime, of the outrage, of the foul deed (n. gen. sg.)
glossary.secessit: sēcēdō — withdrew, went apart, retired (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.sepulcrum: sepulcrum — tomb, grave, burial monument (n. acc. sg.; the form is also nom. sg.)
glossary.sermo: sermō — talk, conversation, discussion (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.signataque: signō — marked, stained, stamped (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., also n. nom./acc. pl.; here f. nom. sg., with est forming the perfect passive 'has been marked') + -que 'and'
glossary.similesque: similis — like, matching, of the same kind (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; takes gen. or dat.; here acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.singultibus: singultus — sobs, catches of the breath (m. 4th decl., dat. or abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.sitae: situs — situated, lying, placed (perf. pass. part. of sinō used as an adjective, f. nom. pl.; the form is also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.sithoniae: Sīthonius — Sithonian, i.e. Thracian (adj., f. nom. pl.; from Sithonia in Thrace; the form is also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.solemus: soleō — we are accustomed, we usually (do) (1 pl. pres.; takes an infinitive)
glossary.solido: solidus — solid, whole, unbroken (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; here n. abl. sg.; the form is also 1 sg. pres. of solidō 'make firm')
glossary.sollicitae: sollicitus — anxious, troubled, worn with worry (f. gen. or dat. sg., also f. nom. pl.; here gen. sg.)
glossary.sollicitare: sollicitō — to work upon, tempt, bribe, stir up (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.sontem: sōns — guilty, criminal, deserving punishment (adj., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.sparsis: spargō — scattered, spattered, flung loose (perf. pass. part., m./f./n. dat. or abl. pl.; here m. abl. pl.)
glossary.sparte: Spartē — Sparta, the chief city of Laconia (f. nom. sg., the Greek form of Latin Sparta; the form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.spondere: spondeō — to promise solemnly, pledge, guarantee (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.stabulorum: stabulum — of the stalls, steading, farm buildings (n. gen. pl.)
glossary.stimulatus: stimulō — goaded, spurred on, driven (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.stravere: sternō — spread, laid out, made up (a bed) (3 pl. perf., the -ēre ending for -ērunt)
glossary.stridunt: strīdō — hiss, sizzle, shriek (3 pl. pres.; the verb also has a 2nd-conjugation form strīdeō)
glossary.structa: struō — built, constructed, piled up (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. nom. pl.)
glossary.subii: subeō — I went under, I made my way beneath (1 sg. perf.)
glossary.subnixa: subnīxus — propped on, resting upon, supported by (+ abl.) (perf. part. of subnītor used adjectivally, f. nom. sg.)
glossary.subvectaque: subvehō — carried up, brought over (by water) (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. nom. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.successisse: succēdō — to have turned out well, to have prospered (perf. act. inf.; used impersonally with a dative of the person for whom it went well)
glossary.supponat: suppōnō — should set beneath, should put (fire) under (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.supposuique: suppōnō — I set beneath, I thrust under (1 sg. perf.) + -que 'and'
glossary.suppressit: supprimō — checked, held back, reined in (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.supremumque: suprēmus — last, final (n. acc. sg., here adverbial/internal accusative, 'for the last time'; the form is also m. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.suspendit: suspendō — hung up, set up (a warp on the loom) (3 sg.; the present and perfect of this verb are identical in form, so the tense is fixed only by context — perfect in these lines; uncertain)
glossary.tacitaque: tacitus — silent, unspoken, kept to oneself (f. nom. or abl. sg., also n. nom./acc. pl.; here f. abl. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.tartareas: Tartareus — of Tartarus, infernal, belonging to the underworld (adj., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.tellusque: tellūs — earth, land, ground (f. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.tenebor: teneō — I shall be held, kept, shut in (1 sg. fut. pass.)
glossary.terea: Tēreus — Tereus, king of Thrace, husband of Procne (m. acc. sg.; the Greek accusative Tērea, not Latin -eum)
glossary.tereo: Tēreus — Tereus (m. abl. sg.; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.tereu: Tēreus — Tereus (m. voc. sg., the Greek vocative in -eu)
glossary.tereus: Tēreus — Tereus, the Thracian king who marries Procne (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.terrebant: terreō — were terrifying, were menacing (3 pl. imperf.)
glossary.terribilis: terribilis — terrifying, dreadful to look at (adj., m./f. nom. sg.; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.testari: testor — to bear witness to, to attest, to declare (pres. inf. of the deponent, active in meaning)
glossary.testarique: testor — to call to witness, to invoke as witnesses (pres. inf. of the deponent, active in meaning) + -que 'and'
glossary.thalamique: thalamus — of the bedchamber, of the bridal chamber (m. gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.thracesque: Thrāx (pl. Thrāces) — Thracians, the men of Thrace (m. nom. pl., Greek declension; the form is also acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.thracia: Thrācia — Thrace, the land north of the Aegean (f. nom. sg.; the form is also abl. sg., and n. nom./acc. pl. of the adj. Thrācius — here the country as subject)
glossary.thracius: Thrācius — Thracian, of Thrace (adj., m. nom. sg.; used on its own as a noun, 'the Thracian')
glossary.threicius: Thrēicius — Thracian (adj., m. nom. sg.; the Grecizing doublet of Thrācius, from Θρηΐκιος)
glossary.timentem: timeō — fearing, afraid of (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.; here f.)
glossary.torvae: torvus — grim, fierce-eyed, savage of aspect (f. dat. or gen. sg., also f. nom. pl.; here dat. sg.)
glossary.tradat: trādō — hands over, delivers (3 sg. pres. subj.; in an indirect question)
glossary.tremoribus: tremor — tremblings, quakings, shudders (m. dat. or abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.trepidamque: trepidus — trembling, panicky, agitated (adj., f. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.trieterica: triētēricus — triennial, held every other year (adj., n. nom./acc. pl.; of the Bacchic festival, counted inclusively as every third year; here acc. pl.)
glossary.troezen: Troezēn — Troezen, a city of the Argolid ruled by Pittheus (f. nom. sg., Greek)
glossary.tuearis: tueor — you may protect, watch over, look after (2 sg. pres. subj. of the deponent, active in meaning)
glossary.turbasti: turbō — you have thrown into confusion, you have wrecked (2 sg. perf., syncopated for turbāvistī)
glossary.tyranno: tyrannus — king, absolute ruler (m. dat. sg.; the form is also abl. sg.; in verse usually without the pejorative force of English 'tyrant')
glossary.ullus: ūllus — any (m. nom. sg.; used chiefly in negative and conditional clauses)
glossary.utilitas: ūtilitās — advantage, benefit, what serves one's good (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.utriusque: uterque — of each of the two, of them both (m./f./n. gen. sg.)
glossary.vacat: vacō — there is time, there is leisure (3 sg. pres., impersonal with an infinitive; personally, 'is empty, is free of')
glossary.vagina: vāgīna — sheath, scabbard (f. abl. sg.; the form is also nom. sg. — here abl., of separation)
glossary.validisne: validus — strong, powerful, mighty (m./n. dat. or abl. pl.; here abl. pl.) + the enclitic -ne, marking the second limb of a double question, 'or by…'
glossary.velamima: vēlāmen — coverings, robes, garments (n. acc. pl.); the archive prints 'velamima', which is not a Latin word but a damaged digitization of vēlāmina — Lectorium prints its witness unaltered
glossary.veloque: vēlum — sail (n. abl. sg.; the form is also dat. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.venerem: venus — sexual desire, lust, lovemaking (f. acc. sg.; capitalized, the goddess Venus)
glossary.veribus: verū — spits, roasting-spits (n. 4th decl., dat. or abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.verrit: verrō — sweeps, brushes, drags over (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.verto: vertō — I overturn, I twist round, I wrench up (1 sg. pres. act.)
glossary.vescitur: vescor — feeds on, eats (3 sg. pres. of the deponent, active in meaning; takes the ablative)
glossary.vetustis: vetustus — old, ancient, long-standing (m./f./n. dat. or abl. pl.; here f. abl. pl.)
glossary.videntem: videō — seeing, catching sight of (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.villo: villus — shaggy hair, fleece, the nap of wool (m. abl. sg.; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.vincendo: vincō — by conquering, through winning (abl. of the gerund)
glossary.vincitur: vincō — is overcome, is won over (3 sg. pres. pass.; the same spelling can belong to vinciō 'bind' — vincītur, 'is bound' — but here it is vincō)
glossary.vipereasque: vipereus — snaky, viper-haired, of vipers (adj., f. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.virginem: virgō — maiden, unmarried girl, virgin (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.virisque: vir — men, fighting men (m. dat. or abl. pl.; here abl.; not from vīrēs 'strength', whose dat./abl. pl. is vīribus) + -que 'and'
glossary.visendam: vīsō — to be seen, to be visited, for seeing (gerundive, f. acc. sg.)
glossary.visura: videō — about to see, going to see (fut. act. part., f. nom. sg.; with a verb of motion it expresses purpose, 'to go and see')
glossary.vite: vītis — vine, vine-branch, vine-leaves (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.vivaque: vīvus — living, still alive (n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.vocanti: vocō — calling, calling out for (pres. act. part., m./f. dat. sg.)
glossary.volucri: volucris — bird (f. dat. sg.; the form is also abl. sg., and dat./abl. sg. of the adj. volucer 'winged, flying' — here the noun, dat.)
glossary.voluere: volō — they wished, they were willing (3 pl. perf., the -ēre ending for -ērunt)
glossary.voluisti: volō — you wished, you willed it (2 sg. perf.)
glossary.zetesque: Zētēs — Zetes, winged son of Boreas and Orithyia, brother of Calais (m. nom. sg., Greek) + -que 'and'
